title: Vesperine & the Velvet Marches
subtitle: A Campaign World Guide of Masks, Murder, and Misbehavior · World: Carnelia · Gateway: The Oathless Glass · Main adventure: The Black Kiss
author: Prepared for Riley Renwick
summary: Lord Aurelian Sable, Oathwarden of Vesperine for thirty years, kissed the diva Seraphine Lark on the Rosewater balcony at midnight on the Night of Unmasking, staggered, clawed at his mask and fell dead by the chaise. His lips and the skin beneath his mask were stained black as Ledger ink. The crowd screamed 'poison kiss.'

source.note: Vesperine & the Velvet Marches, its solo companion Through the Oathless Glass and the Carnelia Bestiary were written for Riley Renwick by DnD Bot. overview.title: Content compass
overview.html:
Mature fantasy intrigue: flirtation, seduction-as-strategy, scandal, vice, betrayal, and violence. Romance and sexual content are always suggestive, never explicit, and fade to black between consenting adults. Nothing romantic or sexual ever involves captives, coercion, or anyone underage. The ogress den is played as danger plus bawdy comedy, not titillation at a prisoner's expense. Use your table's preferred safety tools (Lines & Veils, an X-card, or a quick 'too far? cut to morning' agreement).

  • Enthrallment is not consent: a character at fey Enthrallment stage 2+ cannot consent to romance, and any kiss-oath sealed under enthrallment is a forgery.
  • Fade to black: when consenting adult characters go somewhere private, cut to 'The next morning…'.
  • In-world law: the Accord of Lips rejects any forced, tricked, or unwilling kiss.

npcs.name: Lysander of the Silvered Glass
npcs.role: Gateway character; the man in the mirror
npcs.publicRole: Gateway character; the man in the mirror
npcs.publicDescription: Tall and slender, quicksilver-sheened skin, white-silver hair tied with a black ribbon, polished-steel eyes that reflect you. A five-hundred-year-old silver brocade doublet; he chimes faintly like a wineglass when he moves. Courtly, wistful, playful, very lonely. He speaks from any reflective surface.
npcs.dmSecret: Oriane Sable's lover and Mirelle's apprentice, bound inside the Oathless Glass by a kiss-sealed promise ('I will watch over your house forever'). He can leave only if someone freely and knowingly agrees to trade places, or when the Glass opens home. He watched the murder from inside the mirror at 11:47, saw Thessaly come through the secret door, and knows by her eyes she is Oriane's blood (Isaveth Sable). Torn between justice and protecting the last of House Sable. Trades his eyewitness testimony (a Keystone clue) for a promise to help free him, or freely at Allure 3 (Smitten).
tells: Mirrors your posture, accent and phrasing
Says exactly what you most need to hear
Fishes for ambiguous agreement ('Would you let me walk beside you, just once?')
npcs.allureDc: Influence: Charisma (Persuasion) DC 15; Advantage for genuine spontaneity

stat.notes: Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D (Glass-Bound; Show Them Their Face; Mirror Ward).

npcs.name: Sabine Velour
npcs.role: Gateway character; owner of The Blue Hour card salon; the last oathless judge
npcs.publicRole: Gateway character; owner of The Blue Hour card salon; the last oathless judge
npcs.publicDescription: A glamorous woman in her mid-fifties: warm brown skin, finger-waved black hair streaked with silver, midnight-blue beaded gown, opera gloves, an unlit jeweled cigarette holder and a Queen of Hearts in her clutch. Voice of smoke and honey; calls everyone 'sugar' or 'kid'. Runs The Blue Hour in the Velvet Quarter and cheats beautifully at cards.
npcs.dmSecret: Summoned through the Glass thirty years ago as the last oathless judge, she endorsed young Aurelian Sable as Oathwarden with a kiss (her Anchor, now released by his death) and suspects he stole something to get his name. The Blue Hour is bankrolled by Old Mother Brine and she owes the Thorn Syndicate a fortune. She owns a shard of the Glass (a hand-mirror, 'the Queen's Shard'); the Syndicate wants it because a shard-holder can choose who goes through when the Glass opens. Her deal with Brine: deliver the new oathless judges and steer them to the Syndicate's candidate for her debts and a ticket home. At Allure 3+ she confesses and gives the PCs the shard.
tells: Asks greedily about your world's songs and slang
Glances at the clock when a deal is due
Never lights her cigarette
npcs.allureDc: Influence: Charisma (Persuasion) DC 13; automatic if a PC sings/recites something from the real world

stat.notes: Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D (Marked Card, Torch Song, the Queen's Shard).

npcs.name: Prince Caelum of the Dusk
npcs.role: Gateway character; the Fae Duke's youngest son
npcs.publicRole: Gateway character; a fey prince of the Dusk
npcs.publicDescription: Unearthly tall, twilight-violet skin, golden eyes, antlers twined with climbing red roses, rose-red velvet coat stitched with thorns, a briar crown, and an air of private amusement.
npcs.dmSecret: The Fae Duke's youngest son, sent to ensure the Accord fails on Night 7. Secretly he wants Vesperine for himself as a fey-touched city of eternal revels, and he has half fallen in love with its mortals. Deeper secret: if a PC becomes Oathwarden and freely marries him, the Accord would make him a citizen, free of his father (Insight DC 18 to sense he is withholding something). Queen Ilysse is his former paramour; Lady Nocturne Vesh is his rival and plans to denounce him to the Duke on Night 7. His 'one dance at the seventh bell' bargain binds a PC to be wherever he is at midnight on Night 7.
tells: Never says 'thank you' and deflects it ('Don't thank me, darling, it's bad luck')
Cut flowers open as he enters
Perception DC 15 in candlelight: his shadow has antlers
Flinches from iron coins; pays only in silver and gold
Insight DC 17: speaks only carefully true sentences
revealTriggers: He seals a kiss-bound bargain (roses burst from the air)
Nocturne threatens a PC he is fond of
A PC reaches Allure 3 and asks the right question (Insight DC 18)
Sunset in the Lanternwood
A cold-iron blade at his throat
npcs.trueForm: Twilight-violet skin, golden eyes, rose-twined antlers and a briar crown; in a mirror he looks at the viewer and puts a finger to his lips.
npcs.allureDc: Contested Charisma (Persuasion or Deception) vs his Charisma (Deception) +8

stat.notes: Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D. Deception +8 is canonical; in the solo book he deliberately plays at +4 (L1) / +6 (L2-3).

npcs.sourceSection: Part 2 > Gateway Characters > 3; Part 6 > Glamours & Reveals

npcs.name: Marisol Tidewhisper
npcs.role: Gateway character; rebellious siren of the Drowned Choir
npcs.publicRole: Gateway character; rebellious siren of the Drowned Choir
npcs.publicDescription: A merfolk siren who can take a two-legged shape on land: sea-green scales along cheekbones and collarbones, black hair braided with sea-glass and tiny bells, eyes like moonlit surf, a pearl-and-abalone bodice and sea-silk wraps. Always slightly damp and grinning. Wild, reckless, a laugh like a breaking wave; she flirts by daring.
npcs.dmSecret: She gave the Pearl Heart to Captain Kray to break Mother-of-Pearl Nerissa's centuries-old rule; Kray betrayed her and enslaved her sisters. She stole a Glass shard from a shipwreck to recruit outsiders no one in Carnelia could buy, and wants the PCs to hand the Pearl Heart to her rather than Nerissa, making her the new Mother of the Choir. Her betrayal can be exposed (Insight DC 16, or Bel Okafor's testimony).
motivations: A crew of champions (and maybe a sweetheart)
tells: Phrases kiss-promises so they sound like nothing
Goes pale beneath her scales when Kray or Nerissa is named

stat.notes: Choir Siren with HP 95, Speed 30 ft./Swim 50 ft., no Stolen Voice, Siren's Laugh and Undertow Dare; treat as CR 4.

spicy.note: Preferred alternate portrait (used as the main image on the NPC sheets).

npcs.name: Sir Valentin Dusk
npcs.role: Gateway character; exiled vampire consort of House Dusk
npcs.publicRole: Gateway character; exiled vampire consort of House Dusk
npcs.publicDescription: Pale as candle wax, tousled raven hair, a beauty mark beneath one heavy-lidded eye, black velvet coat with garnet buttons, ruffled cravat, oxblood gloves. A vampire: in mirrors only his clothes show. Decadent, sardonic, romantic, tired of eternity, and he asks permission for everything.
npcs.dmSecret: Countess Morwenna Dusk's consort for a hundred years until her steward Lucan Vey framed him for a murder Lucan committed (the solo book names the victim: Count Aurelio). Morwenna exiled him. He wants Lucan destroyed and Morwenna's forgiveness, and secretly plans to pass through the Oathless Glass to a world without the Accord, where legend says a vampire might walk in sunlight again, with or without the PCs' blessing. He never feeds on anyone who has not enthusiastically agreed.
tells: Asks permission for everything
Notices your pulse
Invisible in mirrors except for his clothes
npcs.allureDc: Charisma (Persuasion) DC 14 (candor), or offering something he hasn't felt in centuries

stat.notes: Vampire Spawn: Bite only on the willing, Shadow Step, Gentleman's Grip, no reflection.

spicy.note: Preferred alternate portrait (used as the main image on the NPC sheets).

npcs.name: Lord Aurelian Sable
npcs.role: The victim; Oathwarden of Vesperine for thirty years
npcs.publicDescription: Age 58, silver at the temples, a dimpled smile, always in midnight-blue velvet. Beloved in public (generous, witty, the best dancer at any ball), feared in private as keeper of every broken promise. Engaged to Lady Celestine Morrow; kept the diva Seraphine Lark as his 'muse'. Died at midnight on the Night of Unmasking after kissing Seraphine, his face stained black as Ledger ink.
npcs.dmSecret: Born Aurel Fenn, a penniless apprentice of the Hall of Vows. Thirty-one years ago, coached by Lady Nocturne Vesh (her price: his true name, now in a black-glass name-jar in the Thornwake), he had the Ledger read his bride Isaveth Sable's wedding vow ('Everything I am is yours') literally, taking her name, title, inheritance and memory. He cut the vow-page from the Ledger decades ago. His journal reads 'The masks remember. She cannot. She must not.' His last letter to his lawyer (stolen by Vexirra's kobolds): 'I believe Isaveth has remembered. If I die, look to the woman who makes my face.' Under Speak with Dead he cannot say his birth name.
motivations: Keep the office and the Ledger

stat.notes: Deceased. Rises as an Undying Oathwarden only if his true name escapes Nocturne's jar (Part 7, Loose Threads). Deadly: flee or bargain.

npcs.name: Dame Ottoline Graves
npcs.role: Opera Council spokesperson; the PCs' employer
npcs.publicRole: Opera Council spokesperson; the PCs' employer
npcs.publicDescription: A tiny, elderly, terrifyingly polite patron in an enormous crimson gown with a jeweled lorgnette. She hands the oathless PCs the Red Ribbon Warrant: entry to any house and the right to question anyone once. Reward: 500 ducats each and a Council favor sealed with a kiss.
npcs.dmSecret: She knows exactly what the Oathless Glass does: the Council's charter requires an oathless judge to confirm the next Oathwarden, which is why the PCs get the Warrant. Her beloved grandson Teodor is among the dream-thief sleepers (saving him buys +1 night). She is one possible allied Council vote for Ending B.
motivations: Save the city before the seventh bell

stat.notes: Lorgnette of Seeing (1/Day: see Invisible creatures and through illusions for 1 minute); Insight +6, Persuasion +5.

npcs.sourceSection: Part 4 > The Investigator's Warrant; Appendix A
npcs.notes: Portrait prompt #9 exists in the guide, but no portrait image was generated.

npcs.name: Seraphine Lark
npcs.publicDescription: Human, early 30s, a cascade of copper hair, emerald silk gown, a voice that could melt candle wax, black-stained lips she refuses to wash ('Let them look'). Dramatic, quick-witted, exhausted by her own legend; funny when she forgets to perform. Alibi: on stage until 11:50, then on the balcony with the crowd until the midnight kiss.
npcs.dmSecret: She has spied on Aurelian for the Thorn Syndicate for two years (passing on his pillow-talk) and is in love with Lady Celestine Morrow. Her alibi is true (forty witnesses). Under pressure: Aurelian was frightened for weeks, received a faceless porcelain mask and murmured 'The masks remember'; at about quarter to midnight she glimpsed in the mirror wall 'Madame Rook's silver braid, fussing with his ribbon, then gone.' On Night 3 the Syndicate plants a forged 'S.' letter in her dressing room.
npcs.allureDc: DC 15 (DC 10 if a PC compliments something other than her beauty)

stat.notes: Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D (Aria of Ruin, Showstopper, Star Power).

npcs.name: Lady Celestine Morrow
npcs.role: Suspect: the Fiancée; heir of House Morrow
npcs.publicRole: Suspect: the Fiancée; heir of House Morrow
npcs.publicDescription: Half-elf, 28, platinum hair in a severe crown braid, ice-blue high-collared gown, a single sapphire at her throat; moves like a duelist. Cold, cutting, brilliant; treats conversation as fencing. Claims she was 'alone on the balcony, enjoying the view.'
npcs.dmSecret: In love with Seraphine and desperate to escape her engagement oath; a month ago she bought fake oath-breaking salts from Ezren Vos (the white crystals in her vanity). Her alibi is false: she was in the Morrow family box writing (then burning) a love letter to Seraphine (Mending restores '…we'll be free by the end of the festival, my lark…'). She saw Captain Hale take a fat purse from a masked man in a thorn-green domino at 11:30. House Morrow is of founding blood: she can be sworn in as Oathwarden on Night 7.
motivations: Save the city if she must
npcs.allureDc: DC 17; Advantage if a PC beats her at cards, words or a duel

stat.notes: Knight reflavored as a duelist: AC 16, rapier (Piercing), Parry, Fencer's Footwork.

npcs.name: Captain Dorian Hale
npcs.role: Suspect: the Watchman; captain of the Lantern Watch
npcs.publicRole: Suspect: the Watchman; captain of the Lantern Watch
npcs.publicDescription: Human, mid-40s, broad shoulders, a scar along his jaw, Lantern Watch coat with the top buttons undone; smells of pipe smoke and rain. Tired, gruff, decent at heart, dry humor. Claims he was 'walking the perimeter.'
npcs.dmSecret: Owes the Thorn Syndicate 2,000 ducats in gambling debts; took Varo Kestrel's bribe to pull his guards from the Dressing Gallery corridor between 11:30 and midnight; quietly ordered the body moved; a Syndicate purse sits in his strongbox. Under pressure: the bribe, Varo's name, and 'The dressing corridor was empty for half an hour… the mirror wall's got a door.' Lost his own house (and horse) at cards.
motivations: Redemption, if someone gives him a chance

stat.notes: Companion stat block (Part 9).

npcs.name: Ezren Vos
npcs.role: Suspect: the Perfumer; owner of Vos Perfumery
npcs.publicRole: Suspect: the Perfumer; owner of Vos Perfumery
npcs.publicDescription: Tiefling, 30s, lavender skin, gold rings on curling horns, a loose silk robe over an embroidered vest; speaks softly and leans in to smell you. Sensual, curious, theatrical, a little amoral, genuinely brilliant. Made the bloodrose perfume Seraphine wears. Alibi: running the perfume fountain on the ground floor all night.
npcs.dmSecret: Sells illegal, mostly fake 'oath-breaking salts' (sea salt and crushed pearl). His alibi is true. Under pressure he identifies Widow's Sigh, which is inert until it breathes bloodrose ('It was on his face, inside the mask'), and his scent-coded ledger shows 'Lavender (Madame R.): 1 vial bloodrose' bought a month ago, odd since Thessaly wears only lavender. He can identify a listening mask.

stat.notes: Companion version scaled down (HP 40, limited spells), Part 9.

npcs.name: Varo Kestrel
npcs.role: Suspect: the Fixer; Thorn Syndicate rogue
npcs.publicRole: Suspect: the Fixer; Thorn Syndicate rogue
npcs.publicDescription: Half-elf, late 20s, dark curls, crooked grin, rose-thorn earring, thorn-green domino mask; dresses better than he can afford. Shameless, charming, cheerful even when caught; loyal to friends only. Alibi: 'Dancing.' With whom? 'Everyone.'
npcs.dmSecret: Six months ago he stole a page from Aurelian's desk for Syndicate blackmail: the original wedding-vow page ('Aurel Fenn' and 'Isaveth Sable'); Mother Brine sold it to a lady in a grey veil for three masks. Tonight he bribed Hale and lifted Aurelian's Ledger-vault key from his coat; he has it now and will trade it for immunity. His original report sits in Kray's blackmail archive. Can become a recurring rogue companion.

stat.notes: Companion: +10 HP and +1 Hit Point Die per hero level above 3; solo book uses Bandit at L1.

npcs.name: Madame Thessaly Rook
npcs.publicDescription: Human, about 60, a long silver braid pinned with gold, laugh lines, magnificent dark eyes, fingertips flecked with gold leaf, always a lavender shawl; never wears a mask herself. Warm, wicked, hilarious: everybody's favorite aunt. Lives above her Atelier on Needle Row with three cats named after her ex-lovers. Gives each PC a free, beautiful mask 'for the investigation'. Alibi: in the Dressing Gallery all evening, fitting masks.
npcs.dmSecret: THE KILLER. She is Lady Isaveth Sable, Aurelian's first wife, whose identity he stole with a literal reading of her wedding vow thirty-one years ago. Six months ago she bought the stolen vow-page (as 'a lady in a grey veil') and touching it restored her memory. She obtained Widow's Sigh from the Moth Court (paying with her wedding-day dream), bought bloodrose from Ezren (as 'Madame R.'), sabotaged Aurelian's mask ribbon, and at 11:47 came through the mirror-wall door from the Dressing Gallery to swap his mask for a poisoned twin, knocking the clock pendulum and snagging her lavender ribbon. The original mask is hidden in a Dressing Gallery costume trunk; the vow-page is in a hatbox in her Atelier. Her gift masks include a listening mask (Divination aura; Arcana DC 16 or Ezren to identify). Motive: revenge and restoration; she intends to claim the Oathwardenship as founding-blood heir. Deflects toward Celestine; with two or more hard clues grows quiet; with the vow-page or empty crypt she reveals herself: 'My name is Isaveth Sable. He took it from me with a kiss. I took it back the same way.'
motivations: Reclaim her name, House and fortune
Avoid the city's fall, which frightens her
tells: Deflects to Celestine ('ask her about the salts')
'Stepped out once, around quarter to' (actors)
Answers Zone of Truth questions only literally
A thirty-year habit: made Aurelian's mask every year and never charged him

stat.notes: Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D (Gilded Needles, Mask of Mercy, 'Darling, Please'). She fights to escape, not to kill.

npcs.notes: Portrait prompt #8 (Isaveth revealed) has no generated image; thessaly-rook.png is the pre-reveal portrait. Revealed-form portrait (prompt #8): portraits/the-lady-of-the-hall.png (alias file name; gated).

aliases.name: the lady in the grey veil

revealed.note: Revealed form; show only after the reveal (alias file name).

npcs.name: Lady Oriane Sable
npcs.role: Founder of House Sable (historical, ~500 years ago)
npcs.publicDescription: The first of House Sable, who did not trust the Accord of Lips and asked the Fae Duke for one more clause.
npcs.dmSecret: Author of the Oathless Clause and commissioner of the Oathless Glass; Lysander's lover, to whom he swore 'I will watch over your house forever.' Thessaly/Isaveth has her eyes.

stat.notes: Historical; appears only as a memory in the Glass or the Mirror Gallery.

npcs.sourceSection: Part 2 > The Lore of the Glass

npcs.name: Mirelle of the Thousand Faces
npcs.role: Fey glass-wright of the Fae Duke (historical)
npcs.publicRole: Fey glass-wright of the Fae Duke (historical)
npcs.publicDescription: A legendary fey artisan said to have made the oldest mirrors of Vesperine.
npcs.dmSecret: Built the Oathless Glass for Oriane Sable, its silver quenched in Ledger ink and its frame carved from living rose-thorn. Lysander was her apprentice. Her current whereabouts are never described.

stat.notes: Fey creature type; jailer of the Thousand-Faced Reflection at the bottom of the Glass.

npcs.sourceSection: Part 2 > The Lore of the Glass

npcs.name: The Fae Duke of the Dusk
npcs.displayName: The Fae Duke of the Dusk
npcs.role: Ruler of the Dusk Court; creditor of the Accord of Lips
npcs.publicRole: Ruler of the Dusk Court; creditor of the Accord of Lips
npcs.publicDescription: Never seen directly, only as roses and a voice. Five hundred years ago he struck the Accord of Lips with Vesperine's founders. If no Oathwarden is sworn by midnight on Night 7, he comes to collect.
npcs.dmSecret: Wants the city's founding bloodlines. On a d12 temptation roll of 12 he speaks from a hedge offering anything for a kiss-sealed promise (+2 Enthrallment). Caelum is his youngest son; Nocturne is his Mistress of Glamours; Amaranth his herald.

stat.notes: By design the Duke never appears; his power acts through a Herald Ascendant and the Seventh Bell's lair actions.
stat.statName: Herald Ascendant of the Dusk Court

npcs.sourceSection: Part 6 > The Courts of the Fair Folk

npcs.name: Old Mother Brine
npcs.role: True boss of the Thorn Syndicate (publicly only its fence)
npcs.publicDescription: A tiny, toothless fence wrapped in shawls with eyes like wet pebbles, who runs Things That Shouldn't Be Sold in the Drowned Market and asks a password riddle through a slot in her door.
npcs.dmSecret: Brine is the Thorn Syndicate's true boss; the harmless-old-fence act is her public cover. Former pirate queen of the Saltgrave. She sold the vow-page to 'a lady in a grey veil' without knowing what it was, holds the Drowned Shard (a seat in the Glass), owns Sabine's debt and Hale's markers, and backs her puppet candidate, Lord Silvano Quell, for Oathwarden. She hires Ilaria Venn on Night 3 and leads the Syndicate's ambush on the Bridge of Sighing Lanterns on Night 7.

stat.notes: Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D (Cane-Sword, Sea-Pistol, three curios, Bodyguard Clause).

npcs.sourceSection: Part 3 Gazetteer; Part 4 Clue Trail; Riddle 5
npcs.notes: Round 2 canon: Brine is the boss everywhere (Gazetteer, Part 4, SA3, solo book).

npcs.name: Sister Corvina
npcs.role: A Veiled Sister of the Hall of Vows
npcs.publicRole: A Veiled Sister of the Hall of Vows
npcs.publicDescription: A Veiled Sister, one of the silent keepers of the Hall of Vows (named only in Appendix C).
npcs.dmSecret: The Veiled Sisters ask Riddle 2 at the Vault, confirm that a vow-page touched by its swearer restores what it holds, can strike forged vows from the Ledger, and reveal the 'freely kissed into office by a founding heir' loophole (History DC 16 or a gift).

stat.notes: Religion +4, History +4; knows the founding-heir loophole.

npcs.name: The Veiled Sisters
npcs.role: Order of keepers who tend the Ledger of Vows
npcs.publicRole: Order of keepers who tend the Ledger of Vows
npcs.publicDescription: Veiled keepers of the Hall of Vows who tend the Ledger on its lectern of living rose-thorn and call the Ledger's back pages 'the Margins.'
npcs.dmSecret: They ask the vault riddle, can annul forged (enthralled) vows, and know the Oathwarden-succession loophole. Collective NPC.
motivations: Preserve the Ledger and the Accord

stat.notes: They never attack inside the Hall of Vows.

npcs.name: Pell Ambrose
npcs.role: Velvet Opera stage carpenter; captive witness
npcs.publicRole: Velvet Opera stage carpenter; captive witness
npcs.publicDescription: The Opera's nervous, sweet stage carpenter, who fled the city the morning after the murder and vanished on the Bog Causeway.
npcs.dmSecret: He built the mirror-wall door and was mending a sandbag rope at 11:47: he saw Madame Rook come back through it 'with a mask under her shawl', white as milk (Keystone testimony). Now a captive 'husband-candidate' of the Honeyhorn Matrons who has failed two of five trials.

stat.notes: Athletics +4; knows every trapdoor in the Opera.

npcs.name: Benedetto Fiore
npcs.publicDescription: A tenor of the Velvet Opera.
npcs.dmSecret: Not developed beyond Appendix C.

stat.notes: Performance +7.

npcs.name: Allegra Vane
npcs.publicDescription: A card-salon owner in the Velvet Quarter.
npcs.dmSecret: Not developed beyond Appendix C.

stat.notes: Sleight of Hand +6; Dowager Ysolde's daughter.

npcs.name: Pim Gallowglass
npcs.publicDescription: A Vesperine gondolier.
npcs.dmSecret: Not developed beyond Appendix C.

stat.notes: Swim 30 ft.; knows the smugglers' arches; ferries the PCs on Night 7.

npcs.name: Teodor Graves
npcs.publicDescription: A young nobleman, Dame Ottoline's beloved grandson, fallen into an enchanted smiling sleep dusted with silver moth-powder.
npcs.dmSecret: Wrapped in silk in the Silk Library of the Cocoon Palace, dreaming of being a famous sailor. Saving him grants +1 night on the Unravelling clock.

stat.notes: Faints convincingly as a distraction.

npcs.name: Big Mother Hulga Tenderbone
npcs.publicDescription: A ten-foot ogress matriarch with braids woven with bones and dried roses and an apron reading KISS THE COOK. Loud, sentimental, quick to weep and quicker to smash.
npcs.dmSecret: Secretly writes love poems to her petrified husband Grunwald but has never once said 'I love you' aloud (DC 20, and she must be last to break the curse). A champion who wins the Moot is 'betrothed' to her.

stat.notes: Bestiary stat block written for her.

npcs.name: Brunhilde "Bru"
npcs.publicDescription: Bodybuilder energy; flirts by arm-wrestling and lifting people over her head; respects anyone who beats her at anything.
npcs.dmSecret: Runs the Hog-Hoist trial (Athletics +6). Creatures have Disadvantage on saves to avoid her grapples.

stat.notes: One of the five Ogre matrons.

npcs.notes: Portrait prompt #11 has no generated image.

npcs.name: Little Gretch
npcs.publicDescription: Romantic, shy, reads stolen chapbook romances; most likely to help the PCs.
npcs.dmSecret: First to declare her love at the Sulking Stones. Can become a companion (Ogre, HP 45) and a pen-pal for Vexirra. Her hand-mirror shard causes the d8 gateway 'comic misfire'.

stat.notes: Companion: HP 45 (6d10 + 12).

npcs.notes: Portrait prompt #12 has no generated image.

npcs.name: Granny Moss
npcs.publicDescription: Ancient, blind and sharp-tongued; trades information for gossip.
npcs.dmSecret: The only one who remembers exactly what the hag said when she cursed the husbands.

stat.notes: Counts among the five Ogre matrons if the clan fights.

npcs.name: Auntie Sallowmere
npcs.publicDescription: A petty, vain, hilarious bog hag living in a chicken-legged hut beneath the bog, decorated with forty years of wedding invitations she sent herself.
npcs.dmSecret: Cursed the proud Honeyhorn ogre men into the Sulking Stones forty years ago 'until somebody finally says it'. Surrenders to flattery, an apology, or a better grudge; can lift the curse (Persuasion DC 16). Feuding with Ondine Mirewillow.

npcs.name: Grunwald
npcs.publicDescription: One of six ogre husbands petrified as the Sulking Stones.
npcs.dmSecret: Steps out mid-sentence, forty years late, if the curse breaks.

stat.notes: Implied; the freed husbands are ogres.

npcs.name: Rufus
npcs.publicDescription: A carter who has accepted his fate and is enjoying the cake.
npcs.dmSecret: Does not want to leave without the cake.

npcs.name: Watchman Dobbs
npcs.publicDescription: A Lantern Watch recruit, captive and in denial.

stat.notes: Implied.

npcs.name: Watchman Pirelli
npcs.publicDescription: A Lantern Watch recruit, captive and in denial.

stat.notes: Implied.

npcs.name: Lorcan the Poet
npcs.publicDescription: A poet having the time of his life at the Moot.
npcs.dmSecret: Technically a willing guest: he walked in on purpose.

stat.notes: Performance +5.

npcs.name: Queen Ilysse of the Hush
npcs.publicDescription: Queen of the Moth Court of the Lanternwood: wings of dusky violet and gold, ink-wet eyes, a gown spun of moonlight; speaks in a near-whisper so you must lean close. Collects compliments, dances and truths.
npcs.dmSecret: Gorging on Vesperine's dreams as the treaty weakens, pressed by the Duke. She keeps Isaveth's wedding-day dream (traded for Widow's Sigh) in a cocoon in the Silk Library (Keystone). Supplies dream-powder for glimmer under protest; proof of this can turn her against the Thornwake. Caelum's former paramour; holds his rose love-token (solo).
motivations: Be free of the Duke's demands
tells: Moonlight powder on her fingertips and tonic bottles
Candle flames lean toward her; moths gather at her windows
Speaks only in whispers
Replaced iron candleholders with glass
Insight DC 16: seems hungry when a client describes a beautiful dream
revealTriggers: Someone falls asleep in her presence
A sudden gust or a lantern thrust at her face
Pipwhistle's dream-sugar trade exposed in front of her
A PC wins the Moth Waltz or names her true title
npcs.trueForm: Great wings of dusky violet and gold patterned like eyes, ink-dark eyes, a gown spun from moonlight.
npcs.allureDc: Moth Waltz: Performance/Acrobatics DC 14 ×3 + compliments Persuasion DC 15

stat.notes: Fey type; HP 81; Advantage on saves vs Charmed; Lullaby of the Hush (Recharge 5-6) replaces the 2014 sleep.

npcs.name: Sir Fennic Ashwing
npcs.publicDescription: The Queen's jealous, theatrical champion; a skilled duelist who challenges anyone she smiles at.
npcs.dmSecret: Demands a first-blood duel after the Moth Waltz. Falls asleep if hummed to (solo). Bewildered loyalty to Caelum ('Old friend').

stat.notes: Fly 40 ft. Group play: Gladiator. Solo book (L1-3): 'Wounded Fennic', a Scout, nursing a cold-iron wound from a duel with a Thornwake knight; healed by Side Adventure 2.

npcs.name: The Dust-Maidens
npcs.publicDescription: Giggling attendants who scatter sleep-pollen.
npcs.dmSecret: They witness and gossip about PCs' embarrassing dreams; one recites the Silk Library rhyme.

stat.notes: Use the Bestiary Minion adjustment for crowds.

npcs.name: Mother-of-Pearl Nerissa
npcs.publicDescription: Silver-scaled siren with hair like kelp in moonlight, her voice now a hoarse whisper; proud, furious, irresistibly charismatic even voiceless.
npcs.dmSecret: Has ruled the Choir for six hundred years. Her true voice (and the Choir's) is in the Pearl Heart, stolen by Kray via Marisol's betrayal. Returning the Heart wins eternal friendship and the Song of Calling for Night 7.

stat.notes: Choir Siren with the Bestiary Elite adjustment (HP 117, +1 AC/attack/DC, a Reaction); voiceless until the Pearl Heart is returned.

npcs.name: Captain Morven "Saltlick" Kray
npcs.publicDescription: Human, one eye, knuckles tattooed SALT / LICK, a grin full of gold teeth; flirts by insulting you. Vain and lonely.
npcs.dmSecret: Holds the Pearl Heart and forces the Choir to sing ships onto the rocks for his wreckers. Keeps the Syndicate's blackmail archive (Hale's debts, Varo's report, dirt on half the Council) in his strongroom. Skims from Mother Brine. Can command two Coral Sentinels at level 7.

stat.notes: Canonical: Bandit Captain with HP 71 (11d8 + 22), CR 3. The solo book's 'Kray (solo variant)' is a labeled scaled-down variant: HP 30/40, one attack per turn, CR 1.

npcs.name: Quill-Fin
npcs.publicDescription: A young adult siren who guides travelers through the underwater ways for a kiss on the cheek (a dare she gives everyone).
npcs.dmSecret: The cheek-kiss seals a small oath of guidance under the Accord.

stat.notes: Amphibious; Swim 40 ft.; Survival +5 underwater.

npcs.name: Bel Okafor
npcs.publicDescription: A tall woman with a shaved head, a scar through one eyebrow and profound disgust for her own crew.
npcs.dmSecret: Hates Kray and is looking for an excuse to walk out; can provide the strongroom key, a back way out, and testimony (including about Marisol's betrayal).

stat.notes: Used for Kray's first mate in the combat path.

npcs.name: Countess Morwenna Dusk
npcs.publicDescription: Tall, raven-haired, gown of black and wine-red velvet, lips like a fresh cut. Witty, melancholy, devastatingly flirtatious in a slow old-world way. Reclusive vintner of the Crimson Vintage; host of the Harvest Masquerade. Everyone suspects she is a vampire.
npcs.dmSecret: She is a vampire, and a civilized one: for two centuries she has fed only on willing, well-paid donors. Her steward Lucan is behind the disappearances. She knew Isaveth Sable as a child and attended her wedding 31 years ago (diary entry in the Vintage Vault); she will recognize Thessaly instantly (Keystone). Controls a Council vote.
npcs.allureDc: Persuasion DC 16 or proof of Lucan's crimes

stat.notes: Should never come to a fight.

npcs.notes: Her maker, the Crimson Patriarch, appears only in the Bestiary.

npcs.name: Lucan Vey
npcs.publicDescription: Handsome, golden, polite to a fault; an immaculate steward in cream-and-gold livery.
npcs.dmSecret: A vampire spawn turning stolen villagers into a secret army (Dusk Fledglings), framed Valentin for Count Aurelio's murder, and plans to destroy Morwenna and deliver her Council vote so the Syndicate can install its puppet Oathwarden. Offers the PCs a share of the 'new order' and will betray them on Night 7.

stat.notes: Vampire Spawn with HP 112 and Legendary Resistance (1/Day) everywhere (guide, solo book, 5-player scaling). Never fought in the solo book: an escape set piece instead.

npcs.name: Marta Ilic
npcs.publicDescription: A sharp-eyed village innkeeper whose son vanished; the PCs' contact in the valley.
npcs.dmSecret: Her son is among the caged villagers (Bestiary hook: turned into a Dusk Fledgling only a week ago).

stat.notes: Insight +4.

npcs.name: The Donors
npcs.role: Willing blood-donors at the Harvest Masquerade
npcs.publicRole: Willing blood-donors at the Harvest Masquerade
npcs.publicDescription: Well-dressed adults who attend the masquerade willingly and boast about it like a spa visit.

npcs.name: Vexirra
npcs.publicDescription: A young copper dragon with scales like a new penny, a talent for impressions and terrible taste in jokes; insists she is an 'adult'. Desperately romantic. Sometimes visits the city disguised as a shy red-haired woman with freckles and copper-rimmed spectacles.
npcs.dmSecret: Hoarding Vesperine's love letters because she has never received one; among them is Aurelian's last letter (Keystone). Will fly to Vesperine on Night 7 if befriended.
npcs.allureDc: Write her a letter that makes her cry (Performance DC 17)

stat.notes: Add the Copper Guise trait (Magic action shape-shift).

aliases.name: the red-haired woman in copper spectacles

guise.note: Show this until the reveal (alias file name).

npcs.name: Scribbletail
npcs.role: Kobold chief poet of the Inkscale Troupe
npcs.publicRole: Kobold chief poet of the Inkscale Troupe
npcs.publicDescription: Writes appalling sonnets; jealous of anyone the dragon likes.

stat.notes: Implied: kobold copyist.

npcs.name: Forewoman Brannagh Copperhand
npcs.publicDescription: Grizzled, practical dwarven guild boss who posted the bounty on Vexirra.
npcs.dmSecret: Secretly a romantic who writes letters to her late husband and burns them; a perfect pen-pal for Vexirra.

stat.notes: Dwarf: Darkvision 60 ft., Resistance to Poison; miner's pick (Piercing).

npcs.name: Pipwhistle Dewlace
npcs.publicDescription: As players first meet her: Pip Dewley, the bubbly, curly-haired, full-size barmaid at The Gilded Thimble on Needle Row, quick with gossip and always asking for 'a little something for luck.' Buttons go missing whenever she's near.
npcs.dmSecret: A hand-sized pixie (dandelion-fluff hair, dragonfly wings, rose-petal dress, thimble hat) who kisses noses 'for luck' to collect tiny promises, which she trades to the Moth Court for dream-sugar. That trade tells the Court whose dreams to harvest; she has no idea it hurts anyone and is horrified if shown. Pocket Bargains cause comic curses, not Enthrallment. As an ally (Allure 3+) she scouts invisibly and steals small items.
tells: Buttons vanish; her apron pockets jingle
Serves in pewter, never touches iron tankards
Perception DC 12: seems much smaller for a blink when startled
Pink sparkles on anyone she nose-kisses
Insight DC 12: remembers every promise to the word
revealTriggers: She sneezes
Someone pays her in buttons
A PC refuses or breaks a tiny promise
Someone offers her a whole cake
Cold iron in her hand
npcs.trueForm: A hand-sized pixie with dragonfly wings, standing on the bar where Pip's tray should be, waving.
npcs.allureDc: Persuasion DC 11, or automatic with sweets/buttons/a lullaby

stat.notes: SRD 5.2.1 has no Pixie; or use the Bestiary Buttonthief (CR 0). Pixie Dust: DC 12 Wis or Confusion effect until end of next turn.

npcs.sourceSection: Part 6 > The Fey NPCs > 1; Glamours & Reveals
npcs.notes: Round 2 canon: Pipwhistle is a she and a pixie everywhere (solo Adventure 3 and the Bestiary Buttonthief lore now agree). The solo image solo-img/pip-dewley.jpg (alias file name) predates this fix.

portrait.note: True-form portrait; reveal only when a glamour drops.

npcs.name: Ondine Mirewillow
npcs.publicDescription: As players first meet her: Dina Mire, the giggling, sun-freckled bath-attendant at the Lilywater Baths in Lanternside who scrubs backs, braids hair and gossips about everyone.
npcs.dmSecret: A river nymph (green-gold skin, willow-leaf hair, rippling eyes) whose lure is lost time: those who 'rest a moment' wake hours or a year later, and she keeps their shoes. Her pool is on the Bog Causeway. Feuding with Auntie Sallowmere. Dreaming Waters can advance the Unravelling clock.
tells: Hems always damp
Frogs sing in the drains when she laughs
A mountain of single shoes in lost-and-found
Hasn't aged in forty years
Insight DC 14: asks every customer for 'just a little something'
revealTriggers: Cold water in her face
Someone mentions Auntie Sallowmere
Caught with a sleeper's shoes
She uses Water Stride to escape
npcs.trueForm: Green-gold skin, willow-leaf hair threaded with water-lilies, rippling eyes; ripples water so reflections are hard to read.
npcs.allureDc: Persuasion DC 13 (out-tease her or bring Sallowmere gossip)

stat.notes: Water Stride replaces Tree Stride; Fey Charm = at-will Charm Monster (DC 14) +1 Enthrallment; Dreaming Waters.

portrait.note: True-form portrait; reveal only when a glamour drops.

npcs.name: Rillo Fennamint
npcs.role: Tempter; the Piper of the Revels; Moth Court talent scout
npcs.publicRole: Dance master and fiddler of the Opera's after-parties
npcs.publicDescription: As players first meet him: Master Orrin Mintleaf, the beloved bearded dance master and fiddler who leads the revel-band at every Velvet Opera after-party, always in a wide-brimmed hat and tall, oddly heavy boots.
npcs.dmSecret: A satyr (gilded ram's horns, chestnut curls, goat legs) who leads the best dreamers out to the Lanternwood 'for an after-party' and into Ilysse's cocoons. Has a soft spot for the PCs and can be turned into a guide (Advantage on the Dimming path).
tells: Perception DC 13: boots clip-clop like hooves
Never removes his hat
Avoids iron-studded floors and the Opera's iron railings
His tunes are always your song
Insight DC 14: scans crowds for 'dreamers'
revealTriggers: Loses himself in the dance past midnight
Out-played in a music duel
Dawn while he plays in the Lanternwood
An iron heel stamped on his 'foot'
npcs.trueForm: Gilded ram's horns, chestnut curls and goat legs, dancing even when standing still.
npcs.allureDc: Performance DC 14 (dance with abandon or win a music duel)

stat.notes: Or Satyr (SRD 5.2.1) with HP 45 (10d8) and Revel Pipes.

portrait.note: True-form portrait; reveal only when a glamour drops.

npcs.name: Lady Nocturne Vesh
npcs.role: Thorn; Mistress of Glamours; ruler of the Thornwake
npcs.publicRole: Wealthy widow and hostess of the Black Fan salon
npcs.publicDescription: As players first meet her: Madame Noor Vesperelle, a rich, mysterious widow 'from across the sea' who hosts the Black Fan, the most exclusive masked salon in the Gilded Crescent, in a palazzo where every mirror is draped in black crepe. Invitations are black envelopes sealed with a lip-print.
npcs.dmSecret: The Duke's Mistress of Glamours and Caelum's bitterest rival. Harvests true names through enchanted kisses and kiss-bound vows; on Night 7 every name she holds becomes the Duke's and hers to command. Means to enthrall a PC (oathless vows count double) as puppet Oathwarden or weapon against Caelum. Thirty-one years ago she whispered the literal-vow trick to Aurel Fenn for his true name, kept in a black-glass jar in the Thornwake Name-Jar Cellar. Plans to denounce Caelum on Night 7. Cannot be charmed.
motivations: Collect Vesperine's names for the Duke
tells: Never near an uncovered mirror (Insight DC 14 to find the 'custom' suspicious)
Long gloves; silver cutlery, never iron
Guests can't describe her face (Int DC 13 fails at Enthrallment 1+)
Dead rose petals where she sat
Insight DC 18: her smile arrives before her eyes
revealTriggers: A draped mirror uncovered, or the Glass/a shard turned on her
Cold iron touches her skin
Laughed at publicly and sincerely (Performance DC 18)
A PC reaches Enthrallment 4 with her
Midnight at her Night 6 masquerade
npcs.trueForm: Bone-white skin, black lips, starless eyes, black hair woven with dead roses, a dark sapphire choker pulsing with a stolen name.

stat.notes: Full 2024 stat block in Part 6 (8,400 XP in lair).

spicy.note: Preferred alternate portrait (used as the main image on the NPC sheets).

npcs.name: Sir Merrow Ashgrave, the Sorrowkiss
npcs.role: Thorn; the Glimmer Knight; Thornwake enforcer
npcs.publicRole: Mourning friar who sits with the grieving
npcs.publicDescription: As players first meet him: Brother Ash, a tall, grey-robed mourning friar of no order anyone can name, who sits with the grieving at Lanternside wakes and Cypress Isle funerals.
npcs.dmSecret: A sorrowful fey knight in black thorned plate inlaid with silver moths who hooks Vesperine on glimmer (fey dust refined from Moth Court dream-powder, sold through the Syndicate). Glimmer-addicts can't resist Nocturne. Sorrow's Mercy: won't attack anyone weeping or grieving openly; open grief and honesty (Persuasion DC 17) can make him lay down his sword. Buys Caelum's rose for Nocturne in solo Adventure 3.
tells: Silver dust on his lips and on mourners' hands
Grey petals drift from his hem
Never eats or drinks at a wake
Won't carry a coffin; avoids iron nails
Insight DC 16: his grief is centuries old
revealTriggers: Someone refuses his comfort and names his trade
His glimmer trade is threatened
Someone grieves openly and honestly before him
Cold iron or a coffin nail in his palm
npcs.trueForm: A knight in black thorned plate inlaid with silver moths, helm under his arm, tears on a pale face.

stat.notes: Full 2024 stat block in Part 6.

npcs.sourceSection: Part 6 > The Fey NPCs > 5; Glamours & Reveals

portrait.note: True-form portrait; reveal only when a glamour drops.

npcs.name: Amaranth, the Smiling Herald
npcs.role: Thorn; Herald of the Dusk Court
npcs.publicRole: Contract notary on the bridge to the Hall of Vows
npcs.publicDescription: As players first meet them: Notary Amar Thorne, a meticulous, soft-spoken contract notary with a tiny office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows, who never lies, not even politely.
npcs.dmSecret: The Fae Duke's herald, tallying what Vesperine owes in the red Book of Forfeit Names. From Night 5 collects names openly; on Night 7 reads the Book aloud at the Council vote. Bound by the rules: cannot lie, cannot take an unwilling name, must honor any loophole (each of six Dusk Court debts has one; DC 17 Investigation). This is the 'Fae Duke's Herald' of the Unravelling clock and portrait prompt #32 (#20 is the Herald Ascendant). Round 2: Amaranth is the CR 6 herald in mortal Vesperine; inside the Thornwake, or at midnight on Night 7 if the Accord fails, they become the Herald Ascendant of the Dusk Court (Bestiary, CR 16).
motivations: Professional delight in a good loophole
tells: Never lies
Ink blooms into tiny roses as it dries
Refuses iron paperweights
Perception DC 14 in lamplight: antlered shadow
Smells of roses and old paper
revealTriggers: Dusk on Night 5
A PC signs anything Amaranth notarized
Someone finds a genuine loophole
Offered bread and salt as a guest
npcs.trueForm: An antlered herald in a dusk-colored coat, holding the vast red Book of Forfeit Names, still smiling.

stat.notes: Full 2024 stat block in Part 6.

portrait.note: True-form portrait; reveal only when a glamour drops.

npcs.name: Gristle Pike
npcs.publicDescription: A huge man with a hook for a hand and a voice like gravel.
npcs.dmSecret: Collects for Mother Brine; tonight he comes for Sabine's oathless guest and her mirror ('both or neither').

stat.notes: Campaign: Bandit Captain. Solo book (L1-3): a Tough with 40 HP at every level.

npcs.name: Anka
npcs.publicDescription: A twenty-three-year-old maid at Château Dusk with puncture marks on her wrist and a glassy look: a thrall of Lucan's.
npcs.dmSecret: Knows villagers are taken 'downstairs' and that Lucan's study has the red seal. If freed from compulsion she smuggles the PCs a servants' key in Side Adventure 4.

stat.notes: Implied; non-combatant.

npcs.name: Count Aurelio
npcs.role: Murder victim Valentin was framed for (solo only)
npcs.publicDescription: A count whose death Valentin was blamed for.
npcs.dmSecret: Lucan killed him and framed Valentin ('The consort will hang for Count Aurelio's death as planned'). Not mentioned in the world guide.

stat.notes: Flashbacks only (deceased).

npcs.name: Lord Silvano Quell
npcs.role: The Thorn Syndicate's puppet candidate for Oathwarden
npcs.publicRole: Poet-heir of House Quell; candidate for Oathwarden
npcs.publicDescription: The beautiful, languid last scion of House Quell, a founding house gone to seed. Writes poetry, faints elegantly, and owes everyone money.
npcs.dmSecret: Owes the Syndicate 11,000 ducats and has sworn Mother Brine a kiss-oath to 'stand when called'. Founding blood makes him a legal candidate. His proof of descent may be glimmer-forged. If sworn, Brine rules the Ledger through him.

stat.notes: Performance +4 (poetry).

npcs.name: Lord Orsino Varga
npcs.publicDescription: A broad, grey-bearded shipping magnate whose ships carry half of Lanternside's trade.
npcs.dmSecret: Syndicate-leaning; his vote can be swung by Kray's blackmail archive. One of the three Council names in Nocturne's jars.

stat.notes: Intimidation +4.

npcs.name: Madame Liliane Corvaux
npcs.role: Opera Council: impresaria of the Velvet Opera
npcs.publicRole: Opera Council: impresaria of the Velvet Opera
npcs.publicDescription: The Opera's glamorous impresaria; a sleek black bob with a white streak and a jeweled cane.
npcs.dmSecret: She hired Pell Ambrose to build the mirror door. Her vote is won by a performance worthy of her stage (Performance DC 16).

stat.notes: Performance +6.

npcs.name: Archivist-Mother Severine
npcs.role: Opera Council: abbess of the Veiled Sisters
npcs.publicRole: Opera Council: abbess of the Veiled Sisters
npcs.publicDescription: The serene abbess of the Veiled Sisters, keeper of the Ledger's rites.
npcs.dmSecret: Votes for whichever candidate's founding blood is proven before the Ledger. Source of the 'freely kissed into office' loophole.

stat.notes: Never attacks inside the Hall of Vows.

npcs.name: Lord Tancredi Morrow
npcs.publicDescription: A silver-haired half-elf lord with a duelist's bearing and a black rose on his lapel.
npcs.dmSecret: His name is in one of Nocturne's jars (Enthrallment 3): he votes as she commands until it is freed.

stat.notes: Enthrallment 3; cold iron makes him weep.

npcs.name: Dowager Ysolde Vane
npcs.publicDescription: A sharp-eyed, powdered dowager who never leaves a card table and cheats with style.
npcs.dmSecret: Allegra Vane's mother. Hers was the first name Amaranth wrote in the Book of Forfeit Names; strike it and she is yours. One of Nocturne's three.

stat.notes: Sleight of Hand +5.

npcs.name: Ilaria Venn, "the Last Kiss"
npcs.publicDescription: A sunny flower-seller with a basket of bloodroses who sells boutonnieres at the Opera doors.
npcs.dmSecret: Ilaria Venn, the most expensive Velvet Garrote in the Marches, hired by Mother Brine on Night 3 to kill the PCs (or Seraphine in the Tower of Penitence). Flirts targets onto balconies. Wants out of the Syndicate; a seat in the Glass would buy her.
tells: Insight DC 15: a false note in her laugh
Her reflection isn't smiling (Glass-Marked PCs)
A painted beauty mark in a different place every night
revealTriggers: She strikes on Night 3
A PC exposes her cover aloud in a crowd
She is caught with the garrote choker

stat.notes: Velvet Garrote (Bestiary) with the Nell Daisy trait and Bloodrose Calling Card reaction.

npcs.sourceSection: Part 4 > The Night 3 Assassin; Appendix D

guise.note: Cover identity; show this until the reveal (alias file name).

npcs.name: Sergeant Bettina Crane
npcs.role: Warden of the Tower of Penitence
npcs.publicRole: Warden of the Tower of Penitence
npcs.publicDescription: The honest, outnumbered sergeant who keeps the city's prison tower.
npcs.dmSecret: Won't take Syndicate money; will help the PCs protect a prisoner if they help her hold the stair.
npcs.sourceSection: Part 7 > Loose Threads > The Tower of Penitence

locations.name: Carnelia
locations.publicDescription: A sun-drenched, wine-dark land of canals, vineyards and old magic, ruled less by kings than by contracts. Five hundred years ago Vesperine's founders struck the Accord of Lips with the Fae Duke of the Dusk: any promise sealed with a kiss is magically binding and recorded in the Ledger of Vows. A forced or stolen kiss creates no oath.
locations.dmNotes: The Accord fails at midnight on Night 7 unless a new Oathwarden is sworn.
locations.text: A sun-drenched, wine-dark land of canals, vineyards and old magic, ruled less by kings than by contracts. Five hundred years ago Vesperine's founders struck the Accord of Lips with the Fae Duke of the Dusk: any promise sealed with a kiss is magically binding and recorded in the Ledger of Vows. A forced or stolen kiss creates no oath.

locations.name: Vesperine, the City of Masks
locations.publicDescription: Built on a hundred islands knit by bridges, gondola lanes and gossip; colored-glass lanterns over every canal. Masks are legal and fashionable at all hours. ~60,000 people. Ruled in practice by the Opera Council; policed by the Lantern Watch; currency gold ducats and silver kisses. Notable vices: masquerades, card salons, Vinehold wine, dream-moth dust, duelling for love.
locations.dmNotes: Hub of the central mystery. See the Unravelling clock (Part 4) for what changes each night.
locations.sourceSection: Part 1 > The Hub City; Part 3 > Map of Vesperine
locations.text: Built on a hundred islands knit by bridges, gondola lanes and gossip; colored-glass lanterns over every canal. Masks are legal and fashionable at all hours. ~60,000 people. Ruled in practice by the Opera Council; policed by the Lantern Watch; currency gold ducats and silver kisses. Notable vices: masquerades, card salons, Vinehold wine, dream-moth dust, duelling for love.

locations.name: The Velvet Marches
locations.publicDescription: The countryside Vesperine depends on and pretends not to need: Thicketmoor, Lanternwood, Saltgrave Coast, Duskvine Valley, Emberpeaks.
locations.dmNotes: Each region hosts one side adventure (one night on the clock each).
locations.sourceSection: Part 1 > The Velvet Marches; Part 3 > Map
locations.text: The countryside Vesperine depends on and pretends not to need: Thicketmoor, Lanternwood, Saltgrave Coast, Duskvine Valley, Emberpeaks.

locations.name: The Thicketmoor
locations.publicDescription: Brambles the size of houses, golden honey dripping from wasp hives, and warm mud pits ogres consider a spa. Travellers vanish. Mostly men. Mostly loudly.
locations.dmNotes: Home of the Honeyhorn Clan; Side Adventure 1. Pell Ambrose is held here.
locations.travel: 1 day on foot / ½ day by horse
locations.text: Brambles the size of houses, golden honey dripping from wasp hives, and warm mud pits ogres consider a spa. Travellers vanish. Mostly men. Mostly loudly.

locations.name: The Lanternwood
locations.publicDescription: A forest where the trees give off soft blue light and moths the size of cats drift between them. Sleepers who wander here wake days later, smiling, with no memory of their dreams.
locations.dmNotes: Seat of the Moth Court (Side Adventure 2); the Dusk Court is reachable through it at twilight. Caelum's gateway landing point. Source of the moth-orchid used for Widow's Sigh.
locations.travel: 1½ days on foot / 1 day by horse
locations.text: A forest where the trees give off soft blue light and moths the size of cats drift between them. Sleepers who wander here wake days later, smiling, with no memory of their dreams.

locations.name: The Saltgrave Coast
locations.publicDescription: Black cliffs, shipwrecks, and singing at night that every sailor pretends not to hear. Smugglers bring Syndicate cargo through the sea caves.
locations.dmNotes: Home of the Drowned Choir and Kray's Smugglers' Grotto (Side Adventure 3). Marisol's gateway landing point.
locations.travel: 1 day on foot / ½ day by boat
locations.text: Black cliffs, shipwrecks, and singing at night that every sailor pretends not to hear. Smugglers bring Syndicate cargo through the sea caves.

locations.name: The Duskvine Valley
locations.publicDescription: The most beautiful countryside in Carnelia: golden terraces, poplars, villages where everyone is a little too pale and very well-rested. Château Dusk crowns the hill.
locations.dmNotes: Side Adventure 4: Lucan Vey's abductions.
locations.travel: 2 days on foot / 1 day by horse
locations.text: The most beautiful countryside in Carnelia: golden terraces, poplars, villages where everyone is a little too pale and very well-rested. Château Dusk crowns the hill.

locations.name: The Emberpeaks
locations.publicDescription: Steaming hot springs, copper-veined cliffs and rope sky-bridges. Miners leave love poems at shrine-stones to keep the dragon in a good mood.
locations.dmNotes: Vexirra's lair (Side Adventure 5); Copperhand Miners' Guild.
locations.travel: 3 days on foot / 2 days by horse
locations.text: Steaming hot springs, copper-veined cliffs and rope sky-bridges. Miners leave love poems at shrine-stones to keep the dragon in a good mood.

locations.name: The Dusk Court (palace 'just behind the sunset')
locations.publicDescription: Fairy-tale talk of a palace 'just behind the sunset'.
locations.dmNotes: Reachable through the Lanternwood at twilight. If the Accord fails (Ending D) the way home runs through this court. Never mapped or described in detail.
locations.text: Fairy-tale talk of a palace 'just behind the sunset'.

locations.name: The Gilded Crescent (District 1)
locations.publicDescription: Noble palazzos facing the Grand Canal; balconies built for eavesdropping. Home of House Morrow and the shuttered Sable Palazzo.
locations.dmNotes: Also hosts the Black Fan salon.
locations.text: Noble palazzos facing the Grand Canal; balconies built for eavesdropping. Home of House Morrow and the shuttered Sable Palazzo.

locations.name: The Velvet Quarter (District 2)
locations.publicDescription: Theaters, salons, pleasure-gardens and the Velvet Opera, a cathedral of red plush and gold leaf.
locations.dmNotes: Also The Blue Hour and the Hush House.
locations.text: Theaters, salons, pleasure-gardens and the Velvet Opera, a cathedral of red plush and gold leaf.

locations.name: Needle Row (District 3)
locations.publicDescription: Artisans' lanes: tailors, wigmakers, perfumers, and the Atelier of Madame Rook.
locations.dmNotes: Also Vos Perfumery and The Gilded Thimble.
locations.text: Artisans' lanes: tailors, wigmakers, perfumers, and the Atelier of Madame Rook.

locations.name: The Drowned Market (District 4)
locations.publicDescription: A half-sunken flea market under the old city: ankle-deep water, floating lanterns, stalls on stilts. Reached by the stairs at Gull Steps.
locations.dmNotes: The Thorn Syndicate sells anything here, including secrets, debts and (from Night 3) glimmer.
locations.text: A half-sunken flea market under the old city: ankle-deep water, floating lanterns, stalls on stilts. Reached by the stairs at Gull Steps.

locations.name: The Hall of Vows (District 5)
locations.publicDescription: A white-marble temple-library on its own island: silence and the sound of a pen that writes by itself. The Ledger of Vows rests on a lectern of living rose-thorn, tended by the Veiled Sisters. Since the murder the ink bleeds and pages blank out.
locations.dmNotes: Above the Vault of Broken Vows. The Sisters can annul forged vows and reveal the succession loophole.
locations.text: A white-marble temple-library on its own island: silence and the sound of a pen that writes by itself. The Ledger of Vows rests on a lectern of living rose-thorn, tended by the Veiled Sisters. Since the murder the ink bleeds and pages blank out.

locations.name: Lanternside (District 6)
locations.publicDescription: Docks, taverns, sailors, and the Lantern Watch's leaning headquarters, the Tilted House.
locations.dmNotes: Riots on Night 3; Brother Ash (Merrow) comforts mourners at wakes here. Isaveth woke on these docks with no name 31 years ago.
locations.text: Docks, taverns, sailors, and the Lantern Watch's leaning headquarters, the Tilted House.

locations.name: Cypress Isle
locations.publicDescription: The cemetery island.
locations.dmNotes: Ghosts walk here from Night 4. The Sable Crypt and, beneath it, the Thornwake.
locations.text: The cemetery island.

locations.name: The Velvet Opera
locations.publicDescription: A gold-and-crimson temple to spectacle: five tiers of private boxes, each with its own little curtain for 'private conversations'. Backstage is a maze of rope, sandbags and costume racks. Feel: perfumed heat, applause, whispers behind fans.
locations.dmNotes: Venue of the murder and of the Night 7 Council vote.
locations.text: A gold-and-crimson temple to spectacle: five tiers of private boxes, each with its own little curtain for 'private conversations'. Backstage is a maze of rope, sandbags and costume racks. Feel: perfumed heat, applause, whispers behind fans.

locations.name: The Rosewater Gallery
locations.publicDescription: A long salon above the stage lined with mirrors and rose-trellises around a fountain of scented rosewater. Its tall clock, the city's most famous timepiece, stopped at 11:47 on the night of the murder. The mirror wall's great central pane is very old and very flattering.
locations.dmNotes: The murder scene. A secret door behind the mirror wall connects to the Dressing Gallery. The central pane is the Oathless Glass. Clues: stopped clock (Riddle 6, Keystone), lavender ribbon on the trellis, stain darkest under the mask.
locations.text: A long salon above the stage lined with mirrors and rose-trellises around a fountain of scented rosewater. Its tall clock, the city's most famous timepiece, stopped at 11:47 on the night of the murder. The mirror wall's great central pane is very old and very flattering.

locations.name: The Dressing Gallery
locations.publicDescription: Racks of costumes, wig-stands, and Madame Rook's fitting table covered in feathers and gold leaf.
locations.dmNotes: Connected to the Rosewater Gallery by the mirror-wall door. The original unpoisoned mask (ribbon cut, not frayed) is hidden in a costume trunk (Keystone); actors say Thessaly stepped out around quarter to midnight. Hale's guards were pulled from its corridor 11:30-midnight.
locations.text: Racks of costumes, wig-stands, and Madame Rook's fitting table covered in feathers and gold leaf.

locations.name: The Sable Palazzo
locations.publicDescription: Aurelian's home in the Gilded Crescent: elegant, cold, too big, now shuttered.
locations.dmNotes: Study with a riddle-locked writing desk (Riddle 1: journal and the faceless porcelain mask); a portrait gallery with a painted-over young bride with Thessaly's eyes; a hidden cache with his private journal in the bedchamber.
locations.text: Aurelian's home in the Gilded Crescent: elegant, cold, too big, now shuttered.

locations.name: House Morrow's palazzo
locations.publicDescription: The Gilded Crescent seat of House Morrow, a founding family.
locations.dmNotes: Celestine's vanity holds the fake oath-breaking salts; her grate holds the burned love letter. Never described in detail.
locations.text: The Gilded Crescent seat of House Morrow, a founding family.

locations.name: The Atelier of Madame Rook
locations.publicDescription: A cozy shop overflowing with masks: feathered, porcelain, lacquered, beaded. Thessaly lives above it with three cats named after her ex-lovers.
locations.dmNotes: Back workroom: glue pots, gold leaf, and a hatbox holding a wedding mask and the vow-page itself wrapped in lavender silk (Keystone); a pressed moth-orchid in a book of poems. Search: Investigation DC 16 or Stealth DC 15 to search unseen.
locations.notes: Gazetteer says the wedding mask was made 'forty years ago'; the Clue Trail calls it 'thirty-year-old'; the wedding was 31 years ago.
locations.text: A cozy shop overflowing with masks: feathered, porcelain, lacquered, beaded. Thessaly lives above it with three cats named after her ex-lovers.

locations.name: Vos Perfumery
locations.publicDescription: Glass bottles in every color, a copper still, and a tiefling who can identify anyone by scent.
locations.dmNotes: Ezren's scent-coded order ledger (Riddle 3): 'Lavender: 1 vial bloodrose' (Keystone); salts order for 'Lady C.M.' (red herring).
locations.text: Glass bottles in every color, a copper still, and a tiefling who can identify anyone by scent.

locations.name: The Vault of Broken Vows
locations.publicDescription: Below the Hall of Vows; stores torn-out, annulled pages.
locations.dmNotes: Door riddle (Riddle 2) plus Varo's key or Thieves' Tools DC 18. Missing page stub dated 31 years ago: '…Aurel Fenn and Isaveth Sable, everything I am…'.
locations.text: Below the Hall of Vows; stores torn-out, annulled pages.

locations.name: Things That Shouldn't Be Sold (Mother Brine's shop)
locations.publicDescription: A stall-shop in the Drowned Market; you are asked a password through a slot in the door.
locations.dmNotes: Password Riddle 5. Brine's sale record of the vow-page and one of the three masks, signed with Thessaly's maker's mark (Keystone).
locations.text: A stall-shop in the Drowned Market; you are asked a password through a slot in the door.

locations.name: Gull Steps
locations.publicDescription: The stairs down into the Drowned Market.
locations.text: The stairs down into the Drowned Market.

locations.name: The Tilted House
locations.publicDescription: Lantern Watch headquarters, leaning so badly that pens roll off desks.
locations.dmNotes: Captain Hale's office has a locked strongbox containing a Syndicate purse.
locations.text: Lantern Watch headquarters, leaning so badly that pens roll off desks.

locations.name: The Sable Crypt
locations.publicDescription: The Sable family tomb on Cypress Isle: cold marble, wilted lilies, a line of old family sarcophagi.
locations.dmNotes: Includes a marble sarcophagus inscribed 'Lady Isaveth Sable, Beloved Wife, Lost to the Sea' (the name is a spoiler term, so it stays out of players.md until found). The sarcophagus is empty except for a lavender silk wedding veil (Keystone). Riddle 4 on the lid. Ghosts (Night 4+) whisper 'she lives, she sews, she smiles'. A stair of black roses beneath leads to the Thornwake.
locations.text: The Sable family tomb on Cypress Isle: cold marble, wilted lilies, a line of old family sarcophagi.

locations.name: The Thornwake Ballroom
locations.dmNotes: A sunken ballroom forgotten three centuries ago, beneath the Sable Crypt: Rose Stair, Hall of Partners, Mirror Gallery, Glimmer Vats, Name-Jar Cellar (Aurel Fenn's name), Black Throne. Nocturne holds court here Nights 5-7.

locations.name: The Blue Hour
locations.publicDescription: Sabine Velour's card salon: blue light, smoke, a grand piano, velvet booths and a gilded mirror in the back room.
locations.dmNotes: Bankrolled by Old Mother Brine. Sabine's gateway landing point. Cael Rosier (Caelum) gambles here.
locations.text: Sabine Velour's card salon: blue light, smoke, a grand piano, velvet booths and a gilded mirror in the back room.

locations.name: The Black Fan
locations.publicDescription: The most exclusive masked salon in the Gilded Crescent, hosted by the widow Madame Noor Vesperelle in a candlelit palazzo where every mirror is draped in black crepe.
locations.dmNotes: Nocturne Vesh's human-guise salon.
locations.text: The most exclusive masked salon in the Gilded Crescent, hosted by the widow Madame Noor Vesperelle in a candlelit palazzo where every mirror is draped in black crepe.

locations.name: The Lilywater Baths
locations.publicDescription: The city's cheapest and most popular bathhouse; patrons who doze in the warm pools sometimes wake much later than they meant to.
locations.dmNotes: Ondine's guise workplace (Dina Mire); a mountain of single shoes in the lost-and-found.
locations.text: The city's cheapest and most popular bathhouse; patrons who doze in the warm pools sometimes wake much later than they meant to.

locations.name: The Gilded Thimble
locations.publicDescription: A cozy tavern on Needle Row with pewter mugs and iron tankards on the top shelf.
locations.dmNotes: Pipwhistle's guise workplace (Pip Dewley).
locations.text: A cozy tavern on Needle Row with pewter mugs and iron tankards on the top shelf.

locations.name: The Hush House
locations.publicDescription: A dream-reader's parlor opened this season, selling little blue bottles of sleep-tonic.
locations.dmNotes: Queen Ilysse's guise (Madame Ilse Hush); some clients don't wake for days.
locations.text: A dream-reader's parlor opened this season, selling little blue bottles of sleep-tonic.

locations.name: Notary Amar Thorne's office
locations.publicDescription: A tiny notary's office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows; ink here dries into tiny roses.
locations.dmNotes: Amaranth's guise office.
locations.text: A tiny notary's office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows; ink here dries into tiny roses.

locations.name: The Tower of Penitence
locations.publicDescription: Vesperine's prison: a narrow white tower on a rock in the lagoon, reached only by a Watch barge, where the condemned make lace, masks, and confessions.
locations.dmNotes: Where the city puts anyone the PCs accuse; Ilaria's cell assassination of Seraphine (Night +1); Isaveth's cell in Ending A; seed 'Visiting Hours'.
locations.text: Vesperine's prison: a narrow white tower on a rock in the lagoon, reached only by a Watch barge, where the condemned make lace, masks, and confessions.

locations.name: The Bog Causeway
locations.publicDescription: The causeway road from Vesperine into the Thicketmoor, where men have been vanishing.
locations.dmNotes: Ondine's pool lies along it. Honeyhorn matrons raid it if the clan is wronged.
locations.text: The causeway road from Vesperine into the Thicketmoor, where men have been vanishing.

locations.name: The Hive-Hall of Honeyhorn
locations.publicDescription: The Honeyhorn den, with famous mud wallows.
locations.dmNotes: Eight areas: Bramble Gate, Wallows, Pampering Pen, Kitchen of the Disappointment Pot, Moot Ring, Hulga's Bower, Sulking Stones, Sallowmere's Hut.
locations.text: The Honeyhorn den, with famous mud wallows.

locations.name: The Sulking Stones
locations.publicDescription: Six grey standing stones in a circle, each vaguely ogre-shaped and scowling, arms crossed.
locations.dmNotes: The petrified ogre husbands; riddle on the center stone.
locations.text: Six grey standing stones in a circle, each vaguely ogre-shaped and scowling, arms crossed.

locations.name: Sallowmere's Hut
locations.dmNotes: A chicken-legged hut half-sunk in mud beneath the bog, reached through a sinkhole in the kitchen (DC 15 Perception to notice the draft).

locations.name: The Cocoon Palace
locations.publicDescription: A towering tree of pale silk glowing like a paper lantern; court of the Moth Queen.
locations.dmNotes: Avenue of Lights, Dust Fields, Hall of Wings, Mirror Pool, Silk Library (wedding-dream Keystone, Teodor), Hush Throne.
locations.text: A towering tree of pale silk glowing like a paper lantern; court of the Moth Queen.

locations.name: The Smugglers' Grotto
locations.publicDescription: Sea caves on the Saltgrave cliffs where smugglers land Syndicate cargo.
locations.dmNotes: Wrecker's Beacon, Tidepool Stair (tide timer), Syndicate Warehouse, Drowned Chapel (song-lock), Choir Lagoon, Kray's Strongroom (Pearl Heart, blackmail archive).
locations.text: Sea caves on the Saltgrave cliffs where smugglers land Syndicate cargo.

locations.name: Château Dusk
locations.publicDescription: The château crowning the Duskvine hill, famous for the Harvest Masquerade and the Crimson Vintage.
locations.dmNotes: Grand Tasting Hall, Pressing Room, Barrel Labyrinth, Vintage Vault (Morwenna's diary), Lucan's Crypt-Chapel, Sunroof Tower.
locations.text: The château crowning the Duskvine hill, famous for the Harvest Masquerade and the Crimson Vintage.

locations.name: Duskvine village (Marta Ilic's inn)
locations.publicDescription: A sleepy valley village whose people have been disappearing.
locations.dmNotes: Unnamed in the guide; Marta Ilic's inn is the PCs' contact point.
locations.text: A sleepy valley village whose people have been disappearing.

locations.name: The Copper Road
locations.publicDescription: The courier road from Vesperine to the Emberpeaks, where mailbags are being snatched.
locations.text: The courier road from Vesperine to the Emberpeaks, where mailbags are being snatched.

locations.name: The Vine Road
locations.publicDescription: The road from Vesperine to the Duskvine Valley.
locations.text: The road from Vesperine to the Duskvine Valley.

locations.name: The Lair of Steam & Paper
locations.publicDescription: Vexirra's hot-spring lair.
locations.dmNotes: Sky-Bridge, Kobold Scriptorium, Hot-Spring Galleries, Echo Hall (riddle), Hoard of Letters (fire hazard; Aurelian's last letter), Vexirra's Bath.
locations.text: Vexirra's hot-spring lair.

locations.name: The Bridge of Sighing Lanterns
locations.publicDescription: A long, lantern-hung bridge to the Hall of Vows' island. Its lamps sigh when an oath is broken nearby.
locations.dmNotes: Night 7, Phase 2: the Procession of Lanterns and Brine's ambush (Encounter 1). Vexirra can light it; a Coral Sentinel can hold one end.
locations.text: A long, lantern-hung bridge to the Hall of Vows' island. Its lamps sigh when an oath is broken nearby.

locations.name: The Notary Quarter
locations.publicDescription: A tangle of archways, stairs and tiny offices around the Hall of Vows' landing, where contracts are witnessed and fine print explained.
locations.dmNotes: Includes Notary Amar Thorne's office. The Syndicate wants every Witness Raven here dead before Night 7 (Bestiary hook).
locations.text: A tangle of archways, stairs and tiny offices around the Hall of Vows' landing, where contracts are witnessed and fine print explained.

locations.name: The Deep Crypt of Château Dusk
locations.dmNotes: The Crimson Patriarch sleeps here under Morwenna's kiss-oath of rest. Lucan's true plan is to wake him (Night 5).
locations.sourceSection: Part 7 > Loose Threads > The Crimson Patriarch

factions.name: The Opera Council
factions.summary: Seven patrons of the Velvet Opera who own most of the city's debt: Ottoline (chair), Morwenna, Orsino Varga, Liliane Corvaux, Archivist-Mother Severine, Tancredi Morrow, Ysolde Vane. Four votes name an Oathwarden.

factions.name: The Lantern Watch
factions.summary: Vesperine's underpaid, overdressed city watch; HQ the Tilted House.

factions.name: The Thorn Syndicate
factions.summary: The underworld that sells anything in the Drowned Market, including secrets and debts. Run, though few know it, by Old Mother Brine.

factions.name: The Veiled Sisters
factions.summary: Keepers of the Ledger of Vows in the Hall of Vows.

factions.name: House Sable
factions.summary: Founding house; seat of the late Oathwarden.

factions.name: House Morrow
factions.summary: Founding house of the Gilded Crescent.

factions.name: House Dusk
factions.summary: Vampire nobility of the Duskvine Valley.

factions.name: The Velvet Opera company
factions.summary: Singers, stagehands, and carpenters of the Opera.

factions.name: The Honeyhorn Clan
factions.summary: Ogresses of the Thicketmoor.

factions.name: The Moth Court
factions.summary: Dream-eating fey of the Lanternwood; vassal of the Dusk Court.

factions.name: The Drowned Choir
factions.summary: Merfolk sirens of the Saltgrave sea caves.

factions.name: The Copperhand Miners' Guild
factions.summary: Dwarf and gnome miners of the Emberpeaks.

factions.name: The Inkscale Troupe
factions.summary: Vexirra's kobold poet-servants.

factions.name: The Dusk Court
factions.summary: The Fae Duke's court 'just behind the sunset'; creditor of the Accord.

factions.name: The Hedgefolk
factions.summary: Free fey of hedgerows, fountains, and canal-weeds.

factions.name: The Thornwake
factions.summary: The Duke's secret police of seduction under Cypress Isle.

factions.name: The Oathless Glass (gateway characters)
factions.summary: Those who reach through the Glass for the PCs.

factions.name: Independent
factions.summary: No faction.

mystery.title: The Black Kiss

victim.public: Lord Aurelian Sable, Oathwarden of Vesperine for thirty years, kissed the diva Seraphine Lark on the Rosewater balcony at midnight on the Night of Unmasking, staggered, clawed at his mask and fell dead by the chaise. His lips and the skin beneath his mask were stained black as Ledger ink. The crowd screamed 'poison kiss.'
victim.dm: The stain spread from beneath the mask, not from his lips: Widow's Sigh in the mask lining, activated by Seraphine's bloodrose perfume.

public.claimed_alibi: On stage until 11:50, then on the Rosewater balcony with the crowd until the midnight kiss.
public.looks_guilty: She literally kissed him and he died. Her lips are black.
public.flirt_dc: DC 15 (DC 10 if a PC compliments something other than her beauty)

dm.secret: Syndicate spy on Aurelian for two years; in love with Celestine.
dm.under_pressure: Aurelian was frightened for weeks, got a faceless porcelain mask, murmured 'The masks remember'; at about quarter to midnight she saw Madame Rook's silver braid in the mirror wall fussing with his ribbon.

public.claimed_alibi: Alone on the balcony, enjoying the view.

riddles.title: Riddle 1: Aurelian's Desk
riddles.first_line: Carved to smile, I cannot laugh;
riddles.hint: What does every dancer in Vesperine wear tonight?
riddles.promptHtml: Carved to smile, I cannot laugh; I wear no face, yet I am half of every lie the dancers tell. Lift me, love, and break the spell.

riddles.title: Riddle 2: The Vault of Broken Vows
riddles.hint: What is this whole hall full of?
riddles.promptHtml: Given freely, I weigh nothing; broken, I'm as heavy as stone. Lips make me, lies unmake me, and I am never wholly your own.

riddles.title: Riddle 3: Ezren's Scent-Coded Ledger
riddles.answer: A scent (perfume). Code-names: Lavender = Madame Rook; Frost-Lily = Celestine; Bloodrose = Seraphine.
riddles.promptHtml: I arrive before the lover and linger when she's gone. You cannot see or hold me, yet I swear where she has been.

riddles.title: Riddle 4: The Empty Sarcophagus
riddles.first_line: What can be stolen, yet never be touched,
riddles.promptHtml: What can be stolen, yet never be touched, lost while you hold it, and taken with a kiss — and returned to its owner only by being spoken?

riddles.title: Riddle 5: Mother Brine's Password
riddles.first_line: I have leaves but no branches,
riddles.hint: What does every scholar and lover in the Hall of Vows keep their eyes on?
riddles.promptHtml: I have leaves but no branches, a spine but no bones; I hold a thousand kisses and I've never been kissed.

riddles.title: Riddle 6: The Gallery Clock
riddles.first_line: I have a face but cannot see,
riddles.answer: A clock. The pendulum is bent and caught with lavender silk: knocked, not wound down, at 11:47.
riddles.promptHtml: I have a face but cannot see, two hands but cannot hold. I strike, but I wound no one; stop my heart and I grow cold — yet the moment of my dying is the truth I've always told.

timeline.event: The founders strike the Accord of Lips with the Fae Duke; Lady Oriane Sable adds the Oathless Clause and commissions the Oathless Glass from Mirelle; Lysander is bound into the Glass by his promise to Oriane.
During the Duke's first collection the Glass cracks; shards scatter across many worlds.
The Thornwake ballroom is forgotten by the city.
Caelum gives Queen Ilysse a rose love-token (solo Adventure 3). Morwenna begins two centuries of feeding only on willing donors.
Valentin is Morwenna's consort 'for a hundred years' until Lucan frames him for Count Aurelio's murder; exile date unstated.
At the last proper Courting Moot, Auntie Sallowmere curses the Honeyhorn ogre men into the Sulking Stones.

Nocturne whispers the literal-vow trick to Aurel Fenn for his true name. He marries Isaveth Sable; the Ledger transfers her name, title, inheritance and memory to him. She wakes on the Lanternside docks and becomes Thessaly Rook. Morwenna attends the wedding.
The previous Oathwarden dies; the Glass summons Sabine Velour, who endorses 'Aurelian Sable' with a kiss. He serves as Oathwarden for thirty years; Thessaly makes his festival mask every year.
Aurelian secretly cuts the wedding-vow page out of the Ledger.
Seraphine begins spying on Aurelian for the Thorn Syndicate.
Varo steals the vow-page from Aurelian's desk; Mother Brine sells it to a lady in a grey veil for three masks; Thessaly touches it and remembers everything.
'Madame Noor Vesperelle' arrives and opens the Black Fan. Thessaly attends Morwenna's party (solo Adventure 5).
'Madame R.' buys a vial of bloodrose; Celestine buys fake oath-breaking salts; Thessaly trades her wedding-day dream to the Moth Court for Widow's Sigh.
Aurelian, frightened, receives a faceless porcelain mask. Lucan abducts Duskvine villagers. Vexirra's kobolds steal mailbags on the Copper Road.
Aurelian writes his last letter to his lawyer ('look to the woman who makes my face'); it is snatched on the Copper Road.
Hale takes Varo's purse and pulls guards from the Dressing Gallery corridor until midnight.
Aurelian sends for Thessaly to fix his fraying ribbon; Seraphine glimpses her silver braid in the mirror wall.
Thessaly swaps the mask through the mirror door; the clock stops; her ribbon snags. Pell Ambrose and Lysander both see her.
Seraphine leaves the stage and goes to the balcony.
The unmasking kiss; Aurelian dies. Varo lifts the vault key from his coat in the cloakroom. The Oathless Clause wakes the Glass and pulls the PCs through.
Pell Ambrose flees the city and is taken on the Bog Causeway.
