entries.text: A creature Grappled by the ooze at the end of its turn has its mouth sealed with hot wax and can't speak or cast spells with Verbal components until it uses an action to peel the wax away.

entries.name: Pseudopod
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12).

bestiary.name: Wax Seal Ooze
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Red sealing wax, warmed and poured a thousand times over secrets, can come to love them. A wax seal ooze is a glossy crimson blob that lives in archives and drips over open letters, re-sealing them. It doesn't like readers, so it seals their mouths shut.
bestiary.where: Archives, notaries' offices, the Opera Council's records room.
bestiary.tactics: It drops from a shelf onto anyone opening a document, grapples, and seals their lips.
hooks: The Syndicate's blackmail archive is guarded by a wax seal ooze, and every letter has been re-sealed.
A notary's oldest seal has started walking.
bestiary.imm: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone

lines: Gear Notary's Seal, Sealing Daggers, Contract Satchel
Languages Common, Infernal, Sylvan, and two others

entries.name: Binding Signature
entries.text: A creature that signs a contract the broker presents is bound by its terms as if by a Geas (save DC 13) for as long as the contract says. A creature that is Charmed or coerced when it signs is not bound, and the broker knows it.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The broker makes two Sealing Dagger attacks.

entries.name: Sealing Dagger
entries.text: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The oath-broker casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13): At Will: Comprehend Languages, Message; 1/Day Each: Command, Hold Person, Zone of Truth

entries.name: Clause of Recourse
entries.text: Trigger: A creature within 30 feet that owes the broker anything hits it with an attack. Response: The attacker makes a DC 13 Charisma saving throw. Failure: The attack misses instead.

bestiary.name: Oath-Broker
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Notaries who discovered they could make more money writing bad contracts than honest ones became oath-brokers. Silver-tongued and impeccably dressed, they'll bind anyone to anything: debt, service, marriage, a name. They work for the Syndicate, for Lady Nocturne, and for anyone who pays. They are, crucially, scrupulous about consent. A forced signature is worthless, and they know it.
bestiary.where: The Notary Quarter, Syndicate dens, the back rooms of the Velvet Opera.
bestiary.tactics: A broker talks first, always, and fights only when the paperwork fails. It throws daggers from behind bodyguards and uses Hold Person on whoever seems likeliest to tear up a contract.
hooks: An oath-broker holds the deed to the party's safehouse and wants to discuss terms.
Someone signed a party member's name to a marriage contract. The broker is very sorry, legally speaking.

lines: Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 10

entries.name: Written Thorns
entries.text: Each thorn on the briar is a tiny barbed letter. A creature hit by the briar sees a word of its own secret written on its skin for 1 hour.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The briar makes two Thorn Lash attacks.

entries.name: Thorn Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 15 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13) if it is Medium or smaller.

bestiary.name: Inkthorn Briar
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Under the Syndicate's archive grows a hedge watered with spilled ink. Its thorns are letters and its leaves are pages, and it whispers fragments of every secret ever written in the vault above. Lady Nocturne planted it to guard her name-ledger.
bestiary.where: The Syndicate's archive, overgrown libraries, the garden of a dead notary.
bestiary.tactics: The briar grapples the nearest creature and drags it into its thorns. Fire sends it into a frenzy of thrashing.
hooks: The path to Nocturne's name-ledger runs through an inkthorn briar that knows everyone's secrets.
A notary's garden has sprouted a briar overnight, and the notary is missing.

lines: Immunities Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned
Languages Understands Common but can't speak

entries.name: Catalogue
entries.text: The sentinel knows the exact location of every document in its archive. If any is removed without a signed slip, it knows instantly.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The sentinel makes two Ledger Slam attacks.

entries.name: Ledger Slam
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Confiscate
entries.text: Strength Saving Throw: DC 14, one creature within 10 feet holding a document or book. Failure: The sentinel takes the document and files it inside its chest.

bestiary.name: Archive Sentinel
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: The Accord's great archive is guarded by sentinels of bronze and oak: tall, faceless constructs with filing drawers for ribs and brass ledger-books for fists. They have no malice, only a need for order. Remove a document without a signed slip and they will follow you to the ends of Carnelia to get it back.
bestiary.where: The Accord's archive, the Syndicate's vault, any great library.
bestiary.tactics: The sentinel targets whoever holds a stolen document, confiscates it, then escorts the thief out.
hooks: The evidence that proves Lady Nocturne's crimes is in the Accord's archive, and the clerk who signs slips is dead.
A sentinel has walked out of the archive and into the city, hunting an overdue library book.
bestiary.imm: Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned

lines: Immunities Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Poisoned
Languages The languages it knew in life

entries.name: Bound to the Oath
entries.text: The forsworn dead always knows the direction and distance to the creature it swore its unkept oath against. If reduced to 0 Hit Points while that creature lives, it rises again at dawn with all its Hit Points.

entries.name: Turn Resistance
entries.text: The forsworn dead has Advantage on saving throws against any effect that turns Undead.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The forsworn dead makes two Oathblade attacks.

entries.name: Oathblade
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Accusing Glare
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature the forsworn dead can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition until the end of its next turn. If it is the object of the oath, it is instead Paralyzed for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns.

bestiary.name: Forsworn Dead
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Some knights died swearing vengeance, and the Accord, which honors oaths above all, will not let them rest until they get it. The forsworn dead are armored corpses with grave-light in their eyes, walking slowly and tirelessly toward their betrayers. They can't be bargained with or turned away. They'll stop when the oath is fulfilled, or when someone convinces them it was unjust.
bestiary.where: Old battlefields, the roads of the Velvet Marches, the Accord's courthouse steps.
bestiary.tactics: It ignores everyone but the object of its oath unless they get in the way. Then it hacks through them.
hooks: Sir Valentin Dusk's old squire has risen as forsworn dead, and he's walking toward Valentin.
The forsworn dead marching on Vesperine swore their oaths against the Thornwake. They could be useful allies.

lines: Immunities Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained

entries.name: Swirling Pages
entries.text: The inkstorm is a whirlwind of ink and loose pages. Its space is Heavily Obscured, and it can enter a hostile creature's space.

entries.name: Blotting
entries.text: Any written text the inkstorm passes over is smeared and unreadable unless it is protected by magic.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The inkstorm makes two Ink Lash attacks.

entries.name: Ink Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Inkstorm
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: When the Syndicate burned the Accord's lower archive, the ink and paper didn't burn. They rose. An inkstorm is a howling whirlwind of black ink and fluttering pages, every one of them a ruined contract. Notaries fear them more than fire.
bestiary.where: Ruined archives, the Notary Quarter, storms over the Accord's courts.
bestiary.tactics: The storm surges into crowds, blinding them, and blots out any contract being carried.
hooks: An inkstorm is circling the Notary Quarter, and every contract it touches is being voided.
Someone wants an inkstorm released inside the Syndicate's archive.
bestiary.imm: Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained

lines: Languages Understands every language but can speak only names it has eaten

entries.name: Forgettable
entries.text: Creatures that can see the gnawer have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to notice it, and forget its appearance a minute after it leaves their sight.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The gnawer makes three Gnaw attacks.

entries.name: Gnaw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Eat a Name
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature within 5 feet that is Bloodied. Failure: The target forgets its own name, and everyone who knows it forgets it too, until the gnawer dies or a Remove Curse is cast on the target. While nameless, the target has Disadvantage on Charisma checks.

bestiary.name: Nameless Gnawer
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Some things live between the lines of the Accord. A nameless gnawer is a thin grey shape with too many teeth and no face, which eats names. A person whose name is gnawed away is forgotten by everyone, even those who love them. Lady Nocturne's name-ledger attracts gnawers like spilled sugar attracts ants.
bestiary.where: Between the lines of contracts, archives, Nocturne's vault, the shadows of the Notary Quarter.
bestiary.tactics: The gnawer ambushes from walls, focuses on one victim until Bloodied, then eats its name and slips away. Calling the victim's name aloud lets the target and its allies retain their memory.
hooks: Something is eating names in the Notary Quarter, and nobody can remember who went missing.
A gnawer has eaten one of the party's names. Only something written before the bite can bring it back.

lines: Senses Blindsight 30 ft., Darkvision 120 ft.; Passive Perception 15
Languages Common, Draconic, and every language it has read

entries.name: Living Record
entries.text: The drake's scales are inked with every contract it has witnessed. It can recite any of them verbatim and knows instantly if a creature within 60 feet is breaking one.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The drake makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Ink Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 45 (10d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Vellum Drake
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: A vellum drake is a dragon of the archives: pale as fresh parchment, scales lettered in fine black script, breath of ink. The Accord keeps a few as living witnesses to its most important treaties. They love order, reading, and being consulted. They hate being lied to.
bestiary.where: The Accord's high archive, the courthouse roofs, ancient libraries.
bestiary.tactics: The drake breathes ink to blind, then bites oath-breakers. Proving it was lied to turns it on the liar.
hooks: The only surviving copy of the Accord's founding treaty is tattooed on a vellum drake that has gone missing.
A vellum drake will testify against Lady Nocturne, if the party can get it safely to the courts.

entries.name: Compound Interest
entries.text: Whenever a creature that owes the fiend a debt takes damage from it, the creature takes an extra 4 (1d8) Psychic damage for each week the debt is overdue (maximum 4d8).

entries.name: Debt-Sense
entries.text: The fiend knows the exact amount and location of every debtor in its ledger.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The fiend makes three Ledger Chain attacks.

entries.name: Ledger Chain
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) Necrotic damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 17).

entries.name: Collect
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature Grappled by the fiend. Failure: The target gains 1 Exhaustion level as the fiend takes something it is owed: a memory, a year, a color it will never see again.

bestiary.name: Usury Fiend
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Debts in Carnelia are taken seriously, and some debt-collectors are not mortal. A usury fiend is a hulking, grey-skinned devil in a moneylender's coat, wrapped in chains of iron links engraved with debtors' names. It collects for the debt-hells beneath the Accord's courts. It's always polite, and it always collects.
bestiary.where: Debtors' prisons, the Syndicate's counting houses, the debt-hells below the Accord.
bestiary.tactics: It drags debtors to it with chains and Collects. It will accept payment mid-fight. A fair offer actually stops it, though the new terms are never good.
hooks: A usury fiend has come for Sabine Velour's debt, with interest.
The fiend will forgive one debt if the party collects another for it, from a very dangerous debtor.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The seraph has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Witness of Vows
entries.text: The seraph knows every oath sworn within 1 mile of it and whether it is being kept. Creatures can't lie in its presence.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The seraph makes three Oath-Spear attacks.

entries.name: Oath-Spear
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) Radiant damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The vow seraph casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Zone of Truth; 2/Day Each: Dispel Magic, Remove Curse; 1/Day Each: Geas, Heal

entries.name: Release the Bound
entries.text: The seraph ends the Charmed condition on one creature it can see within 60 feet, or breaks one contract made under coercion.

bestiary.name: Vow Seraph
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: When the Accord was founded, its signatories called on the heavens to witness. The heavens sent vow seraphs: six-winged, silver-armored, eyes like scales of balance. They watch over every oath in Carnelia. They are furious about Lady Nocturne, who forces vows from people who can't refuse them.
bestiary.where: The Accord's high chamber, oath-stones, any place a great vow is sworn.
bestiary.tactics: The seraph frees thralls first with Release the Bound, then spears oath-breakers. It will not harm anyone who is being coerced.
hooks: A vow seraph will free every one of Nocturne's thralls, if someone proves the vows were coerced.
The seraph has judged a party member an oath-breaker and wants an explanation.

entries.name: Verdict
entries.text: Once the giant has heard both sides of a dispute, its ruling is magically binding as a Geas (save DC 17) on any party who agreed to arbitration.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The giant makes three Gavel attacks.

entries.name: Gavel
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 10 ft. Hit: 23 (3d10 + 7) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Sentence
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 20, one creature the giant hit this turn. Failure: 9 (2d8) Thunder damage and the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Arbiter Giant
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: The Accord's highest court is presided over by giants: grey-bearded, plate-armored arbiters who have judged disputes between kingdoms for a thousand years. They are fair, ponderous, and absolutely incorruptible. With the Oathwarden dead, the arbiter giants are the last judges anyone trusts.
bestiary.where: The Accord's high court, ancient treaty-stones, the borders between kingdoms.
bestiary.tactics: An arbiter fights only to enforce a verdict or defend its court. It pounds the most dangerous foe and sentences anyone who strikes it.
hooks: The arbiter giants will try Lady Nocturne, if the party can drag her into court.
An arbiter has ruled against the party's patron, and the patron wants the verdict overturned.

lines: Immunities Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned
Languages All languages ever sworn in

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
entries.text: If the Oathwarden fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: The Last Oath
entries.text: The Oathwarden is bound to finish the oath it swore in life. If destroyed before then, it re-forms at the Seal of the Accord in 1d10 days. It can be laid to rest only by fulfilling the oath or by a court of the Accord releasing it.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The Oathwarden uses Vowfire twice.

entries.name: Vowfire
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 18, one creature the Oathwarden can see within 120 feet. Failure: 38 (7d10) Necrotic damage. A creature that has broken an oath sworn under the Accord also has the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The undying oathwarden casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18): At Will: Detect Thoughts, Dispel Magic, Zone of Truth; 2/Day Each: Banishment, Hold Monster; 1/Day Each: Power Word Stun, Wall of Force

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the undying oathwarden can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The undying oathwarden regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Oathbreaker Touch
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (3d8) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Recite the Oath
entries.text: Each creature within 30 feet that can hear the Oathwarden makes a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw. Failure: The Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Undying Oathwarden
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: The Oathwarden of the Accord was murdered at midnight on the Night of Unmasking, the night the seven-night countdown began. Some say it didn't stay dead. This stat block is for the undying Oathwarden: a gaunt, robed figure with the Seal of the Accord burned into its chest and candle-flame eyes, risen to finish the last oath it swore. Whether that oath was to protect Vesperine or to punish it depends on what the party learns.
bestiary.where: The Accord's high chamber, the Seal vault, the climax of the Night 7 storyline.
bestiary.tactics: It hurls Vowfire at oath-breakers, holds monsters, and recites its oath to cow lesser foes. It speaks before it fights and will stand down if shown its oath has been fulfilled.
hooks: The dead Oathwarden has been seen walking the Accord's halls, asking for the party by name.
The Oathwarden's last oath was to destroy whoever broke the Accord, and the evidence points at someone the party loves.
bestiary.imm: Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned

lines: Skills Arcana +18, Deception +18, History +18, Insight +10, Perception +10
Immunities Fire, Poison; Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
entries.text: If the Archivist fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The Archivist has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: The Forfeit Ledger
entries.text: The Archivist's ledger holds every name forfeited under a broken infernal contract. While the ledger is within 1 mile, the Archivist can't be permanently destroyed. Destroying the ledger frees every name in it.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The Archivist makes three Quill Talon attacks.

entries.name: Quill Talon
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +13, reach 15 ft. Hit: 18 (2d10 + 7) Slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Read the Forfeit (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 20, each creature in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the Archivist. Failure: 66 (12d10) Psychic damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn as it hears its own name read from the ledger. Success: Half damage only.

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the forfeit archivist can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The forfeit archivist regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Rend Page
entries.text: The Archivist makes one Quill Talon attack.

entries.name: Amend Contract
entries.text: The Archivist ends one effect on itself, or imposes Disadvantage on the next saving throw of one creature it can see within 60 feet.

entries.name: Foreclose (Costs 2 Uses)
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 20, one creature within 60 feet that has signed any contract. Failure: The creature gains 1 Exhaustion level and can't regain Hit Points until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Forfeit Archivist
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Beneath the Accord's courts are the debt-hells, and at their bottom is the Forfeit Archivist: a vast, many-winged devil of red ink and black vellum, with quills for talons. Every name ever lost to a broken infernal contract is written in its ledger. It is patient, courteous, and old as the first lie. Lady Nocturne Vesh signed with it long ago, which is why her name-ledger works. It is also why she is afraid.
bestiary.where: The deepest debt-hell beneath the Accord; an epic-tier capstone for the Ledger & Oath storyline.
bestiary.tactics: It reads names from the Forfeit to stun the party, then tears through them with Quill Talons. It will negotiate at any point. It loves a bargain more than a victory. Burning the ledger is the only lasting win.
hooks: Lady Nocturne's contract with the Archivist comes due on Night 7, and she would rather the party paid it.
Every forfeited name in Carnelia, including the party's lost friends, is in one book at the bottom of the debt-hells.

bestiaryInfo.title: The Carnelia Bestiary
bestiaryInfo.subtitle: Monsters of Masque, Glamour, Salt, and Oath

collections.name: Masquerade & Mirror
collections.intro: Vesperine never takes its mask off. Behind the opera boxes, gambling salons, and canal-side galleries, the city breeds monsters out of vanity, gossip, perfume, and the silvered glass of a thousand mirrors. Some of them are only rumors in velvet. Others wait in the reflections, patient as debt. Most of these creatures can pass for guests until the music stops.

collections.name: Fair Folk & Glamour
collections.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
collections.intro: Where the trees glow blue and the sky forgets to finish setting, the Fair Folk keep court. Their monsters are guests, servants, hounds, and lovers, and every one of them understands bargains better than you do. Nothing here is simply hostile. Everything here wants something, and most of it will ask nicely first.

collections.name: Bog & Thicket
collections.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
collections.intro: Brambles the size of houses, honey dripping from wasp hives, and warm mud the ogresses call a spa. The Thicketmoor is ridiculous right up to the moment it drowns you. Its monsters are bawdy, territorial, and often lovesick, and the bog itself remembers every broken promise sworn on its banks.

collections.name: Salt & Siren
collections.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
collections.intro: Ships wreck on the Saltgrave cliffs every night, and the sea keeps what it takes. The coast's monsters sing, lure, wreck, and drown, and a few of them only want to be kissed once more before the tide turns. Every sailor here knows the rule: never answer a song you can feel in your teeth.

collections.name: Vine & Blood
collections.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
collections.intro: The Duskvine is beautiful the way a cut is beautiful. Its vineyards climb toward châteaux where the old nobility of House Dusk keep candlelit masquerades, willing donors, and a famous vintage. Not every noble is civilized, not every vine drinks rain, and the cellars run deeper than the maps.

collections.name: Ember & Hoard
collections.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
collections.intro: Steaming hot springs, copper-veined cliffs, rope sky-bridges, and a dragon who hoards love letters. The Emberpeaks are hot-tempered and covetous. Their monsters guard treasure, crave treasure, or simply are treasure that has learned to bite. Some of them are lonely enough to talk first.

collections.name: Ledger & Oath
collections.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
collections.intro: In Carnelia, a kiss is a contract and a promise is a chain. The Accord binds every vow sworn in its lands, and where vows break, things crawl out of the ink. These monsters enforce, collect, devour, and forge oaths. Many of them are perfectly polite. All of them read the fine print.

gaps.detail: The Clue Trail says there are 'ten Keystones' (six city + four side adventures), but eleven clues are marked Keystone: six city ★, Pell (SA1), wedding dream (SA2), Morwenna (SA4), Aurelian's letter (SA5), and Lysander's testimony (Part 2). SA3 offers none; the Lanternwood Clue Trail row is unstarred.
gaps.where: world-guide Part 4 > The Clue Trail; Part 2
gaps.suggestion: Say 'eleven' or demote Lysander's testimony to a supporting clue.
gaps.resolution: Guide now says eleven Keystones.

gaps.detail: The wedding mask is 'made for a bride forty years ago' (Gazetteer) but 'thirty-year-old' (Clue Trail); the wedding was 31 years ago.
gaps.where: Part 3 Gazetteer vs Part 4 Clue Trail
gaps.resolution: Mask is thirty years old everywhere.

gaps.detail: Mother Brine is 'the Syndicate's fence' in Parts 3-4 but 'the Syndicate's boss' in Side Adventure 3; the Syndicate's leadership is never defined.
gaps.suggestion: Decide who runs the Thorn Syndicate.
gaps.resolution: Brine is the true boss; the fence is cover.

gaps.detail: Pipwhistle is 'she', a pixie with dandelion-fluff hair in the guide, but 'he', a 'mossy, button-eyed sprite' in solo Adventure 3 (and the Bestiary Buttonthief lore follows the solo version).
gaps.where: Part 6 vs solo Adventure 3 / Bestiary c2
gaps.resolution: She/pixie in guide, solo book and Bestiary.

gaps.detail: Bestiary 'Herald of the Dusk Court' (CR 16, appears Night 7) vs the guide's Amaranth (CR 6, 'the Fae Duke's Herald'). The Unravelling clock also says 'heralds', plural and antlered, on Night 5.
gaps.suggestion: State whether Amaranth is one of several heralds or the only one.
gaps.resolution: Amaranth CR 6 in Vesperine; Bestiary creature renamed Herald Ascendant of the Dusk Court (CR 16).

gaps.detail: Bestiary Undying Oathwarden lore says an Oathwarden was murdered 'on the eve of Night 7'; the guide's murder is on the Night of Unmasking (before Night 1).
gaps.resolution: Bestiary lore fixed to the Night of Unmasking.

gaps.detail: Bestiary collection 7 refers to a 'Notary Quarter' and the Accord's archive/courts, which the guide's six districts don't include.
gaps.resolution: Notary Quarter added to the Gazetteer.

gaps.detail: 'Smitten' is both Allure stage 3 and Enthrallment stage 1, and the Allure status 'Charmed' shares a name with the 2024 Charmed condition (the 2024 pass added a clarifying note).
Lucan already has Legendary Resistance (1/Day); the 5-player row now raises it to 2/Day.
gaps.resolution: Lucan's LR is 1/Day everywhere; 5-player row adds a Dusk Fledgling.

gaps.detail: Valentin says he hasn't been 'touched without fear in thirty years', but he was Morwenna's consort for a hundred years; the exile date is never given.
Caelum's Deception is +8 in the guide but +4 (L1) / +6 (L2-3) in solo Adventure 3 (deliberate solo scaling, but unstated).
gaps.resolution: Explained in Appendix D and the solo book.

gaps.detail: Sir Fennic is a Gladiator (CR 5) in SA2 but a Scout (CR 1/2) in solo Adventure 3.
gaps.resolution: Wounded Fennic (solo) explained.

gaps.detail: Kray is a Bandit Captain with HP 71 treated as CR 3 in SA3, but a plain Bandit Captain (HP 62 at L3, CR 2) in solo Adventure 4.
gaps.resolution: Solo Kray labeled as a scaled-down variant.

gaps.detail: The solo book picks a gateway with a d6 (6 = the Glass chooses); the guide uses a d8 with two comic misfires (Gretch, Vexirra) that have no solo entry.
gaps.resolution: Guide d8 is for groups; solo d6 with 6 = player picks.

gaps.detail: Solo entries are for levels 1-3, but the campaign is for levels 3-8; no rule says how a level-1 solo hero joins.
gaps.suggestion: Add 'advance to level 3 on arrival' or a milestone rule.
gaps.resolution: Level 1 -> 3 bridge with boons and contacts.

gaps.detail: The Syndicate's Oathwarden candidate is 'a minor noble bought by Mother Brine' and is never named or described.
gaps.resolution: Lord Silvano Quell.

dmguide.title: 1. The solution (DM eyes only)
dmguide.html:
Killer: Madame Thessaly Rook. Madame Thessaly Rook is Lady Isaveth Sable, Aurelian's first wife. Thirty-one years ago Aurel Fenn had the Ledger read her wedding vow ('Everything I am is yours') literally, taking her name, title, inheritance and memory. Six months ago she bought the stolen vow-page and remembered everything. She poisoned him with a swapped mask.

  1. Obtained Widow's Sigh (a moth-orchid toxin inert until it meets bloodrose) from the Moth Court, paying with her dream of her own wedding day.
  2. Knew Seraphine always wears Ezren Vos's bloodrose perfume and that Aurelian would kiss her at midnight; bought a vial of bloodrose herself a month earlier to test it ('Madame R.' / 'Lavender').
  3. Sabotaged the ribbon of Aurelian's festival mask so it would fray; at 11:45 he sent for her to fix it.
  4. At 11:47 slipped through the secret mirror-wall door from the Dressing Gallery and swapped his mask for a poisoned twin; her skirts caught the gallery clock's pendulum (stopping it at 11:47) and her lavender mask-ribbon snagged on the rose trellis.
  5. At midnight Seraphine's bloodrose-scented kiss and breath activated the toxin in the mask lining.
  6. She hid the original, unpoisoned mask (ribbon cut, not frayed) in a Dressing Gallery costume trunk and has not yet retrieved it.

Motive. Revenge and restoration: with the Ledger keeperless, the Accord demands a new Oathwarden of founding blood within seven nights, and she means to prove who she is with the vow-page and reclaim her name, House and fortune. She does not want the city to fall and is frightened by how fast the oaths unravel.

What she wants. At first to steer the PCs toward Celestine; if exposed, their help to be named Oathwarden.

Accusation rule. Any three Keystone clues make a solid accusation (two for a solo hero, four for five players). Accusation is public, before the Opera Council, sealed with the accuser's kiss-oath.

Deep secret. Lady Nocturne Vesh whispered the literal-vow trick to Aurel Fenn; her price was his true name, held in a black-glass jar in the Thornwake. A late reveal that changes nothing about who killed him.

Victim. Lord Aurelian Sable, Oathwarden of Vesperine for thirty years, kissed the diva Seraphine Lark on the Rosewater balcony at midnight on the Night of Unmasking, staggered, clawed at his mask and fell dead by the chaise. His lips and the skin beneath his mask were stained black as Ledger ink. The crowd screamed 'poison kiss.' DM: The stain spread from beneath the mask, not from his lips: Widow's Sigh in the mask lining, activated by Seraphine's bloodrose perfume.

dmguide.title: 3. Suspects
dmguide.html:
Seraphine Lark (The Diva)

  • Claimed alibi: On stage until 11:50, then on the Rosewater balcony with the crowd until the midnight kiss.
  • Looks guilty because: She literally kissed him and he died. Her lips are black.
  • Flirt DC: DC 15 (DC 10 if a PC compliments something other than her beauty)
  • Secret: Syndicate spy on Aurelian for two years; in love with Celestine.
  • Alibi truth: True: forty witnesses.
  • Under pressure: Aurelian was frightened for weeks, got a faceless porcelain mask, murmured 'The masks remember'; at about quarter to midnight she saw Madame Rook's silver braid in the mirror wall fussing with his ribbon.
  • Clues: clue-seraphine-glimpse

Lady Celestine Morrow (The Fiancée)

  • Claimed alibi: Alone on the balcony, enjoying the view.
  • Looks guilty because: Strong motive (a hated marriage), suspicious white crystals in her vanity, a lie in her alibi.
  • Flirt DC: DC 17; Advantage if a PC beats her at something
  • Secret: In love with Seraphine; bought fake oath-breaking salts from Ezren a month ago.
  • Alibi truth: False: in the Morrow box writing (then burning) a love letter to Seraphine.
  • Under pressure: The salts and the burned letter (Mending restores a damning-looking but innocent fragment); she saw Hale take a purse from a masked man in a thorn-green domino at 11:30.
  • Clues: clue-celestine-salts, clue-burned-letter, clue-hale-bribe-sighting

Captain Dorian Hale (The Watchman)

  • Claimed alibi: Walking the perimeter.
  • Looks guilty because: Obstructs the investigation, has a Syndicate purse in his strongbox, ordered the body moved before the PCs arrived.
  • Flirt DC: DC 14
  • Secret: Owes the Syndicate 2,000 ducats; took Varo's bribe to pull guards from the Dressing Gallery corridor 11:30-midnight.
  • Alibi truth: Partly true: he stayed far from the corridor on purpose.
  • Under pressure: The bribe, Varo's name, and that the dressing corridor was empty for half an hour and the mirror wall has a door everyone backstage knows about.
  • Clues: clue-hale-corridor, clue-hale-purse

Ezren Vos (The Perfumer)

  • Claimed alibi: Running the perfume fountain on the ground floor all night.
  • Looks guilty because: He made the bloodrose perfume on Seraphine's lips, knows poisons, and is nervous.
  • Flirt DC: DC 13
  • Secret: Sells illegal, mostly fake oath-breaking salts.
  • Alibi truth: True.
  • Under pressure: Identifies Widow's Sigh (in the mask, not on her lips); his coded ledger shows 'Madame R.' bought bloodrose a month ago.
  • Clues: clue-widows-sigh-id, clue-scent-ledger

Varo Kestrel (The Fixer)

  • Claimed alibi: Dancing. With whom? Everyone.
  • Looks guilty because: Caught on a balcony with the victim's key ring; Syndicate; bribed the Watch.
  • Flirt DC: DC 12
  • Secret: Stole the vow-page six months ago; tonight lifted the Ledger-vault key from Aurelian's coat (he has it on him).
  • Alibi truth: Evasive but harmless.
  • Under pressure: The vow-page story ('Aurel Fenn' and 'Isaveth Sable', sold by Brine to a lady in a grey veil for masks); leads to Mother Brine; trades the vault key for immunity.
  • Clues: clue-varo-vow-page-story, clue-varo-key

Madame Thessaly Rook (The Maskmaker) ★ THE KILLER

  • Claimed alibi: In the Dressing Gallery all evening, fitting masks.
  • Looks guilty because: Very little at first.
  • Flirt DC: She charms the PCs rather than the reverse.
  • Secret: She is Lady Isaveth Sable and murdered her husband.
  • Alibi truth: Technically true: the Dressing Gallery connects to the murder scene through the mirror door; actors say she stepped out around quarter to.
  • Under pressure: Deflects to Celestine; quiet with two+ hard clues; reveals herself when confronted with the vow-page or the empty crypt, then makes the PCs an offer (see endings).
  • Clues: clue-actors-testimony

dmguide.title: 6. The clock, the climax and the endings
dmguide.html:
Night Unravelling Fey escalation
1 Minor oaths fail. Gambling debts erase themselves; card-salon brawls. Hedgefolk mischief rises; Rillo plays at the revels.
2 Love-vows weaken; couples wonder why they married. Hedgefolk mischief continues.
3 Trade contracts fail; bread prices triple; riots in Lanternside. Glimmer appears in the Drowned Market; the Sorrowkiss comforts mourners.
4 Old curses slip free; ghosts walk Cypress Isle. Nocturne's masquerade invitations arrive.
5 Amaranth, the Fae Duke's Herald, appears at dusk with a train of rose-crowned attendants and asks who will pay. Amaranth collects names openly; Caelum seeks the PCs.
6 Masks stick to their wearers' faces. Nocturne's Masquerade in the Thornwake; she tries to enthrall a PC.
7 At midnight the Accord fails unless a new Oathwarden is sworn. Amaranth reads the Book at the Council vote; Nocturne denounces Caelum.

Wrong accusations:

  • Seraphine Lark: Arrested and held in the Tower of Penitence; the Syndicate sends Ilaria Venn to kill her in her cell (Night +1). Saving her makes her a loyal ally.
  • Lady Celestine Morrow: Arrested; House Morrow withdraws its guard; the Unravelling advances one extra step.
  • Captain Dorian Hale: Arrested; the Watch collapses and Lanternside riots (Masked Revelers and Glimmer-Eaters, Bestiary; build with the 2024 XP budget).
  • Varo Kestrel: Arrested; breaks out within a night, leaving a rude note and the vault key.
  • Any: In every case Thessaly sends a mask and a card, 'Well done, darlings', that smells of bloodrose (clue-bloodrose-card).

The Seventh Bell candidates:

  • Madame Thessaly Rook: Rightful heir of founding blood, if her identity is proven.
  • Lady Celestine Morrow: House Morrow is also of founding blood; legal but loveless.
  • Lord Silvano Quell: The Syndicate's puppet: founding blood (perhaps glimmer-forged), owned by Mother Brine through debt and a kiss-oath. Lucan Vey stands instead if he survived and Quell is exposed.
  • a-pc: Anyone freely kissed into office by a founding heir (loophole revealed by the Veiled Sisters: History DC 16 or a gift).

Endings:

  • Ending A: The Unmasking (Justice). Requires: Expose Thessaly before the Council with three or more Keystones. Outcome: The Ledger writes her true name; she is arrested and recognized as Lady Isaveth Sable. Celestine (or another founding heir) is sworn in. Epilogue: Isaveth asks the PCs to visit her in the Tower of Penitence; she has made each a mask.
  • Ending B: The Restored Name (Mercy). Requires: Present the proof as Aurelian's crime; at least two allied Council votes (Countess Dusk, the blackmail archive, or Dame Ottoline). Outcome: Isaveth is sworn in as Oathwarden; she rewrites the Ledger so no kiss-oath can take a person's self, then confesses and accepts exile to the Lanternwood once a successor is trained. Epilogue: 'Isaveth's Day', one maskless day a year.
  • Ending C: The Velvet Throne (Ambition). Requires: Vault key, vow-page and Thessaly's secret; a founding heir freely kisses a PC into office. Outcome: A PC controls every promise in Carnelia; Thessaly pardoned, exposed or sent away; the Syndicate makes offers; the Fae heralds bow. Opens a second campaign. The office binds the PC to Carnelia.
  • Ending D: The Seventh Bell Tolls (Failure). Requires: No Oathwarden sworn by midnight on Night 7. Outcome: Amaranth ascends as the Herald Ascendant of the Dusk Court (Bestiary, CR 16; Deadly: flee or bargain) and the Fae Duke claims the founding bloodlines; Vesperine is drawn halfway into the Feywild, a city of eternal masquerade. A dark new campaign into the Duke's court; Caelum's dance Anchor may pull a PC into the Feywild.

Fey endgame effects:

  • If Nocturne holds the names of three or more Council members, they vote as she commands; the Syndicate's candidate or an enthralled PC becomes Oathwarden, tilting toward Ending D.
  • If the PCs free the names and expose Nocturne, the Duke's claim weakens; Caelum can stand up to his father; PCs gain Advantage on saves against fey on Night 7.
  • If Caelum is befriended and Nocturne exposed, he can renounce the Dusk Court; his marriage loophole becomes a fourth path to saving the city.
  • If Amaranth's loopholes are found, names are struck from the Book one by one.
  • Teodor saved: a Grace Night between Nights 6 and 7 (the Unravelling doesn't advance); price: Ottoline's first name in the Book of Forfeit Names.
  • Aurel Fenn's true name, freed from Nocturne's jar and spoken over the body, makes Speak with Dead confess the vow-theft: it replaces any one Keystone and gives Ending B the force of law.

dmguide.title: 7. NPC dossiers
dmguide.html:
Lysander of the Silvered Glass

lysander · Gateway character; the man in the mirror · faction oathless-glass · at The Rosewater Gallery · players see: Lysander of the Silvered Glass (Gateway character; the man in the mirror)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: Tall and slender, quicksilver-sheened skin, white-silver hair tied with a black ribbon, polished-steel eyes that reflect you. A five-hundred-year-old silver brocade doublet; he chimes faintly like a wineglass when he moves. Courtly, wistful, playful, very lonely. He speaks from any reflective surface.
  • Secret: Oriane Sable's lover and Mirelle's apprentice, bound inside the Oathless Glass by a kiss-sealed promise ('I will watch over your house forever'). He can leave only if someone freely and knowingly agrees to trade places, or when the Glass opens home. He watched the murder from inside the mirror at 11:47, saw Thessaly come through the secret door, and knows by her eyes she is Oriane's blood (Isaveth Sable). Torn between justice and protecting the last of House Sable. Trades his eyewitness testimony (a Keystone clue) for a promise to help free him, or freely at Allure 3 (Smitten).
  • Wants: Freedom from the Glass; A single real touch; The survival of House Sable
  • Tells: Mirrors your posture, accent and phrasing; Says exactly what you most need to hear; Fishes for ambiguous agreement ('Would you let me walk beside you, just once?')
  • Flirt / Allure: Influence: Charisma (Persuasion) DC 15; Advantage for genuine spontaneity
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#appendix-d-lysander (CR 4, 1,100 XP). Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D (Glass-Bound; Show Them Their Face; Mirror Ward).
  • Portraits: default: portraits/lysander.png (player); solo: solo-img/lysander.jpg

Sabine Velour

sabine-velour · Gateway character; owner of The Blue Hour card salon; the last oathless judge · faction oathless-glass · at The Blue Hour · players see: Sabine Velour (Gateway character; owner of The Blue Hour card salon; the last oathless judge)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: A glamorous woman in her mid-fifties: warm brown skin, finger-waved black hair streaked with silver, midnight-blue beaded gown, opera gloves, an unlit jeweled cigarette holder and a Queen of Hearts in her clutch. Voice of smoke and honey; calls everyone 'sugar' or 'kid'. Runs The Blue Hour in the Velvet Quarter and cheats beautifully at cards.
  • Secret: Summoned through the Glass thirty years ago as the last oathless judge, she endorsed young Aurelian Sable as Oathwarden with a kiss (her Anchor, now released by his death) and suspects he stole something to get his name. The Blue Hour is bankrolled by Old Mother Brine and she owes the Thorn Syndicate a fortune. She owns a shard of the Glass (a hand-mirror, 'the Queen's Shard'); the Syndicate wants it because a shard-holder can choose who goes through when the Glass opens. Her deal with Brine: deliver the new oathless judges and steer them to the Syndicate's candidate for her debts and a ticket home. At Allure 3+ she confesses and gives the PCs the shard.
  • Wants: Go home; Absolution for endorsing Aurelian; Escape her Syndicate debt
  • Tells: Asks greedily about your world's songs and slang; Glances at the clock when a deal is due; Never lights her cigarette
  • Flirt / Allure: Influence: Charisma (Persuasion) DC 13; automatic if a PC sings/recites something from the real world
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#appendix-d-sabine (CR 2, 450 XP). Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D (Marked Card, Torch Song, the Queen's Shard).
  • Portraits: default: portraits/sabine-velour.png (player); solo: solo-img/sabine-velour.jpg

Prince Caelum of the Dusk

prince-caelum · Gateway character; the Fae Duke's youngest son · faction dusk-court · at The Lanternwood · players see: Prince Caelum of the Dusk (Gateway character; a fey prince of the Dusk)

  • Aliases: Cael Rosier [guise, gated]
  • Public: Unearthly tall, twilight-violet skin, golden eyes, antlers twined with climbing red roses, rose-red velvet coat stitched with thorns, a briar crown, and an air of private amusement.
  • Secret: The Fae Duke's youngest son, sent to ensure the Accord fails on Night 7. Secretly he wants Vesperine for himself as a fey-touched city of eternal revels, and he has half fallen in love with its mortals. Deeper secret: if a PC becomes Oathwarden and freely marries him, the Accord would make him a citizen, free of his father (Insight DC 18 to sense he is withholding something). Queen Ilysse is his former paramour; Lady Nocturne Vesh is his rival and plans to denounce him to the Duke on Night 7. His 'one dance at the seventh bell' bargain binds a PC to be wherever he is at midnight on Night 7.
  • Wants: Claim Vesperine for himself; Stay in the mortal world; Outmaneuver Nocturne
  • Tells: Never says 'thank you' and deflects it ('Don't thank me, darling, it's bad luck'); Cut flowers open as he enters; Perception DC 15 in candlelight: his shadow has antlers; Flinches from iron coins; pays only in silver and gold; Insight DC 17: speaks only carefully true sentences
  • Reveal triggers: He seals a kiss-bound bargain (roses burst from the air); Nocturne threatens a PC he is fond of; A PC reaches Allure 3 and asks the right question (Insight DC 18); Sunset in the Lanternwood; A cold-iron blade at his throat (Glamour DC 17)
  • True form: Twilight-violet skin, golden eyes, rose-twined antlers and a briar crown; in a mirror he looks at the viewer and puts a finger to his lips.
  • Flirt / Allure: Contested Charisma (Persuasion or Deception) vs his Charisma (Deception) +8
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#appendix-d-caelum (CR 9, 5,000 XP). Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D. Deception +8 is canonical; in the solo book he deliberately plays at +4 (L1) / +6 (L2-3).
  • Portraits: default: portraits/prince-caelum.png (player); human_guise: portraits/human-guise/prince-caelum.png (player); solo: solo-img/prince-caelum.jpg; solo: solo-img/caelum-guise.jpg

Marisol Tidewhisper

marisol-tidewhisper · Gateway character; rebellious siren of the Drowned Choir · faction drowned-choir · at The Saltgrave Coast · players see: Marisol Tidewhisper (Gateway character; rebellious siren of the Drowned Choir)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: A merfolk siren who can take a two-legged shape on land: sea-green scales along cheekbones and collarbones, black hair braided with sea-glass and tiny bells, eyes like moonlit surf, a pearl-and-abalone bodice and sea-silk wraps. Always slightly damp and grinning. Wild, reckless, a laugh like a breaking wave; she flirts by daring.
  • Secret: She gave the Pearl Heart to Captain Kray to break Mother-of-Pearl Nerissa's centuries-old rule; Kray betrayed her and enslaved her sisters. She stole a Glass shard from a shipwreck to recruit outsiders no one in Carnelia could buy, and wants the PCs to hand the Pearl Heart to her rather than Nerissa, making her the new Mother of the Choir. Her betrayal can be exposed (Insight DC 16, or Bel Okafor's testimony).
  • Wants: Free her sisters; Become Mother of the Choir; A crew of champions (and maybe a sweetheart)
  • Tells: Phrases kiss-promises so they sound like nothing; Goes pale beneath her scales when Kray or Nerissa is named
  • Flirt / Allure: Athletics/Acrobatics stunt, then Charisma (Persuasion) DC 14
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#appendix-d-marisol (CR 4, 1,100 XP). Choir Siren with HP 95, Speed 30 ft./Swim 50 ft., no Stolen Voice, Siren's Laugh and Undertow Dare; treat as CR 4.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/marisol-tidewhisper.png (player); spicy_alt: portraits/spicy/marisol-tidewhisper.png (player); solo: solo-img/marisol.jpg

Sir Valentin Dusk

valentin-dusk · Gateway character; exiled vampire consort of House Dusk · faction house-dusk · at Château Dusk · players see: Sir Valentin Dusk (Gateway character; exiled vampire consort of House Dusk)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: Pale as candle wax, tousled raven hair, a beauty mark beneath one heavy-lidded eye, black velvet coat with garnet buttons, ruffled cravat, oxblood gloves. A vampire: in mirrors only his clothes show. Decadent, sardonic, romantic, tired of eternity, and he asks permission for everything.
  • Secret: Countess Morwenna Dusk's consort for a hundred years until her steward Lucan Vey framed him for a murder Lucan committed (the solo book names the victim: Count Aurelio). Morwenna exiled him. He wants Lucan destroyed and Morwenna's forgiveness, and secretly plans to pass through the Oathless Glass to a world without the Accord, where legend says a vampire might walk in sunlight again, with or without the PCs' blessing. He never feeds on anyone who has not enthusiastically agreed.
  • Wants: Destroy Lucan; Morwenna's forgiveness; Walk in sunlight again
  • Tells: Asks permission for everything; Notices your pulse; Invisible in mirrors except for his clothes
  • Flirt / Allure: Charisma (Persuasion) DC 14 (candor), or offering something he hasn't felt in centuries
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#appendix-d-valentin (CR 5, 1,800 XP). Vampire Spawn: Bite only on the willing, Shadow Step, Gentleman's Grip, no reflection.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/valentin-dusk.png (player); spicy_alt: portraits/spicy/valentin-dusk.png (player); solo: solo-img/valentin.jpg

Lord Aurelian Sable

aurelian-sable · The victim; Oathwarden of Vesperine for thirty years · faction house-sable · at The Sable Palazzo · players see: Lord Aurelian Sable (The murdered Oathwarden of Vesperine)

  • Aliases: Aurel Fenn [former-name, dm_only]
  • Public: Age 58, silver at the temples, a dimpled smile, always in midnight-blue velvet. Beloved in public (generous, witty, the best dancer at any ball), feared in private as keeper of every broken promise. Engaged to Lady Celestine Morrow; kept the diva Seraphine Lark as his 'muse'. Died at midnight on the Night of Unmasking after kissing Seraphine, his face stained black as Ledger ink.
  • Secret: Born Aurel Fenn, a penniless apprentice of the Hall of Vows. Thirty-one years ago, coached by Lady Nocturne Vesh (her price: his true name, now in a black-glass name-jar in the Thornwake), he had the Ledger read his bride Isaveth Sable's wedding vow ('Everything I am is yours') literally, taking her name, title, inheritance and memory. He cut the vow-page from the Ledger decades ago. His journal reads 'The masks remember. She cannot. She must not.' His last letter to his lawyer (stolen by Vexirra's kobolds): 'I believe Isaveth has remembered. If I die, look to the woman who makes my face.' Under Speak with Dead he cannot say his birth name.
  • Wants: (Deceased) Keep his stolen identity hidden; Keep the office and the Ledger
  • Stats: bestiary: undying-oathwarden (CR 16, 15,000 XP). Deceased. Rises as an Undying Oathwarden only if his true name escapes Nocturne's jar (Part 7, Loose Threads). Deadly: flee or bargain.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/aurelian-sable.png (player)

Dame Ottoline Graves

dame-ottoline-graves · Opera Council spokesperson; the PCs' employer · faction opera-council · at The Velvet Opera · players see: Dame Ottoline Graves (Opera Council spokesperson; the PCs' employer)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: A tiny, elderly, terrifyingly polite patron in an enormous crimson gown with a jeweled lorgnette. She hands the oathless PCs the Red Ribbon Warrant: entry to any house and the right to question anyone once. Reward: 500 ducats each and a Council favor sealed with a kiss.
  • Secret: She knows exactly what the Oathless Glass does: the Council's charter requires an oathless judge to confirm the next Oathwarden, which is why the PCs get the Warrant. Her beloved grandson Teodor is among the dream-thief sleepers (saving him buys +1 night). She is one possible allied Council vote for Ending B.
  • Wants: Save the city before the seventh bell; Save her grandson Teodor; Keep the Council in control
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Noble (CR 1/8, 25 XP). Lorgnette of Seeing (1/Day: see Invisible creatures and through illusions for 1 minute); Insight +6, Persuasion +5.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/dame-ottoline-graves.png (player)
  • Note: Portrait prompt #9 exists in the guide, but no portrait image was generated.

Seraphine Lark

seraphine-lark · Suspect: the Diva · faction velvet-opera-company · at The Velvet Opera · players see: Seraphine Lark (Suspect: the Diva)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: Human, early 30s, a cascade of copper hair, emerald silk gown, a voice that could melt candle wax, black-stained lips she refuses to wash ('Let them look'). Dramatic, quick-witted, exhausted by her own legend; funny when she forgets to perform. Alibi: on stage until 11:50, then on the balcony with the crowd until the midnight kiss.
  • Secret: She has spied on Aurelian for the Thorn Syndicate for two years (passing on his pillow-talk) and is in love with Lady Celestine Morrow. Her alibi is true (forty witnesses). Under pressure: Aurelian was frightened for weeks, received a faceless porcelain mask and murmured 'The masks remember'; at about quarter to midnight she glimpsed in the mirror wall 'Madame Rook's silver braid, fussing with his ribbon, then gone.' On Night 3 the Syndicate plants a forged 'S.' letter in her dressing room.
  • Wants: Survive the scandal; Protect Celestine; Escape her Syndicate handlers
  • Flirt / Allure: DC 15 (DC 10 if a PC compliments something other than her beauty)
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#appendix-d-seraphine (CR 2, 450 XP). Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D (Aria of Ruin, Showstopper, Star Power).
  • Portraits: default: portraits/seraphine-lark.png (player)

Lady Celestine Morrow

celestine-morrow · Suspect: the Fiancée; heir of House Morrow · faction house-morrow · at House Morrow's palazzo · players see: Lady Celestine Morrow (Suspect: the Fiancée; heir of House Morrow)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: Half-elf, 28, platinum hair in a severe crown braid, ice-blue high-collared gown, a single sapphire at her throat; moves like a duelist. Cold, cutting, brilliant; treats conversation as fencing. Claims she was 'alone on the balcony, enjoying the view.'
  • Secret: In love with Seraphine and desperate to escape her engagement oath; a month ago she bought fake oath-breaking salts from Ezren Vos (the white crystals in her vanity). Her alibi is false: she was in the Morrow family box writing (then burning) a love letter to Seraphine (Mending restores '…we'll be free by the end of the festival, my lark…'). She saw Captain Hale take a fat purse from a masked man in a thorn-green domino at 11:30. House Morrow is of founding blood: she can be sworn in as Oathwarden on Night 7.
  • Wants: Be free of the engagement; Be with Seraphine; Save the city if she must
  • Flirt / Allure: DC 17; Advantage if a PC beats her at cards, words or a duel
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#appendix-d-celestine (CR 3, 700 XP). Knight reflavored as a duelist: AC 16, rapier (Piercing), Parry, Fencer's Footwork.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/celestine-morrow.png (player)

Captain Dorian Hale

dorian-hale · Suspect: the Watchman; captain of the Lantern Watch · faction lantern-watch · at The Tilted House · players see: Captain Dorian Hale (Suspect: the Watchman; captain of the Lantern Watch)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: Human, mid-40s, broad shoulders, a scar along his jaw, Lantern Watch coat with the top buttons undone; smells of pipe smoke and rain. Tired, gruff, decent at heart, dry humor. Claims he was 'walking the perimeter.'
  • Secret: Owes the Thorn Syndicate 2,000 ducats in gambling debts; took Varo Kestrel's bribe to pull his guards from the Dressing Gallery corridor between 11:30 and midnight; quietly ordered the body moved; a Syndicate purse sits in his strongbox. Under pressure: the bribe, Varo's name, and 'The dressing corridor was empty for half an hour… the mirror wall's got a door.' Lost his own house (and horse) at cards.
  • Wants: Pay off his debts; Hide his corruption; Redemption, if someone gives him a chance
  • Flirt / Allure: DC 14 (courage, plain speaking, genuine kindness)
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Warrior Veteran (CR 3, 700 XP). Companion stat block (Part 9).
  • Portraits: default: portraits/dorian-hale.png (player); solo: solo-img/dorian-hale.jpg

Ezren Vos

ezren-vos · Suspect: the Perfumer; owner of Vos Perfumery · faction independent · at Vos Perfumery · players see: Ezren Vos (Suspect: the Perfumer; owner of Vos Perfumery)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: Tiefling, 30s, lavender skin, gold rings on curling horns, a loose silk robe over an embroidered vest; speaks softly and leans in to smell you. Sensual, curious, theatrical, a little amoral, genuinely brilliant. Made the bloodrose perfume Seraphine wears. Alibi: running the perfume fountain on the ground floor all night.
  • Secret: Sells illegal, mostly fake 'oath-breaking salts' (sea salt and crushed pearl). His alibi is true. Under pressure he identifies Widow's Sigh, which is inert until it breathes bloodrose ('It was on his face, inside the mask'), and his scent-coded ledger shows 'Lavender (Madame R.): 1 vial bloodrose' bought a month ago, odd since Thessaly wears only lavender. He can identify a listening mask.
  • Wants: Protect his shop and reputation; Show off his craft
  • Flirt / Allure: DC 13 (play along with his scent-reading)
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Mage (CR 6, 2,300 XP). Companion version scaled down (HP 40, limited spells), Part 9.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/ezren-vos.png (player)

Varo Kestrel

varo-kestrel · Suspect: the Fixer; Thorn Syndicate rogue · faction thorn-syndicate · at The Drowned Market (District 4) · players see: Varo Kestrel (Suspect: the Fixer; Thorn Syndicate rogue)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: Half-elf, late 20s, dark curls, crooked grin, rose-thorn earring, thorn-green domino mask; dresses better than he can afford. Shameless, charming, cheerful even when caught; loyal to friends only. Alibi: 'Dancing.' With whom? 'Everyone.'
  • Secret: Six months ago he stole a page from Aurelian's desk for Syndicate blackmail: the original wedding-vow page ('Aurel Fenn' and 'Isaveth Sable'); Mother Brine sold it to a lady in a grey veil for three masks. Tonight he bribed Hale and lifted Aurelian's Ledger-vault key from his coat; he has it now and will trade it for immunity. His original report sits in Kray's blackmail archive. Can become a recurring rogue companion.
  • Wants: Profit; Immunity; Loyalty to his friends
  • Flirt / Allure: DC 12 (flirt back better)
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Spy (CR 1, 200 XP). Companion: +10 HP and +1 Hit Point Die per hero level above 3; solo book uses Bandit at L1.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/varo-kestrel.png (player); solo: solo-img/varo-kestrel.jpg

Madame Thessaly Rook

thessaly-rook · Suspect: the Maskmaker · faction house-sable · at The Atelier of Madame Rook · players see: Madame Thessaly Rook (Beloved maskmaker of Needle Row)

  • Aliases: Lady Isaveth Sable [true-name, dm_only], the lady in the grey veil [disguise, dm_only], Madame R. [ledger-name, dm_only]
  • Public: Human, about 60, a long silver braid pinned with gold, laugh lines, magnificent dark eyes, fingertips flecked with gold leaf, always a lavender shawl; never wears a mask herself. Warm, wicked, hilarious: everybody's favorite aunt. Lives above her Atelier on Needle Row with three cats named after her ex-lovers. Gives each PC a free, beautiful mask 'for the investigation'. Alibi: in the Dressing Gallery all evening, fitting masks.
  • Secret: THE KILLER. She is Lady Isaveth Sable, Aurelian's first wife, whose identity he stole with a literal reading of her wedding vow thirty-one years ago. Six months ago she bought the stolen vow-page (as 'a lady in a grey veil') and touching it restored her memory. She obtained Widow's Sigh from the Moth Court (paying with her wedding-day dream), bought bloodrose from Ezren (as 'Madame R.'), sabotaged Aurelian's mask ribbon, and at 11:47 came through the mirror-wall door from the Dressing Gallery to swap his mask for a poisoned twin, knocking the clock pendulum and snagging her lavender ribbon. The original mask is hidden in a Dressing Gallery costume trunk; the vow-page is in a hatbox in her Atelier. Her gift masks include a listening mask (Divination aura; Arcana DC 16 or Ezren to identify). Motive: revenge and restoration; she intends to claim the Oathwardenship as founding-blood heir. Deflects toward Celestine; with two or more hard clues grows quiet; with the vow-page or empty crypt she reveals herself: 'My name is Isaveth Sable. He took it from me with a kiss. I took it back the same way.'
  • Wants: Reclaim her name, House and fortune; Be sworn in as Oathwarden; Avoid the city's fall, which frightens her
  • Tells: Deflects to Celestine ('ask her about the salts'); 'Stepped out once, around quarter to' (actors); Answers Zone of Truth questions only literally; A thirty-year habit: made Aurelian's mask every year and never charged him
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#appendix-d-thessaly (CR 3, 700 XP). Full 2024 stat block in Appendix D (Gilded Needles, Mask of Mercy, 'Darling, Please'). She fights to escape, not to kill.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/thessaly-rook.png (player); revealed: portraits/the-lady-of-the-hall.png (gated); solo: solo-img/thessaly-rook.jpg
  • Note: Portrait prompt #8 (Isaveth revealed) has no generated image; thessaly-rook.png is the pre-reveal portrait. Revealed-form portrait (prompt #8): portraits/the-lady-of-the-hall.png (alias file name; gated).

Lady Oriane Sable

lady-oriane-sable · Founder of House Sable (historical, ~500 years ago) · faction house-sable · at Vesperine, the City of Masks · players see: Lady Oriane Sable (Founder of House Sable (historical))

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: The first of House Sable, who did not trust the Accord of Lips and asked the Fae Duke for one more clause.
  • Secret: Author of the Oathless Clause and commissioner of the Oathless Glass; Lysander's lover, to whom he swore 'I will watch over your house forever.' Thessaly/Isaveth has her eyes.
  • Wants: (Historical)
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Noble (CR 1/8, 25 XP). Historical; appears only as a memory in the Glass or the Mirror Gallery.
  • Portraits: none (missing)

Mirelle of the Thousand Faces

mirelle-of-the-thousand-faces · Fey glass-wright of the Fae Duke (historical) · faction dusk-court · at The Dusk Court (palace 'just behind the sunset') · players see: Mirelle of the Thousand Faces (Fey glass-wright of the Fae Duke (historical))

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: A legendary fey artisan said to have made the oldest mirrors of Vesperine.
  • Secret: Built the Oathless Glass for Oriane Sable, its silver quenched in Ledger ink and its frame carved from living rose-thorn. Lysander was her apprentice. Her current whereabouts are never described.
  • Wants: (Unknown)
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Mage (CR 6, 2,300 XP). Fey creature type; jailer of the Thousand-Faced Reflection at the bottom of the Glass.
  • Portraits: none (missing)

The Fae Duke of the Dusk

fae-duke-of-the-dusk · Ruler of the Dusk Court; creditor of the Accord of Lips · faction dusk-court · at The Dusk Court (palace 'just behind the sunset') · players see: The Fae Duke of the Dusk (Ruler of the Dusk Court; creditor of the Accord of Lips)

  • Aliases: none
