  • Secret: A river nymph (green-gold skin, willow-leaf hair, rippling eyes) whose lure is lost time: those who 'rest a moment' wake hours or a year later, and she keeps their shoes. Her pool is on the Bog Causeway. Feuding with Auntie Sallowmere. Dreaming Waters can advance the Unravelling clock.
  • Wants: Amusement; Humiliate Sallowmere
  • Tells: Hems always damp; Frogs sing in the drains when she laughs; A mountain of single shoes in lost-and-found; Hasn't aged in forty years; Insight DC 14: asks every customer for 'just a little something'
  • Reveal triggers: Cold water in her face; Someone mentions Auntie Sallowmere; Caught with a sleeper's shoes; She uses Water Stride to escape (Glamour DC 14)
  • True form: Green-gold skin, willow-leaf hair threaded with water-lilies, rippling eyes; ripples water so reflections are hard to read.
  • Flirt / Allure: Persuasion DC 13 (out-tease her or bring Sallowmere gossip)
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Dryad (CR 1, 200 XP). Water Stride replaces Tree Stride; Fey Charm = at-will Charm Monster (DC 14) +1 Enthrallment; Dreaming Waters.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/ondine-mirewillow.png (gated); human_guise: portraits/human-guise/dina-mire.png (player)

Rillo Fennamint

rillo-fennamint · Tempter; the Piper of the Revels; Moth Court talent scout · faction moth-court · at The Velvet Opera · players see: Master Orrin Mintleaf (Dance master and fiddler of the Opera's after-parties)

  • Aliases: Master Orrin Mintleaf [guise, player]
  • Public: As players first meet him: Master Orrin Mintleaf, the beloved bearded dance master and fiddler who leads the revel-band at every Velvet Opera after-party, always in a wide-brimmed hat and tall, oddly heavy boots.
  • Secret: A satyr (gilded ram's horns, chestnut curls, goat legs) who leads the best dreamers out to the Lanternwood 'for an after-party' and into Ilysse's cocoons. Has a soft spot for the PCs and can be turned into a guide (Advantage on the Dimming path).
  • Wants: Revelry; Please the Moth Court; Secretly: be forgiven
  • Tells: Perception DC 13: boots clip-clop like hooves; Never removes his hat; Avoids iron-studded floors and the Opera's iron railings; His tunes are always your song; Insight DC 14: scans crowds for 'dreamers'
  • Reveal triggers: Loses himself in the dance past midnight; Out-played in a music duel; Dawn while he plays in the Lanternwood; An iron heel stamped on his 'foot' (Glamour DC 14)
  • True form: Gilded ram's horns, chestnut curls and goat legs, dancing even when standing still.
  • Flirt / Allure: Performance DC 14 (dance with abandon or win a music duel)
  • Stats: bestiary: revel-piper (CR 3, 700 XP). Or Satyr (SRD 5.2.1) with HP 45 (10d8) and Revel Pipes.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/rillo-fennamint.png (gated); human_guise: portraits/human-guise/master-orrin-mintleaf.png (player)

Lady Nocturne Vesh

nocturne-vesh · Thorn; Mistress of Glamours; ruler of the Thornwake · faction thornwake · at The Thornwake Ballroom · players see: Madame Noor Vesperelle (Wealthy widow and hostess of the Black Fan salon)

  • Aliases: Madame Noor Vesperelle [guise, player]
  • Public: As players first meet her: Madame Noor Vesperelle, a rich, mysterious widow 'from across the sea' who hosts the Black Fan, the most exclusive masked salon in the Gilded Crescent, in a palazzo where every mirror is draped in black crepe. Invitations are black envelopes sealed with a lip-print.
  • Secret: The Duke's Mistress of Glamours and Caelum's bitterest rival. Harvests true names through enchanted kisses and kiss-bound vows; on Night 7 every name she holds becomes the Duke's and hers to command. Means to enthrall a PC (oathless vows count double) as puppet Oathwarden or weapon against Caelum. Thirty-one years ago she whispered the literal-vow trick to Aurel Fenn for his true name, kept in a black-glass jar in the Thornwake Name-Jar Cellar. Plans to denounce Caelum on Night 7. Cannot be charmed.
  • Wants: Collect Vesperine's names for the Duke; Destroy Caelum; Enthrall an oathless PC
  • Tells: Never near an uncovered mirror (Insight DC 14 to find the 'custom' suspicious); Long gloves; silver cutlery, never iron; Guests can't describe her face (Int DC 13 fails at Enthrallment 1+); Dead rose petals where she sat; Insight DC 18: her smile arrives before her eyes
  • Reveal triggers: A draped mirror uncovered, or the Glass/a shard turned on her; Cold iron touches her skin; Laughed at publicly and sincerely (Performance DC 18); A PC reaches Enthrallment 4 with her; Midnight at her Night 6 masquerade (Glamour DC 18)
  • True form: Bone-white skin, black lips, starless eyes, black hair woven with dead roses, a dark sapphire choker pulsing with a stolen name.
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#nocturne-stat-block (CR 11, 7,200 XP). Full 2024 stat block in Part 6 (8,400 XP in lair).
  • Portraits: default: portraits/nocturne-vesh.png (gated); human_guise: portraits/human-guise/madame-noor-vesperelle.png (player); spicy_alt: portraits/spicy/nocturne-vesh.png (gated)

Sir Merrow Ashgrave, the Sorrowkiss

merrow-ashgrave · Thorn; the Glimmer Knight; Thornwake enforcer · faction thornwake · at Lanternside (District 6) · players see: Brother Ash (Mourning friar who sits with the grieving)

  • Aliases: Brother Ash [guise, player], the Sorrowkiss [epithet, dm_only]
  • Public: As players first meet him: Brother Ash, a tall, grey-robed mourning friar of no order anyone can name, who sits with the grieving at Lanternside wakes and Cypress Isle funerals.
  • Secret: A sorrowful fey knight in black thorned plate inlaid with silver moths who hooks Vesperine on glimmer (fey dust refined from Moth Court dream-powder, sold through the Syndicate). Glimmer-addicts can't resist Nocturne. Sorrow's Mercy: won't attack anyone weeping or grieving openly; open grief and honesty (Persuasion DC 17) can make him lay down his sword. Buys Caelum's rose for Nocturne in solo Adventure 3.
  • Wants: Spread 'mercy' (glimmer); Serve Nocturne
  • Tells: Silver dust on his lips and on mourners' hands; Grey petals drift from his hem; Never eats or drinks at a wake; Won't carry a coffin; avoids iron nails; Insight DC 16: his grief is centuries old
  • Reveal triggers: Someone refuses his comfort and names his trade; His glimmer trade is threatened; Someone grieves openly and honestly before him; Cold iron or a coffin nail in his palm (Glamour DC 16)
  • True form: A knight in black thorned plate inlaid with silver moths, helm under his arm, tears on a pale face.
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#merrow-stat-block (CR 7, 2,900 XP). Full 2024 stat block in Part 6.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/merrow-ashgrave.png (gated); human_guise: portraits/human-guise/brother-ash.png (player); solo: solo-img/brother-ash.jpg

Amaranth, the Smiling Herald

amaranth · Thorn; Herald of the Dusk Court · faction dusk-court · at Notary Amar Thorne's office · players see: Notary Amar Thorne (Contract notary on the bridge to the Hall of Vows)

  • Aliases: Notary Amar Thorne [guise, player], The Fae Duke's Herald [title, player]
  • Public: As players first meet them: Notary Amar Thorne, a meticulous, soft-spoken contract notary with a tiny office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows, who never lies, not even politely.
  • Secret: The Fae Duke's herald, tallying what Vesperine owes in the red Book of Forfeit Names. From Night 5 collects names openly; on Night 7 reads the Book aloud at the Council vote. Bound by the rules: cannot lie, cannot take an unwilling name, must honor any loophole (each of six Dusk Court debts has one; DC 17 Investigation). This is the 'Fae Duke's Herald' of the Unravelling clock and portrait prompt #32 (#20 is the Herald Ascendant). Round 2: Amaranth is the CR 6 herald in mortal Vesperine; inside the Thornwake, or at midnight on Night 7 if the Accord fails, they become the Herald Ascendant of the Dusk Court (Bestiary, CR 16).
  • Wants: Collect the debt correctly; Professional delight in a good loophole
  • Tells: Never lies; Ink blooms into tiny roses as it dries; Refuses iron paperweights; Perception DC 14 in lamplight: antlered shadow; Smells of roses and old paper
  • Reveal triggers: Dusk on Night 5; A PC signs anything Amaranth notarized; Someone finds a genuine loophole; Offered bread and salt as a guest (Glamour DC 16)
  • True form: An antlered herald in a dusk-colored coat, holding the vast red Book of Forfeit Names, still smiling.
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#amaranth-stat-block (CR 6, 2,300 XP). Full 2024 stat block in Part 6.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/amaranth.png (gated); human_guise: portraits/human-guise/notary-amar-thorne.png (player)

Gristle Pike

gristle-pike · Mother Brine's collector (solo only) · faction thorn-syndicate · at The Drowned Market (District 4) · players see: Gristle Pike (Mother Brine's collector (solo only))

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: A huge man with a hook for a hand and a voice like gravel.
  • Secret: Collects for Mother Brine; tonight he comes for Sabine's oathless guest and her mirror ('both or neither').
  • Wants: Collect
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Bandit Captain (CR 2, 450 XP). Campaign: Bandit Captain. Solo book (L1-3): a Tough with 40 HP at every level.
  • Portraits: none (missing)

Anka

anka · Lucan's compelled maid (solo only) · faction house-dusk · at Château Dusk · players see: Anka (Maid at Château Dusk)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: A twenty-three-year-old maid at Château Dusk with puncture marks on her wrist and a glassy look: a thrall of Lucan's.
  • Secret: Knows villagers are taken 'downstairs' and that Lucan's study has the red seal. If freed from compulsion she smuggles the PCs a servants' key in Side Adventure 4.
  • Wants: Be free
  • Stats: bestiary: thrall-servant (CR 1/8, 25 XP). Implied; non-combatant.
  • Portraits: none (missing)

Count Aurelio

count-aurelio · Murder victim Valentin was framed for (solo only) · faction house-dusk · at Château Dusk · players see: Count Aurelio (A count of the Duskvine (deceased))

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: A count whose death Valentin was blamed for.
  • Secret: Lucan killed him and framed Valentin ('The consort will hang for Count Aurelio's death as planned'). Not mentioned in the world guide.
  • Wants: (Deceased)
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Noble (CR 1/8, 25 XP). Flashbacks only (deceased).
  • Portraits: none (missing)

Lord Silvano Quell

silvano-quell · The Thorn Syndicate's puppet candidate for Oathwarden · faction opera-council · at The Gilded Crescent (District 1) · players see: Lord Silvano Quell (Poet-heir of House Quell; candidate for Oathwarden)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: The beautiful, languid last scion of House Quell, a founding house gone to seed. Writes poetry, faints elegantly, and owes everyone money.
  • Secret: Owes the Syndicate 11,000 ducats and has sworn Mother Brine a kiss-oath to 'stand when called'. Founding blood makes him a legal candidate. His proof of descent may be glimmer-forged. If sworn, Brine rules the Ledger through him.
  • Wants: Get out of debt; Be loved for his poems; Not be murdered
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Noble (CR 1/8, 25 XP). Performance +4 (poetry).
  • Portraits: default: portraits/silvano-quell.png (player)

Lord Orsino Varga

orsino-varga · Opera Council: shipping magnate · faction opera-council · at Lanternside (District 6) · players see: Lord Orsino Varga (Opera Council: shipping magnate)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: A broad, grey-bearded shipping magnate whose ships carry half of Lanternside's trade.
  • Secret: Syndicate-leaning; his vote can be swung by Kray's blackmail archive. One of the three Council names in Nocturne's jars.
  • Wants: Profit; Keep his secrets
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Noble (CR 1/8, 25 XP). Intimidation +4.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/lord-orsino-varga.png (player)

Madame Liliane Corvaux

liliane-corvaux · Opera Council: impresaria of the Velvet Opera · faction opera-council · at The Velvet Opera · players see: Madame Liliane Corvaux (Opera Council: impresaria of the Velvet Opera)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: The Opera's glamorous impresaria; a sleek black bob with a white streak and a jeweled cane.
  • Secret: She hired Pell Ambrose to build the mirror door. Her vote is won by a performance worthy of her stage (Performance DC 16).
  • Wants: The Opera's survival; A great performance
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Noble (CR 1/8, 25 XP). Performance +6.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/madame-liliane-corvaux.png (player)

Archivist-Mother Severine

archivist-mother-severine · Opera Council: abbess of the Veiled Sisters · faction veiled-sisters · at The Hall of Vows (District 5) · players see: Archivist-Mother Severine (Opera Council: abbess of the Veiled Sisters)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: The serene abbess of the Veiled Sisters, keeper of the Ledger's rites.
  • Secret: Votes for whichever candidate's founding blood is proven before the Ledger. Source of the 'freely kissed into office' loophole.
  • Wants: The Ledger's integrity
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Priest (CR 2, 450 XP). Never attacks inside the Hall of Vows.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/archivist-mother-severine.png (player)

Lord Tancredi Morrow

tancredi-morrow · Opera Council: Celestine's uncle · faction house-morrow · at House Morrow's palazzo · players see: Lord Tancredi Morrow (Opera Council: Celestine's uncle)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: A silver-haired half-elf lord with a duelist's bearing and a black rose on his lapel.
  • Secret: His name is in one of Nocturne's jars (Enthrallment 3): he votes as she commands until it is freed.
  • Wants: House Morrow's honor
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Knight (CR 3, 700 XP). Enthrallment 3; cold iron makes him weep.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/lord-tancredi-morrow.png (player)

Dowager Ysolde Vane

ysolde-vane · Opera Council: card-mad dowager · faction opera-council · at The Velvet Quarter (District 2) · players see: Dowager Ysolde Vane (Opera Council: card-mad dowager)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: A sharp-eyed, powdered dowager who never leaves a card table and cheats with style.
  • Secret: Allegra Vane's mother. Hers was the first name Amaranth wrote in the Book of Forfeit Names; strike it and she is yours. One of Nocturne's three.
  • Wants: Win; Get her name back
  • Stats: srd-5.2.1: Noble (CR 1/8, 25 XP). Sleight of Hand +5.
  • Portraits: default: portraits/dowager-ysolde-vane.png (player)

Ilaria Venn, "the Last Kiss"

ilaria-venn · The Syndicate's assassin (Night 3) · faction thorn-syndicate · at The Drowned Market (District 4) · players see: Nell Daisy (Flower-seller at the Opera doors)

  • Aliases: Nell Daisy [guise, player], the Last Kiss [epithet, dm_only]
  • Public: A sunny flower-seller with a basket of bloodroses who sells boutonnieres at the Opera doors.
  • Secret: Ilaria Venn, the most expensive Velvet Garrote in the Marches, hired by Mother Brine on Night 3 to kill the PCs (or Seraphine in the Tower of Penitence). Flirts targets onto balconies. Wants out of the Syndicate; a seat in the Glass would buy her.
  • Wants: Get paid; Get out
  • Tells: Insight DC 15: a false note in her laugh; Her reflection isn't smiling (Glass-Marked PCs); A painted beauty mark in a different place every night
  • Reveal triggers: She strikes on Night 3; A PC exposes her cover aloud in a crowd; She is caught with the garrote choker
  • Stats: custom: world-guide#appendix-d-ilaria (CR 5, 1,800 XP). Velvet Garrote (Bestiary) with the Nell Daisy trait and Bloodrose Calling Card reaction.
  • Portraits: guise: portraits/the-flower-seller.png (player)

Sergeant Bettina Crane

bettina-crane · Warden of the Tower of Penitence · faction lantern-watch · at The Tower of Penitence · players see: Sergeant Bettina Crane (Warden of the Tower of Penitence)

  • Aliases: none
  • Public: The honest, outnumbered sergeant who keeps the city's prison tower.
  • Secret: Won't take Syndicate money; will help the PCs protect a prisoner if they help her hold the stair.
  • Wants: Keep her prisoners alive
  • Stats: bestiary: lantern-watch-sergeant (CR 3, 700 XP)
  • Portraits: none (missing)

dmguide.title: 8. Locations
dmguide.html:
Carnelia

carnelia · world · in None · player

  • Public: A sun-drenched, wine-dark land of canals, vineyards and old magic, ruled less by kings than by contracts. Five hundred years ago Vesperine's founders struck the Accord of Lips with the Fae Duke of the Dusk: any promise sealed with a kiss is magically binding and recorded in the Ledger of Vows. A forced or stolen kiss creates no oath.
  • DM: The Accord fails at midnight on Night 7 unless a new Oathwarden is sworn.

Vesperine, the City of Masks

vesperine · city · in carnelia · player

  • Public: Built on a hundred islands knit by bridges, gondola lanes and gossip; colored-glass lanterns over every canal. Masks are legal and fashionable at all hours. ~60,000 people. Ruled in practice by the Opera Council; policed by the Lantern Watch; currency gold ducats and silver kisses. Notable vices: masquerades, card salons, Vinehold wine, dream-moth dust, duelling for love.
  • DM: Hub of the central mystery. See the Unravelling clock (Part 4) for what changes each night.
  • NPCs: Dame Ottoline Graves, Pim Gallowglass, Lady Oriane Sable
  • Map: map-vesperine-districts

The Velvet Marches

velvet-marches · region · in carnelia · player

  • Public: The countryside Vesperine depends on and pretends not to need: Thicketmoor, Lanternwood, Saltgrave Coast, Duskvine Valley, Emberpeaks.
  • DM: Each region hosts one side adventure (one night on the clock each).
  • Map: map-velvet-marches

The Thicketmoor

thicketmoor · region · in velvet-marches · player

  • Public: Brambles the size of houses, golden honey dripping from wasp hives, and warm mud pits ogres consider a spa. Travellers vanish. Mostly men. Mostly loudly.
  • DM: Home of the Honeyhorn Clan; Side Adventure 1. Pell Ambrose is held here.
  • NPCs: Big Mother Hulga Tenderbone, Brunhilde "Bru", Little Gretch, Granny Moss, Auntie Sallowmere

The Lanternwood

lanternwood · region · in velvet-marches · player

  • Public: A forest where the trees give off soft blue light and moths the size of cats drift between them. Sleepers who wander here wake days later, smiling, with no memory of their dreams.
  • DM: Seat of the Moth Court (Side Adventure 2); the Dusk Court is reachable through it at twilight. Caelum's gateway landing point. Source of the moth-orchid used for Widow's Sigh.
  • NPCs: Queen Ilysse of the Hush, Prince Caelum of the Dusk
  • Clues: clue-ilysse-testimony

The Saltgrave Coast

saltgrave-coast · region · in velvet-marches · player

  • Public: Black cliffs, shipwrecks, and singing at night that every sailor pretends not to hear. Smugglers bring Syndicate cargo through the sea caves.
  • DM: Home of the Drowned Choir and Kray's Smugglers' Grotto (Side Adventure 3). Marisol's gateway landing point.
  • NPCs: Mother-of-Pearl Nerissa, Marisol Tidewhisper, Quill-Fin

The Duskvine Valley

duskvine-valley · region · in velvet-marches · player

  • Public: The most beautiful countryside in Carnelia: golden terraces, poplars, villages where everyone is a little too pale and very well-rested. Château Dusk crowns the hill.
  • DM: Side Adventure 4: Lucan Vey's abductions.
  • NPCs: Countess Morwenna Dusk, Marta Ilic

The Emberpeaks

emberpeaks · region · in velvet-marches · player

  • Public: Steaming hot springs, copper-veined cliffs and rope sky-bridges. Miners leave love poems at shrine-stones to keep the dragon in a good mood.
  • DM: Vexirra's lair (Side Adventure 5); Copperhand Miners' Guild.
  • NPCs: Vexirra, Forewoman Brannagh Copperhand

The Dusk Court (palace 'just behind the sunset')

dusk-court · feywild-site · in None · dm_only

  • Public: Fairy-tale talk of a palace 'just behind the sunset'.
  • DM: Reachable through the Lanternwood at twilight. If the Accord fails (Ending D) the way home runs through this court. Never mapped or described in detail.
  • NPCs: The Fae Duke of the Dusk, Mirelle of the Thousand Faces

The Gilded Crescent (District 1)

gilded-crescent · district · in vesperine · player

  • Public: Noble palazzos facing the Grand Canal; balconies built for eavesdropping. Home of House Morrow and the shuttered Sable Palazzo.
  • DM: Also hosts the Black Fan salon.
  • NPCs: Lady Celestine Morrow

The Velvet Quarter (District 2)

velvet-quarter · district · in vesperine · player

  • Public: Theaters, salons, pleasure-gardens and the Velvet Opera, a cathedral of red plush and gold leaf.
  • DM: Also The Blue Hour and the Hush House.
  • NPCs: Allegra Vane

Needle Row (District 3)

needle-row · district · in vesperine · player

  • Public: Artisans' lanes: tailors, wigmakers, perfumers, and the Atelier of Madame Rook.
  • DM: Also Vos Perfumery and The Gilded Thimble.

The Drowned Market (District 4)

drowned-market · district · in vesperine · player

  • Public: A half-sunken flea market under the old city: ankle-deep water, floating lanterns, stalls on stilts. Reached by the stairs at Gull Steps.
  • DM: The Thorn Syndicate sells anything here, including secrets, debts and (from Night 3) glimmer.
  • NPCs: Varo Kestrel, Old Mother Brine, Gristle Pike
  • Clues: clue-varo-vow-page-story, clue-varo-key

The Hall of Vows (District 5)

hall-of-vows · district · in vesperine · player

  • Public: A white-marble temple-library on its own island: silence and the sound of a pen that writes by itself. The Ledger of Vows rests on a lectern of living rose-thorn, tended by the Veiled Sisters. Since the murder the ink bleeds and pages blank out.
  • DM: Above the Vault of Broken Vows. The Sisters can annul forged vows and reveal the succession loophole.
  • NPCs: The Veiled Sisters, Sister Corvina
  • Map: map-hall-of-vows
  • Painted player view: maps/hall-of-vows-painted.jpg (player)

Lanternside (District 6)

lanternside · district · in vesperine · player

  • Public: Docks, taverns, sailors, and the Lantern Watch's leaning headquarters, the Tilted House.
  • DM: Riots on Night 3; Brother Ash (Merrow) comforts mourners at wakes here. Isaveth woke on these docks with no name 31 years ago.
  • NPCs: Sir Merrow Ashgrave, the Sorrowkiss

Cypress Isle

cypress-isle · district · in vesperine · player

  • Public: The cemetery island.
  • DM: Ghosts walk here from Night 4. The Sable Crypt and, beneath it, the Thornwake.

The Velvet Opera

velvet-opera · site · in velvet-quarter · player

  • Public: A gold-and-crimson temple to spectacle: five tiers of private boxes, each with its own little curtain for 'private conversations'. Backstage is a maze of rope, sandbags and costume racks. Feel: perfumed heat, applause, whispers behind fans.
  • DM: Venue of the murder and of the Night 7 Council vote.
  • NPCs: Dame Ottoline Graves, Seraphine Lark, Rillo Fennamint, Benedetto Fiore, Pell Ambrose
  • Clues: clue-seraphine-glimpse, clue-hale-bribe-sighting, clue-corpse-answers, clue-forged-s-letter

The Rosewater Gallery

rosewater-gallery · site · in velvet-opera · player

  • Public: A long salon above the stage lined with mirrors and rose-trellises around a fountain of scented rosewater. Its tall clock, the city's most famous timepiece, stopped at 11:47 on the night of the murder. The mirror wall's great central pane is very old and very flattering.
  • DM: The murder scene. A secret door behind the mirror wall connects to the Dressing Gallery. The central pane is the Oathless Glass. Clues: stopped clock (Riddle 6, Keystone), lavender ribbon on the trellis, stain darkest under the mask.
  • NPCs: Lysander of the Silvered Glass
  • Clues: clue-clock-1147, clue-lavender-ribbon, clue-stain-pattern, clue-lysander-testimony, clue-dream-moth-dust
  • Map: map-velvet-opera-second-tier
  • Painted player view: maps/velvet-opera-second-tier-painted.jpg (player)

The Dressing Gallery

dressing-gallery · site · in velvet-opera · player

  • Public: Racks of costumes, wig-stands, and Madame Rook's fitting table covered in feathers and gold leaf.
  • DM: Connected to the Rosewater Gallery by the mirror-wall door. The original unpoisoned mask (ribbon cut, not frayed) is hidden in a costume trunk (Keystone); actors say Thessaly stepped out around quarter to midnight. Hale's guards were pulled from its corridor 11:30-midnight.
  • NPCs: Madame Thessaly Rook
  • Clues: clue-original-mask, clue-actors-testimony
  • Map: map-velvet-opera-second-tier
  • Painted player view: maps/velvet-opera-second-tier-painted.jpg (player)

The Sable Palazzo

sable-palazzo · site · in gilded-crescent · player

  • Public: Aurelian's home in the Gilded Crescent: elegant, cold, too big, now shuttered.
  • DM: Study with a riddle-locked writing desk (Riddle 1: journal and the faceless porcelain mask); a portrait gallery with a painted-over young bride with Thessaly's eyes; a hidden cache with his private journal in the bedchamber.
  • NPCs: Lord Aurelian Sable
  • Clues: clue-aurelian-journal, clue-faceless-mask, clue-painted-portrait
  • Map: map-sable-palazzo
  • Painted player view: maps/sable-palazzo-painted.jpg (player)

House Morrow's palazzo

house-morrow-palazzo · site · in gilded-crescent · player

  • Public: The Gilded Crescent seat of House Morrow, a founding family.
  • DM: Celestine's vanity holds the fake oath-breaking salts; her grate holds the burned love letter. Never described in detail.
  • NPCs: Lady Celestine Morrow
  • Clues: clue-celestine-salts, clue-burned-letter

The Atelier of Madame Rook

atelier-of-madame-rook · site · in needle-row · player

  • Public: A cozy shop overflowing with masks: feathered, porcelain, lacquered, beaded. Thessaly lives above it with three cats named after her ex-lovers.
  • DM: Back workroom: glue pots, gold leaf, and a hatbox holding a wedding mask and the vow-page itself wrapped in lavender silk (Keystone); a pressed moth-orchid in a book of poems. Search: Investigation DC 16 or Stealth DC 15 to search unseen.
  • NPCs: Madame Thessaly Rook
  • Clues: clue-wedding-mask, clue-vow-page, clue-moth-orchid, clue-bloodrose-card
  • Map: map-atelier-of-madame-rook
  • Painted player view: maps/atelier-of-madame-rook-painted.jpg (player)
  • Note: Gazetteer says the wedding mask was made 'forty years ago'; the Clue Trail calls it 'thirty-year-old'; the wedding was 31 years ago.

Vos Perfumery

vos-perfumery · site · in needle-row · player

  • Public: Glass bottles in every color, a copper still, and a tiefling who can identify anyone by scent.
  • DM: Ezren's scent-coded order ledger (Riddle 3): 'Lavender: 1 vial bloodrose' (Keystone); salts order for 'Lady C.M.' (red herring).
  • NPCs: Ezren Vos
  • Clues: clue-widows-sigh-id, clue-scent-ledger, clue-salts-order

The Vault of Broken Vows

vault-of-broken-vows · site · in hall-of-vows · player

  • Public: Below the Hall of Vows; stores torn-out, annulled pages.
  • DM: Door riddle (Riddle 2) plus Varo's key or Thieves' Tools DC 18. Missing page stub dated 31 years ago: '…Aurel Fenn and Isaveth Sable, everything I am…'.
  • Clues: clue-missing-page-stub, clue-sisters-vow-page-rule
  • Map: map-hall-of-vows
  • Painted player view: maps/hall-of-vows-painted.jpg (player)

Things That Shouldn't Be Sold (Mother Brine's shop)

things-that-shouldnt-be-sold · site · in drowned-market · player

  • Public: A stall-shop in the Drowned Market; you are asked a password through a slot in the door.
  • DM: Password Riddle 5. Brine's sale record of the vow-page and one of the three masks, signed with Thessaly's maker's mark (Keystone).
  • NPCs: Old Mother Brine
  • Clues: clue-brine-sale-record, clue-signed-mask

Gull Steps

gull-steps · site · in lanternside · player

  • Public: The stairs down into the Drowned Market.

The Tilted House

tilted-house · site · in lanternside · player

  • Public: Lantern Watch headquarters, leaning so badly that pens roll off desks.
  • DM: Captain Hale's office has a locked strongbox containing a Syndicate purse.
  • NPCs: Captain Dorian Hale
  • Clues: clue-hale-purse, clue-hale-corridor

The Sable Crypt

sable-crypt · site · in cypress-isle · player

  • Public: The Sable family tomb on Cypress Isle: cold marble, wilted lilies, a line of old family sarcophagi.
  • DM: Includes a marble sarcophagus inscribed 'Lady Isaveth Sable, Beloved Wife, Lost to the Sea' (the name is a spoiler term, so it stays out of players.md until found). The sarcophagus is empty except for a lavender silk wedding veil (Keystone). Riddle 4 on the lid. Ghosts (Night 4+) whisper 'she lives, she sews, she smiles'. A stair of black roses beneath leads to the Thornwake.
  • Clues: clue-empty-tomb, clue-ghost-whispers

The Thornwake Ballroom

thornwake-ballroom · dungeon · in sable-crypt · dm_only

  • DM: A sunken ballroom forgotten three centuries ago, beneath the Sable Crypt: Rose Stair, Hall of Partners, Mirror Gallery, Glimmer Vats, Name-Jar Cellar (Aurel Fenn's name), Black Throne. Nocturne holds court here Nights 5-7.
  • NPCs: Lady Nocturne Vesh, Sir Merrow Ashgrave, the Sorrowkiss
  • Map: map-thornwake-ballroom
  • Painted player view: maps/thornwake-ballroom-painted.jpg (dm_only)

The Blue Hour

blue-hour · site · in velvet-quarter · player

  • Public: Sabine Velour's card salon: blue light, smoke, a grand piano, velvet booths and a gilded mirror in the back room.
  • DM: Bankrolled by Old Mother Brine. Sabine's gateway landing point. Cael Rosier (Caelum) gambles here.
  • NPCs: Sabine Velour, Prince Caelum of the Dusk

The Black Fan

black-fan · site · in gilded-crescent · player

  • Public: The most exclusive masked salon in the Gilded Crescent, hosted by the widow Madame Noor Vesperelle in a candlelit palazzo where every mirror is draped in black crepe.
  • DM: Nocturne Vesh's human-guise salon.
  • NPCs: Lady Nocturne Vesh

The Lilywater Baths

lilywater-baths · site · in lanternside · player

  • Public: The city's cheapest and most popular bathhouse; patrons who doze in the warm pools sometimes wake much later than they meant to.
  • DM: Ondine's guise workplace (Dina Mire); a mountain of single shoes in the lost-and-found.
  • NPCs: Ondine Mirewillow

The Gilded Thimble

gilded-thimble · site · in needle-row · player

  • Public: A cozy tavern on Needle Row with pewter mugs and iron tankards on the top shelf.
  • DM: Pipwhistle's guise workplace (Pip Dewley).
  • NPCs: Pipwhistle Dewlace

The Hush House

hush-house · site · in velvet-quarter · player

  • Public: A dream-reader's parlor opened this season, selling little blue bottles of sleep-tonic.
  • DM: Queen Ilysse's guise (Madame Ilse Hush); some clients don't wake for days.
  • NPCs: Queen Ilysse of the Hush

Notary Amar Thorne's office

notary-office-amar-thorne · site · in notary-quarter · player

  • Public: A tiny notary's office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows; ink here dries into tiny roses.
  • DM: Amaranth's guise office.
  • NPCs: Amaranth, the Smiling Herald

The Tower of Penitence

tower-of-penitence · site · in vesperine · player

  • Public: Vesperine's prison: a narrow white tower on a rock in the lagoon, reached only by a Watch barge, where the condemned make lace, masks, and confessions.
  • DM: Where the city puts anyone the PCs accuse; Ilaria's cell assassination of Seraphine (Night +1); Isaveth's cell in Ending A; seed 'Visiting Hours'.
  • NPCs: Sergeant Bettina Crane

The Bog Causeway

bog-causeway · route · in thicketmoor · player

  • Public: The causeway road from Vesperine into the Thicketmoor, where men have been vanishing.
  • DM: Ondine's pool lies along it. Honeyhorn matrons raid it if the clan is wronged.
  • NPCs: Ondine Mirewillow

The Hive-Hall of Honeyhorn

hive-hall-of-honeyhorn · dungeon · in thicketmoor · player

  • Public: The Honeyhorn den, with famous mud wallows.
  • DM: Eight areas: Bramble Gate, Wallows, Pampering Pen, Kitchen of the Disappointment Pot, Moot Ring, Hulga's Bower, Sulking Stones, Sallowmere's Hut.
  • NPCs: Big Mother Hulga Tenderbone, Brunhilde "Bru", Little Gretch, Granny Moss, Pell Ambrose, Rufus, Watchman Dobbs, Watchman Pirelli, Lorcan the Poet
  • Clues: clue-pell-testimony
  • Map: map-hive-hall-keyed
  • Painted player view: maps/hive-hall-of-honeyhorn-painted.jpg (player)

The Sulking Stones

sulking-stones · site · in hive-hall-of-honeyhorn · player

  • Public: Six grey standing stones in a circle, each vaguely ogre-shaped and scowling, arms crossed.
  • DM: The petrified ogre husbands; riddle on the center stone.
  • NPCs: Grunwald

Sallowmere's Hut

sallowmere-hut · site · in hive-hall-of-honeyhorn · dm_only

  • DM: A chicken-legged hut half-sunk in mud beneath the bog, reached through a sinkhole in the kitchen (DC 15 Perception to notice the draft).
  • NPCs: Auntie Sallowmere

The Cocoon Palace

cocoon-palace · dungeon · in lanternwood · player

  • Public: A towering tree of pale silk glowing like a paper lantern; court of the Moth Queen.
  • DM: Avenue of Lights, Dust Fields, Hall of Wings, Mirror Pool, Silk Library (wedding-dream Keystone, Teodor), Hush Throne.
  • NPCs: Queen Ilysse of the Hush, Sir Fennic Ashwing, The Dust-Maidens, Teodor Graves
  • Clues: clue-wedding-dream, clue-ilysse-testimony

The Smugglers' Grotto

smugglers-grotto · dungeon · in saltgrave-coast · player

  • Public: Sea caves on the Saltgrave cliffs where smugglers land Syndicate cargo.
  • DM: Wrecker's Beacon, Tidepool Stair (tide timer), Syndicate Warehouse, Drowned Chapel (song-lock), Choir Lagoon, Kray's Strongroom (Pearl Heart, blackmail archive).
  • NPCs: Captain Morven "Saltlick" Kray, Bel Okafor, Mother-of-Pearl Nerissa
  • Clues: clue-varo-report, clue-hale-debts

Château Dusk

chateau-dusk · dungeon · in duskvine-valley · player

  • Public: The château crowning the Duskvine hill, famous for the Harvest Masquerade and the Crimson Vintage.
  • DM: Grand Tasting Hall, Pressing Room, Barrel Labyrinth, Vintage Vault (Morwenna's diary), Lucan's Crypt-Chapel, Sunroof Tower.
  • NPCs: Countess Morwenna Dusk, Lucan Vey, Sir Valentin Dusk, The Donors, Anka
  • Clues: clue-morwenna-witness

Duskvine village (Marta Ilic's inn)

duskvine-village · site · in duskvine-valley · player

  • Public: A sleepy valley village whose people have been disappearing.
  • DM: Unnamed in the guide; Marta Ilic's inn is the PCs' contact point.
  • NPCs: Marta Ilic

The Copper Road

copper-road · route · in emberpeaks · player

  • Public: The courier road from Vesperine to the Emberpeaks, where mailbags are being snatched.

The Vine Road

vine-road · route · in duskvine-valley · player

  • Public: The road from Vesperine to the Duskvine Valley.

The Lair of Steam & Paper

lair-of-steam-and-paper · dungeon · in emberpeaks · player

  • Public: Vexirra's hot-spring lair.
  • DM: Sky-Bridge, Kobold Scriptorium, Hot-Spring Galleries, Echo Hall (riddle), Hoard of Letters (fire hazard; Aurelian's last letter), Vexirra's Bath.
  • NPCs: Vexirra, Scribbletail
  • Clues: clue-aurelian-last-letter

The Bridge of Sighing Lanterns

bridge-of-sighing-lanterns · landmark · in vesperine · player

  • Public: A long, lantern-hung bridge to the Hall of Vows' island. Its lamps sigh when an oath is broken nearby.
  • DM: Night 7, Phase 2: the Procession of Lanterns and Brine's ambush (Encounter 1). Vexirra can light it; a Coral Sentinel can hold one end.
  • NPCs: Old Mother Brine, Ilaria Venn, "the Last Kiss", Pim Gallowglass

The Notary Quarter

notary-quarter · district · in vesperine · player

  • Public: A tangle of archways, stairs and tiny offices around the Hall of Vows' landing, where contracts are witnessed and fine print explained.
  • DM: Includes Notary Amar Thorne's office. The Syndicate wants every Witness Raven here dead before Night 7 (Bestiary hook).
  • NPCs: Amaranth, the Smiling Herald

The Deep Crypt of Château Dusk

dusk-deep-crypt · dungeon · in chateau-dusk · dm_only

  • DM: The Crimson Patriarch sleeps here under Morwenna's kiss-oath of rest. Lucan's true plan is to wake him (Night 5).

dmguide.title: 9. Adventures and 2024 XP checks
dmguide.html:
The Courting Moot of the Honeyhorn Matrons

sa1-courting-moot-of-the-honeyhorn-matrons · side-adventure · levels 3-5 · The Thicketmoor

  • Hook: Men are vanishing on the Bog Causeway, among them Pell Ambrose, the Velvet Opera's stage carpenter, who fled the city the morning after the murder.
  • Situation: The six Honeyhorn Matrons, without their menfolk for forty years since Auntie Sallowmere cursed the ogre husbands into the Sulking Stones, kidnap 'husband-candidates' for courtship trials. Captives are absurdly pampered and want to go home; anyone who fails all five trials goes in the Disappointment Pot. The Moot is in two days. Pell built the mirror-wall door and saw Madame Rook come back through it at 11:47.
  • Scenes: Bramble Gate → The Wallows → The Pampering Pen → Kitchen of the Disappointment Pot → The Moot Ring → Hulga's Bower → The Sulking Stones → Sallowmere's Hut
  • The whole clan (Combat path): 1× Honeyhorn Matron (CR 5), 5× Ogre (CR 2) = 4,050 XP → L5×4: High (L/M/H 2,000/3,000/4,400). Beyond High at levels 3-4; use the level-3/4 variants.
  • Level 3 cap: two Ogres at once: 2× Ogre (CR 2) = 900 XP → L3×4: Moderate (L/M/H 600/900/1,600)
  • Level 4: Hulga alone: 1× Honeyhorn Matron (CR 5) = 1,800 XP → L4×4: High (L/M/H 1,000/1,500/2,000)
  • Level 4: three Ogres: 3× Ogre (CR 2) = 1,350 XP → L4×4: Moderate (L/M/H 1,000/1,500/2,000)
  • Auntie Sallowmere: 1× Green Hag (CR 3) = 700 XP → L3×4: Moderate (L/M/H 600/900/1,600)
  • Honey-wasp hive dropped: 1× Swarm of Insects (CR 1/2) = 100 XP → L3×4: Low (L/M/H 600/900/1,600). Hazard; the guide gives no count.
  • Riddle: The Riddle of the Sulking Stones: "I love you" - spoken sincerely by the matrons themselves (Persuasion/Performance DC 15 each; Gretch first, Hulga DC 20 last).
  • Paths: Combat; Charm: win three of five Moot trials (Hog-Hoist vs Bru +6, Serenade DC 14, Feast DC 15 Con, Love Poem DC 13, Mud Waltz DC 14); Stealth: the Mud-Bath Snore (group Stealth DC 14); Bargain: break the curse (Granny Moss, riddle, confessions, or Sallowmere Persuasion DC 16)
  • Rewards: Pell Ambrose's testimony; 300 gp mixed coins; Potion of Giant Strength (Hill); Honeyhorn mead (Advantage on one Charisma check; you will sing); Honeyhorn ogres defend Vesperine on Night 7 (if curse broken)

The Dreamthieves of the Moth Court

sa2-dreamthieves-of-the-moth-court · side-adventure · levels 4-6 · The Lanternwood

  • Hook: Across Vesperine people fall into enchanted, smiling sleep, dusted with silver moth-powder, among them Teodor Graves, Dame Ottoline's grandson. Save him and the Council buys one extra night.
  • Situation: Queen Ilysse is gorging on dreams as the treaty weakens. She keeps the wedding-day dream the silver-haired woman paid for Widow's Sigh in her Silk Library (Keystone).
  • Scenes: The Avenue of Lights → The Dust Fields → The Hall of Wings → The Mirror Pool → The Silk Library → The Hush Throne

  • Endings: Ending A: The Unmasking; Ending B: The Restored Name; Ending C: The Velvet Throne; Ending D: The Seventh Bell Tolls
  • Rewards:

The Last Oath of Aurel Fenn

seed-last-oath-of-aurel-fenn · seed · levels 8-8 · Cypress Isle

  • Hook: A thief breaks a black-glass jar on Night 6, and something walks out of the Sable Crypt.
  • Situation: If Aurel Fenn's name-jar is shattered, Aurelian rises as an Undying Oathwarden and walks to the Hall of Vows; it can only be answered, not killed.
  • Scenes:
  • The Undying Oathwarden: 1× Undying Oathwarden (CR 16) = 15,000 XP → L8×4: above High (Deadly: flee or bargain) (L/M/H 4,000/6,800/8,400)
  • Rewards:

The Fine Print

seed-the-fine-print · seed · levels 4-8 · The Notary Quarter

  • Hook: Teodor learns his grandmother signed her first name into the Book as surety for his Grace Night.
  • Situation: Steal Ottoline's page back from Notary Thorne's office; Witness Ravens and impeccable manners guard it.
  • Scenes:
  • Witness Ravens: 2× Witness Raven (CR 1/4) = 100 XP → L4×4: Low (L/M/H 1,000/1,500/2,000)
  • Rewards:

Visiting Hours

seed-visiting-hours · seed · levels 6-8 · The Tower of Penitence

  • Hook: Brine needs a prisoner silenced before the Council hears them.
  • Situation: A barge of Syndicate 'visitors' reaches the Tower at the same time as the PCs; Sergeant Bettina Crane is honest but outnumbered.
  • Scenes:
  • Syndicate visitors: 4× Tough (CR 1/2), 2× Bandit Captain (CR 2), 1× Pirate Captain (CR 6) = 3,600 XP → L6×4: Moderate (L/M/H 2,400/4,000/5,600)
  • Rewards:

The Deepest Vintage

seed-the-deepest-vintage · seed · levels 7-8 · Château Dusk

  • Hook: Lucan escaped, and he has gone down to the deepest crypt.
  • Situation: Lucan plans to wake the Crimson Patriarch, Morwenna's maker, and trade her for his heirship.
  • Scenes:
  • Lucan and three Dusk Fledglings on the stair: 1× Lucan Vey (CR 6), 3× Dusk Fledgling (CR 2) = 3,650 XP → L7×4: Moderate (L/M/H 3,000/5,200/6,800)
  • The Crimson Patriarch, awake: 1× Crimson Patriarch (CR 18) = 20,000 XP → L8×4: above High (Deadly: flee or bargain) (L/M/H 4,000/6,800/8,400)
  • Rewards:

The Warden-Song

seed-the-warden-song · seed · levels 5-7 · The Drowned Market (District 4)

  • Hook: Kray's sentinels now guard Brine's Drowned Shard under the Drowned Market.
  • Situation: Learn the warden-song from Quill-Fin and command the sentinels, or outrun them at low tide.
  • Scenes:
  • Two Coral Sentinels: 2× Coral Sentinel (CR 5) = 3,600 XP → L5×4: High (L/M/H 2,000/3,000/4,400); L6×4: Moderate (L/M/H 2,400/4,000/5,600)
  • Rewards:

What Climbs Up the Glass

seed-what-climbs-up-the-glass · seed · levels 8-8 · The Rosewater Gallery

  • Hook: When the Glass opens, every mirror in the gallery speaks with Mirelle's voice: something is climbing.
  • Situation: Mirelle has held the Thousand-Faced Reflection at the bottom of the Glass for five hundred years.
  • Scenes:
  • The Thousand-Faced Reflection: 1× Thousand-Faced Reflection (CR 14) = 11,500 XP → L8×4: above High (Deadly: flee or bargain) (L/M/H 4,000/6,800/8,400)
  • Rewards:

dmguide.title: 12. Known gaps and inconsistencies
dmguide.html:
• [inconsistency, low] The Clue Trail says there are 'ten Keystones' (six city + four side adventures), but eleven clues are marked Keystone: six city ★, Pell (SA1), wedding dream (SA2), Morwenna (SA4), Aurelian's letter (SA5), and Lysander's testimony (Part 2). SA3 offers none; the Lanternwood Clue Trail row is unstarred. (world-guide Part 4 > The Clue Trail; Part 2) Suggestion: Say 'eleven' or demote Lysander's testimony to a supporting clue.
  • [inconsistency, low] The wedding mask is 'made for a bride forty years ago' (Gazetteer) but 'thirty-year-old' (Clue Trail); the wedding was 31 years ago. (Part 3 Gazetteer vs Part 4 Clue Trail) Suggestion: Use thirty-one years.
  • [inconsistency, medium] Mother Brine is 'the Syndicate's fence' in Parts 3-4 but 'the Syndicate's boss' in Side Adventure 3; the Syndicate's leadership is never defined. (Part 3, Part 4, SA3) Suggestion: Decide who runs the Thorn Syndicate.
  • [inconsistency, medium] Pipwhistle is 'she', a pixie with dandelion-fluff hair in the guide, but 'he', a 'mossy, button-eyed sprite' in solo Adventure 3 (and the Bestiary Buttonthief lore follows the solo version). (Part 6 vs solo Adventure 3 / Bestiary c2)
  • [inconsistency, medium] Bestiary 'Herald of the Dusk Court' (CR 16, appears Night 7) vs the guide's Amaranth (CR 6, 'the Fae Duke's Herald'). The Unravelling clock also says 'heralds', plural and antlered, on Night 5. (Bestiary c2 vs Part 6 / Part 4) Suggestion: State whether Amaranth is one of several heralds or the only one.
  • [inconsistency, low] Bestiary Undying Oathwarden lore says an Oathwarden was murdered 'on the eve of Night 7'; the guide's murder is on the Night of Unmasking (before Night 1). (Bestiary c7 vs Part 1)
  • [inconsistency, low] Bestiary collection 7 refers to a 'Notary Quarter' and the Accord's archive/courts, which the guide's six districts don't include. (Bestiary c7)
  • [inconsistency, low] 'Smitten' is both Allure stage 3 and Enthrallment stage 1, and the Allure status 'Charmed' shares a name with the 2024 Charmed condition (the 2024 pass added a clarifying note). (Part 8 vs Part 6) Suggestion: Rename one track's stages.
  • [inconsistency, low] Lucan already has Legendary Resistance (1/Day); the 5-player row now raises it to 2/Day. (SA4 vs Part 9 scaling)
  • [inconsistency, low] Valentin says he hasn't been 'touched without fear in thirty years', but he was Morwenna's consort for a hundred years; the exile date is never given. (solo Adventure 5 vs Part 2)
  • [inconsistency, low] Caelum's Deception is +8 in the guide but +4 (L1) / +6 (L2-3) in solo Adventure 3 (deliberate solo scaling, but unstated). (Part 2 vs solo Adventure 3)
  • [inconsistency, low] Sir Fennic is a Gladiator (CR 5) in SA2 but a Scout (CR 1/2) in solo Adventure 3. (SA2 vs solo Adventure 3)
  • [inconsistency, low] Kray is a Bandit Captain with HP 71 treated as CR 3 in SA3, but a plain Bandit Captain (HP 62 at L3, CR 2) in solo Adventure 4. (SA3 vs solo Adventure 4)
  • [inconsistency, low] The solo book picks a gateway with a d6 (6 = the Glass chooses); the guide uses a d8 with two comic misfires (Gretch, Vexirra) that have no solo entry. (Solo 'How to Use' vs Part 2)
  • [inconsistency, medium] Solo entries are for levels 1-3, but the campaign is for levels 3-8; no rule says how a level-1 solo hero joins. (Solo book vs campaign levels) Suggestion: Add 'advance to level 3 on arrival' or a milestone rule.
  • [dangling-thread, medium] The Syndicate's Oathwarden candidate is 'a minor noble bought by Mother Brine' and is never named or described. (Part 7 > The Seventh Bell)
  • [dangling-thread, low] Aurel Fenn's true name in Nocturne's name-jar has no stated payoff ('changes nothing about who killed him'). (Part 6)
  • [dangling-thread, low] Saving Teodor grants '+1 night', but the clock rules don't say how an eighth night interacts with the Accord's seven-night deadline. (SA2 Rewards)
  • [dangling-thread, low] The Tower of Penitence appears only in Ending A's epilogue. (Part 7)
  • [dangling-thread, medium] 'Everyone wants a seat' (Lysander, Valentin, Sabine, the Syndicate; one passenger per traveler) has no resolution procedure. (Part 2 > The Way Home)
  • [dangling-thread, low] Thessaly's listening masks have no stated consequence beyond eavesdropping (what does she do with what she hears?). (Part 4 Suspect 6)
  • [dangling-thread, low] Count Aurelio (whose murder Lucan pinned on Valentin) appears only in solo Adventure 5. (solo Adventure 5)
  • [dangling-thread, low] The Bestiary's Crimson Patriarch (CR 18, Morwenna's maker) is never mentioned in the guide. (Bestiary c5)
  • [dangling-thread, low] Kray 'has learned to command' two Coral Sentinels, but they appear nowhere in the grotto rooms. (SA3)

  • [no-stats, low] The Lanternside riot names creature types but no counts (build it with the 2024 budget). (Part 7)

  • [no-stats, low] Side Adventure 3 is the only side adventure without a Keystone clue (Varo's report is 'supporting'). (SA3)

(bestiary/, portraits/README.md)

dmguide.title: Seats in the Glass (rules)
dmguide.html:
From the world guide, Part 2 (not in dm.md).

When the Glass opens at midnight, the travelers themselves need no seat: each one who has kept their mirror-promise and cleared their Anchors simply kisses their own reflection and steps through. Everyone else needs a seat. That means Lysander, Sir Valentin, a lover a traveler wants to bring home, a Syndicate agent fleeing the city, or a traveler whose promise is still unkept. Seats are few and tied to the shards, so the players have to choose.

How many seats. At the stroke of midnight the Glass counts:

  1. One seat for every shard of the Glass held by hand in the Rosewater Gallery. The holder decides who sits in that seat (themselves included, if they need one) by pressing the shard into that person's palm. A shard is spent when its seat is used: it melts into the Glass like a coin into wax. A traveler who spends their shard goes home without the keepsake shard described in After going home.
  2. One more seat, the Warden's Seat, in the gift of the new Oathwarden. The Oathwarden grants it with a kiss on the brow, freely given. A PC Oathwarden can grant it to anyone, but they can't use it themselves (the office binds them; see The Oathwarden's chain).

Known shards. There are only a handful in Carnelia, and every one has someone who wants it:

Shard Who holds it at the start Who wants it
The Queen's Shard (Sabine's hand-mirror) Sabine Velour Mother Brine (it was the price of Sabine's debts), Sabine herself (home, after thirty years)
The Sea-Glass Shard (Marisol's shipwreck find) Marisol Tidewhisper Kray (if he survives), Nerissa (as a trophy), Marisol (so she never has to choose between worlds)
The Gilded Shard (set in a mirror frame at Château Dusk) Countess Morwenna Dusk, without knowing it Valentin (sunlight), Lucan (escape)
The Honeyhorn Hand-Mirror (in Little Gretch's beauty kit) Little Gretch Nobody yet. Gretch would give it to a PC who helped her clan, or trade it for a romance novel from another world
The Drowned Shard (bought by Brine for the Syndicate) Old Mother Brine Brine: a back door out of Carnelia for her fortune if Night 7 goes badly

Rules of the seats.

  • No seat can be taken by force. The Accord governs the Glass: a shard pressed into a palm under threat, theft, or enchantment opens nothing. A stolen shard is still a shard, though, and its new holder can give its seat freely.
  • A seat goes to the holder's world. A passenger arrives in the world of the traveler whose hand they hold as they step through. A passenger with no traveler's hand to hold goes nowhere and stays behind (Lysander's terrible problem).
  • Lysander can leave in any seat. Freeing him without a seat requires someone to trade places with him, freely and with full understanding (Part 2).
  • Valentin believes a seat will let him walk in sunlight. The Glass doesn't promise that; the GM decides.
  • The Syndicate wants seats to sell. Every shard the PCs let Brine keep is a Syndicate fortune in another world.

Choices this creates. With two or three shards in play, the table must decide: does Sabine go home, or does Lysander finally leave? Does a PC take their beloved home or spend the shard to free a stranger in a mirror? Is the Warden's Seat a reward, a bribe, or a mercy? And does anyone trust the PC who holds the most shards? Run the decision as a scene, not a roll. Every seat that goes unused at 12:01 is lost until the next Oathwarden dies.

After going home: A traveler who returns keeps a small shard of the Glass. Once a year, at midnight, it shows Vesperine, and anyone who swore them a kiss-oath can wave back.

handbook.title: Vesperine & the Velvet Marches — Player Primer
handbook.lead: A Campaign World Guide of Masks, Murder, and Misbehavior. World: Carnelia . Rules: D&D 2024 (SRD 5.2.1) , levels 3-8. This primer holds only what your characters could know (or what you need at the table). Everything else lives with the DM.

sections.title: Safety and content
sections.html:
Mature fantasy intrigue: flirtation, seduction-as-strategy, scandal, vice, betrayal, and violence. Romance and sexual content are always suggestive, never explicit, and fade to black between consenting adults. Nothing romantic or sexual ever involves captives, coercion, or anyone underage. The ogress den is played as danger plus bawdy comedy, not titillation at a prisoner's expense. Use your table's preferred safety tools (Lines & Veils, an X-card, or a quick 'too far? cut to morning' agreement).

  • Enthrallment is not consent: a character at fey Enthrallment stage 2+ cannot consent to romance, and any kiss-oath sealed under enthrallment is a forgery.
  • Fade to black: when consenting adult characters go somewhere private, cut to 'The next morning…'.
  • In-world law: the Accord of Lips rejects any forced, tricked, or unwilling kiss.

sections.title: Session zero
sections.html:
• [ ] Confirm the content compass: suggestive, never explicit; fade to black; no captives, coercion, or minors in any romantic context.
  • [ ] Agree on Lines (never appears) and Veils (happens off-screen). Typical Veils for this campaign: graphic gore, torture.
  • [ ] Pick a personal tie to one of the people of interest below (an old flame, an old arrest, a signature perfume, a debt, a duel, a favorite 'aunt').
  • [ ] Learn the fey etiquette below and agree that enthralled characters cannot consent to romance.
  • [ ] If you're coming through the Oathless Glass: write down the promise your character once made to their own reflection, and roll (or choose) your gateway character.
  • [ ] Rules baseline: D&D 2024 (SRD 5.2.1) only, including Heroic Inspiration and 2024 Exhaustion.
  • [ ] Decide: group, solo with a GM, or GM-less solo; and whether the Allure track is in use.

sections.title: The world: Carnelia
sections.html:
A sun-drenched, wine-dark land of canals, vineyards and old magic, ruled less by kings than by contracts. Five hundred years ago Vesperine's founders struck the Accord of Lips with the Fae Duke of the Dusk: any promise sealed with a kiss is magically binding and recorded in the Ledger of Vows. A forced or stolen kiss creates no oath.

Every kiss-oath is recorded in shimmering self-writing ink in the Ledger of Vows, kept by a single magically appointed guardian, the Oathwarden. At midnight on the Night of Unmasking, the last night of the city's month-long masquerade, the Oathwarden Lord Aurelian Sable was found dead in the Rosewater Gallery of the Velvet Opera, his lips stained black as ink, moments after kissing the city's most famous diva in front of a hundred masked witnesses. Each night without a new Oathwarden, oaths unravel; on the seventh night the Accord itself fails and the Fae Duke of the Dusk comes to collect.

You carry the Red Ribbon Warrant: the Opera Council's sealed authority to enter any house, question anyone once, and name the murderer before the seventh bell. Reward: 500 ducats each and a favor of the Council (sealed with a kiss, naturally).

Tone. Seductive intrigue; masks and true faces; promises and their price; decadence with teeth. Consent matters in-world too: the Accord cannot bind an unwilling kiss.

sections.title: Vesperine, the City of Masks
sections.html:
Built on a hundred islands knit by bridges, gondola lanes and gossip; colored-glass lanterns over every canal. Masks are legal and fashionable at all hours. ~60,000 people. Ruled in practice by the Opera Council; policed by the Lantern Watch; currency gold ducats and silver kisses. Notable vices: masquerades, card salons, Vinehold wine, dream-moth dust, duelling for love.

District What's there
The Gilded Crescent (District 1) Noble palazzos facing the Grand Canal; balconies built for eavesdropping. Home of House Morrow and the shuttered Sable Palazzo.
The Velvet Quarter (District 2) Theaters, salons, pleasure-gardens and the Velvet Opera, a cathedral of red plush and gold leaf.
Needle Row (District 3) Artisans' lanes: tailors, wigmakers, perfumers, and the Atelier of Madame Rook.
The Drowned Market (District 4) A half-sunken flea market under the old city: ankle-deep water, floating lanterns, stalls on stilts. Reached by the stairs at Gull Steps.
The Hall of Vows (District 5) A white-marble temple-library on its own island: silence and the sound of a pen that writes by itself. The Ledger of Vows rests on a lectern of living rose-thorn, tended by the Veiled Sisters. Since the murder the ink bleeds and pages blank out.
Lanternside (District 6) Docks, taverns, sailors, and the Lantern Watch's leaning headquarters, the Tilted House.
Cypress Isle The cemetery island.
The Notary Quarter A tangle of archways, stairs and tiny offices around the Hall of Vows' landing, where contracts are witnessed and fine print explained.

sections.title: The Velvet Marches
sections.html:
Region What travelers say From Vesperine
The Thicketmoor Brambles the size of houses, golden honey dripping from wasp hives, and warm mud pits ogres consider a spa. Travellers vanish. Mostly men. Mostly loudly. 1 day on foot / ½ day by horse
The Lanternwood A forest where the trees give off soft blue light and moths the size of cats drift between them. Sleepers who wander here wake days later, smiling, with no memory of their dreams. 1½ days on foot / 1 day by horse
The Saltgrave Coast Black cliffs, shipwrecks, and singing at night that every sailor pretends not to hear. Smugglers bring Syndicate cargo through the sea caves. 1 day on foot / ½ day by boat
The Duskvine Valley The most beautiful countryside in Carnelia: golden terraces, poplars, villages where everyone is a little too pale and very well-rested. Château Dusk crowns the hill. 2 days on foot / 1 day by horse
The Emberpeaks Steaming hot springs, copper-veined cliffs and rope sky-bridges. Miners leave love poems at shrine-stones to keep the dragon in a good mood. 3 days on foot / 2 days by horse

sections.title: Places you may hear about
sections.html:
• The Velvet Opera. A gold-and-crimson temple to spectacle: five tiers of private boxes, each with its own little curtain for 'private conversations'. Backstage is a maze of rope, sandbags and costume racks. Feel: perfumed heat, applause, whispers behind fans.
  • The Rosewater Gallery. A long salon above the stage lined with mirrors and rose-trellises around a fountain of scented rosewater. Its tall clock, the city's most famous timepiece, stopped at 11:47 on the night of the murder. The mirror wall's great central pane is very old and very flattering.
  • The Dressing Gallery. Racks of costumes, wig-stands, and Madame Rook's fitting table covered in feathers and gold leaf.
  • The Sable Palazzo. Aurelian's home in the Gilded Crescent: elegant, cold, too big, now shuttered.
  • House Morrow's palazzo. The Gilded Crescent seat of House Morrow, a founding family.
  • The Atelier of Madame Rook. A cozy shop overflowing with masks: feathered, porcelain, lacquered, beaded. Thessaly lives above it with three cats named after her ex-lovers.
  • Vos Perfumery. Glass bottles in every color, a copper still, and a tiefling who can identify anyone by scent.
  • The Vault of Broken Vows. Below the Hall of Vows; stores torn-out, annulled pages.
  • Things That Shouldn't Be Sold (Mother Brine's shop). A stall-shop in the Drowned Market; you are asked a password through a slot in the door.
  • Gull Steps. The stairs down into the Drowned Market.
  • The Tilted House. Lantern Watch headquarters, leaning so badly that pens roll off desks.
  • The Sable Crypt. The Sable family tomb on Cypress Isle: cold marble, wilted lilies, a line of old family sarcophagi.
  • The Blue Hour. Sabine Velour's card salon: blue light, smoke, a grand piano, velvet booths and a gilded mirror in the back room.
  • The Black Fan. The most exclusive masked salon in the Gilded Crescent, hosted by the widow Madame Noor Vesperelle in a candlelit palazzo where every mirror is draped in black crepe.
  • The Lilywater Baths. The city's cheapest and most popular bathhouse; patrons who doze in the warm pools sometimes wake much later than they meant to.
  • The Gilded Thimble. A cozy tavern on Needle Row with pewter mugs and iron tankards on the top shelf.
  • The Hush House. A dream-reader's parlor opened this season, selling little blue bottles of sleep-tonic.
  • Notary Amar Thorne's office. A tiny notary's office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows; ink here dries into tiny roses.
  • The Tower of Penitence. Vesperine's prison: a narrow white tower on a rock in the lagoon, reached only by a Watch barge, where the condemned make lace, masks, and confessions.
  • The Bog Causeway. The causeway road from Vesperine into the Thicketmoor, where men have been vanishing.
  • The Sulking Stones. Six grey standing stones in a circle, each vaguely ogre-shaped and scowling, arms crossed.
  • Duskvine village (Marta Ilic's inn). A sleepy valley village whose people have been disappearing.
  • The Copper Road. The courier road from Vesperine to the Emberpeaks, where mailbags are being snatched.
  • The Vine Road. The road from Vesperine to the Duskvine Valley.

sections.title: Travelers through the Oathless Glass
sections.html:
If your character came from another world through a mirror, these rules apply:

  • Glass-Marked. Your reflection lags half a heartbeat behind you; fey, the Veiled Sisters, and careful observers (DC 15 Wisdom (Perception)) notice. Your reflection always shows your true face, and so does everyone else's in a mirror you watch.
  • Oathless. You are immune to the Unravelling. A kiss-oath you choose to swear is twice as strong (the GM may grant Advantage on a D20 Test to enforce it).
  • Anchors. Every kiss-oath you swear in Carnelia becomes an Anchor that binds you here until kept or freely released. Forced, tricked, or enchanted kisses create no oath.
  • Reflection Drift (optional). At each dawn roll a d6; on a 1 your reflection does something on its own.
  • The way home opens only at midnight, only once a new Oathwarden is sworn and judged by the oathless. To pass you must keep your mirror-promise, clear your Anchors, and kiss your own reflection in the Glass while speaking the kept promise.

Gateway characters

Five figures reach through the Glass. Each is an adult, each flirts with intent, and none can force a kiss-oath.

Lysander of the Silvered Glass

Tall and slender, quicksilver-sheened skin, white-silver hair tied with a black ribbon, polished-steel eyes that reflect you. A five-hundred-year-old silver brocade doublet; he chimes faintly like a wineglass when he moves. Courtly, wistful, playful, very lonely. He speaks from any reflective surface.

[[face:f37b38e84cced]]

Sabine Velour

A glamorous woman in her mid-fifties: warm brown skin, finger-waved black hair streaked with silver, midnight-blue beaded gown, opera gloves, an unlit jeweled cigarette holder and a Queen of Hearts in her clutch. Voice of smoke and honey; calls everyone 'sugar' or 'kid'. Runs The Blue Hour in the Velvet Quarter and cheats beautifully at cards.

[[face:fecb013931ff3]]

Prince Caelum of the Dusk

Unearthly tall, twilight-violet skin, golden eyes, antlers twined with climbing red roses, rose-red velvet coat stitched with thorns, a briar crown, and an air of private amusement.

[[face:f6d92284bc247]]

Marisol Tidewhisper

A merfolk siren who can take a two-legged shape on land: sea-green scales along cheekbones and collarbones, black hair braided with sea-glass and tiny bells, eyes like moonlit surf, a pearl-and-abalone bodice and sea-silk wraps. Always slightly damp and grinning. Wild, reckless, a laugh like a breaking wave; she flirts by daring.

[[face:fb7f328f5ae06]]

Sir Valentin Dusk

Pale as candle wax, tousled raven hair, a beauty mark beneath one heavy-lidded eye, black velvet coat with garnet buttons, ruffled cravat, oxblood gloves. A vampire: in mirrors only his clothes show. Decadent, sardonic, romantic, tired of eternity, and he asks permission for everything.

[[face:fe1c1ea4a5741]]

sections.title: People of interest on the Night of Unmasking
sections.html:
• Seraphine Lark (Suspect: the Diva). Human, early 30s, a cascade of copper hair, emerald silk gown, a voice that could melt candle wax, black-stained lips she refuses to wash ('Let them look'). Dramatic, quick-witted, exhausted by her own legend; funny when she forgets to perform. Alibi: on stage until 11:50, then on the balcony with the crowd until the midnight kiss.
  • Lady Celestine Morrow (Suspect: the Fiancée; heir of House Morrow). Half-elf, 28, platinum hair in a severe crown braid, ice-blue high-collared gown, a single sapphire at her throat; moves like a duelist. Cold, cutting, brilliant; treats conversation as fencing. Claims she was 'alone on the balcony, enjoying the view.'
  • Captain Dorian Hale (Suspect: the Watchman; captain of the Lantern Watch). Human, mid-40s, broad shoulders, a scar along his jaw, Lantern Watch coat with the top buttons undone; smells of pipe smoke and rain. Tired, gruff, decent at heart, dry humor. Claims he was 'walking the perimeter.'
  • Ezren Vos (Suspect: the Perfumer; owner of Vos Perfumery). Tiefling, 30s, lavender skin, gold rings on curling horns, a loose silk robe over an embroidered vest; speaks softly and leans in to smell you. Sensual, curious, theatrical, a little amoral, genuinely brilliant. Made the bloodrose perfume Seraphine wears. Alibi: running the perfume fountain on the ground floor all night.
  • Varo Kestrel (Suspect: the Fixer; Thorn Syndicate rogue). Half-elf, late 20s, dark curls, crooked grin, rose-thorn earring, thorn-green domino mask; dresses better than he can afford. Shameless, charming, cheerful even when caught; loyal to friends only. Alibi: 'Dancing.' With whom? 'Everyone.'
  • Madame Thessaly Rook (Beloved maskmaker of Needle Row). Human, about 60, a long silver braid pinned with gold, laugh lines, magnificent dark eyes, fingertips flecked with gold leaf, always a lavender shawl; never wears a mask herself. Warm, wicked, hilarious: everybody's favorite aunt. Lives above her Atelier on Needle Row with three cats named after her ex-lovers. Gives each PC a free, beautiful mask 'for the investigation'. Alibi: in the Dressing Gallery all evening, fitting masks.
  • Dame Ottoline Graves (Opera Council spokesperson; the PCs' employer). A tiny, elderly, terrifyingly polite patron in an enormous crimson gown with a jeweled lorgnette. She hands the oathless PCs the Red Ribbon Warrant: entry to any house and the right to question anyone once. Reward: 500 ducats each and a Council favor sealed with a kiss.

sections.title: Rumors in the salons
sections.html:
1. "Aurelian was never really a Sable. I heard his grandmother sold eels."
  2. "The diva poisoned him on the Syndicate's orders."
  3. "The Countess of the Duskvine drinks the blood of virgins."
  4. "Men are vanishing in the Thicketmoor and coming back fat and happy."
  5. "Madame Rook has made Aurelian's mask every year for thirty years, and never charged him a coin."
  6. "The Ledger is bleeding."
  7. "A dragon is reading our mail."
  8. "Captain Hale lost his own house in a card game."

Rumors are rumors. Some are true.

sections.title: Charm, flirtation and fey etiquette
sections.html:
• Influence (2024). Persuading a hesitant NPC is the Influence action. NPCs start Indifferent; each person of interest has their own flirt angle and DC.
  • The Allure track (if used): 0 Guarded, 1 Intrigued, 2 Charmed (a mood, not the Charmed condition), 3 Smitten, 4 Devoted. Fill boxes with successful Influence, fitting gifts, bravery, winning a game or duel, or a great line at the table.
  • Fey etiquette. Never say "thank you" (say "you honor me" or "I'll remember this"). Never give your full name. Refuse gifts graciously, three times if you must. Pay fairly for what you take. Don't eat the honey.
  • Counter-charms people swear by: cold iron, cold water to the face, a true name spoken thrice, clothes worn inside out, bread and salt under a mortal roof, and laughter.
  • Heroic Inspiration (2024): expend it to reroll any one die immediately after rolling it. You can't hold more than one. Fading to black after a consensual romance scene often earns it.
  • Exhaustion (2024): each level is -2 to every D20 Test and -5 ft. Speed; level 6 is death; a Long Rest removes one level.

Nursery rhyme, recited in salons as a drinking game: "Never thank them. Never give your name. Never eat the honey. And if one of them kisses you, darling, check your pockets, your purse, and your soul, in that order."

solo.title: Through the Oathless Glass
solo.subtitle: Five Solo Entry Adventures for Vesperine & the Velvet Marches (D&D 2024 (5.5e), SRD 5.2.1 compatible, levels 1–3)

intro.html: Everyone has kissed a mirror once. Tonight, one of them kisses back.

intro.title: How to Use This Book
intro.html:
These are five solo gamebook adventures, one for each gateway character of the Oathless Glass (world guide, Part 2). Each pulls a single adventurer out of their own world, through a mirror, and into Carnelia on the Night of Unmasking, the night Lord Aurelian Sable dies. Each one ends by handing your character into the main murder mystery (The Black Kiss) or into that gateway character's side adventure, carrying a clue, an ally, or a complication.

Pick your door. Choose the gateway character who intrigues you most, or roll a d6: 1 Lysander, 2 Sabine, 3 Caelum, 4 Marisol, 5 Valentin, 6 you pick (choose the one who intrigues you most). (The world guide's d8 gateway table is for groups; solo play always uses this d6.)

Content compass. These adventures are flirtatious and full of intrigue: suggestive, never explicit. Romance between consenting adults fades to black. A character under enthrallment (stage 2+) can't consent, and the Accord itself voids any vow sealed that way. Anything that crosses your personal lines can simply be skipped.

intro.title: What You Need
intro.html:
• A 1st- to 3rd-level character (any class), dice, and a notebook.
  • The world guide's Allure track (Part 8) and Enthrallment track (Part 6). A quick reference is below.
  • A Glass Sheet: write down your Mirror-Promise, Allure (0–4) with your gateway character, Enthrallment (0–5, per fey), Anchors (kiss-bound promises you've made), Clues, and Favors.

intro.title: Reading the Gamebook
intro.html: Each mission is a set of numbered scenes. Read a scene, make your choice, and follow the link, for example → go to 4. Ability checks list DCs as L1 / L2–3 where they scale. Combat stat blocks are SRD 5.2.1 (2024) creatures, named in italics with their 2024 names, or monsters from The Carnelia Bestiary marked (Bestiary), scaled for one hero (see below). This book uses the 2024 rules only: the 2024 conditions and Exhaustion, Heroic Inspiration, and the 2024 XP Budget per Character.

intro.title: Quick Reference: Allure & Enthrallment
intro.html:
Track 1 2 3 4
Allure (their feelings for you) Intrigued: one honest answer Charmed: reveals a secret if asked Smitten: volunteers help Devoted: an ally who takes risks for you; romance possible (fade to black)
Enthrallment (their hold on you) Smitten: you daydream of them Beguiled: can't consent; Disadvantage on Insight vs. them Enthralled: the Charmed condition; follow one suggestion a day Bound: forged vows (stage 5, Nameless, can't happen in these entry adventures)

Resist-or-yield scenes are marked 🌹. Each offers a temptation. Yield and you usually gain something (Allure, a gift, a boon) at the price of Enthrallment or an Anchor. Resist and you keep your head, but the moment may pass. Neither choice is wrong. Counter-charms from Part 6 work here: cold iron, refusing gifts graciously three times, never saying "thank you," and cold water.

intro.title: Solo Rules for the Entry Adventures
intro.html:
The Oracle (d20). When you're unsure what happens, ask a yes/no question and roll: 1–3 No, and… · 4–8 No · 9–11 No, but… · 12–14 Yes, but… · 15–18 Yes · 19–20 Yes, and… Shift the result by ±3 for likely or unlikely questions. Each adventure adds its own d6 oracle prompts for colour.

Gateway Aid. Your gateway character can help you three times per adventure (each adventure says how they help). Mark a box each time. Some aid costs Allure or adds an Anchor, as noted.

Scaling for one hero.

Your level Enemy hit points Enemy numbers Extras
1 Halve non-boss HP 1 enemy per listed "slot" Gateway Aid can also heal 1d8 + 2 once
2 ¾ HP As listed —
3 Full HP Add 1 minion to the largest fight Hero's Surge: once per combat, take an extra action

Encounter budgets (2024). A lone hero's budget is one character's XP Budget per Character: L1 50 / 75 / 100, L2 100 / 150 / 200, L3 150 / 225 / 400 (Low / Moderate / High). Each fight below lists an XP check, and every fight you're expected to win is tuned to High or below. The few that are beyond High are labeled Deadly: flee or bargain. They are chases or set pieces with their escape options written in. Gateway Aid, Hero's Surge, Death's Door, and the chase rules are how a lone hero survives them, and running is always an option.

Death's Door. When you drop to 0 HP, you may instead stay at 1 HP and take a Scar (a lasting complication noted in each adventure's consequence table). Once per adventure.

Arrival ties. Whichever door you choose, you arrive on Night 1. Your entry adventure takes most of that night, and the Unravelling clock (world guide, Part 4) starts at dawn.

intro.title: Mirror-Promise Prompts (d12)
intro.html:
Before you begin, decide (or roll) what your character once promised their reflection. The Glass heard it.

d12 "I promised my reflection…"
1 "…that I'd stop being afraid of being seen."
2 "…that I'd find someone who'd choose me first."
3 "…that I would never go back to them."
4 "…that I'd finally do something brave."
5 "…that I'd find out the truth about what happened."
6 "…that I'd stop pretending to be someone I'm not."
7 "…that I'd make them pay."
8 "…that I'd go somewhere nobody knows my name."
9 "…that I'd forgive myself."
10 "…that I'd fall in love properly, just once."
11 "…that I'd protect someone who couldn't protect themselves."
12 "…that I'd stop wasting my life."

Your promise matters at the end of every adventure. Keeping it is part of the way home (world guide, Part 2).

intro.title: After the Entry Adventure: Level 1 → 3 Bridge
intro.html:
The solo entry adventures are for levels 1–3; The Black Kiss starts at level 3. This bridge joins them.

Finishing a solo entry. When a hero finishes any ending of a solo entry adventure, they advance to level 3 at the first dawn of Night 1, whatever level they played it at. In the fiction, the Glass catches them up: every reflection they've passed tonight has been living a little ahead of them, and at dawn the reflections step back in. The hero keeps everything their ending grants (clues, allies, Anchors, Scars), and also gains one Glass Boon and one Contact from their gateway character's row below. A hero who already played the solo at level 3 gains the boon and contact, plus Heroic Inspiration.

Entry adventure Glass Boon (once per Long Rest unless noted) Contact
1. The Glass Remembers (Lysander) Silvered Sight. As a Magic action, look out of any mirror or still, reflective surface you have touched in the last day, as if you were standing there, for up to 1 minute. Lysander, who can whisper from any mirror in Vesperine
2. The Blue Hour (Sabine) Card Up the Sleeve. After you fail a Charisma (Deception) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, you can reroll it and use the new roll. Sabine Velour, and through her an introduction to Varo Kestrel
3. A Rose Before Midnight (Caelum) Rose of Twilight. You have Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed condition from Moth Court fey. Once per campaign, ask Caelum one question that he must answer truthfully. Pipwhistle Dewlace, who will scout for you for sweets
4. Hold Your Breath (Marisol) Siren's Breath. You can hold your breath for 1 hour and gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed (always on). Quill-Fin, who knows every underwater way under Vesperine
5. May I Come In? (Valentin) Invited. You have Advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks against any creature whose skin you've touched in the past minute (Valentin taught you to read a pulse). Marta Ilic, the Duskvine innkeeper, whose inn is a safe house

Joining a group. A solo hero who joins a group at level 3 counts as a full member of the party. Their entry clue counts toward the group's Keystones (Lysander's testimony and the wedding dream from A Rose Before Midnight are Keystones; the others are supporting clues or leads). Their Anchors are theirs alone. If several players each ran a solo entry, reunite the party at the Velvet Opera at first dawn, as in the world guide's Part 2.

Running straight on solo. A hero who continues alone into The Black Kiss uses the world guide's Part 9 solo rules, starts at level 3, and gains the gateway character as a companion (use the stat block in the world guide's Appendix D, scaled per Companion NPCs) if their Allure with that character is 2 or more.

adventures.title: The Glass Remembers

sections.title: Your Side of the Glass
sections.html:
You live an ordinary life somewhere that is not Carnelia. Roll or choose:

d6 Your life tonight
1 Closing up an antique shop alone. The oldest mirror in the back has been fogging from the inside.
2 Getting ready for a party you don't want to go to, staring at yourself in the hallway mirror.
3 Home late after a breakup, brushing your teeth, refusing to cry at your own face.
4 Working a night shift; the restroom mirror flickers under the bad lighting.
5 Packing to leave a life you've outgrown, with one last look in the dressing-table glass.
6 Sleepless at 3 a.m., talking to your reflection the way you did as a teenager.

The call. You whisper your Mirror-Promise to the glass again, maybe without meaning to. This time your reflection smiles before you do.

sections.title: The Pull-Through
sections.html: Your reflection smiles, slowly and fondly, the way someone smiles at an old friend. Then it steps aside, and someone else is standing behind you in the glass: a tall man with skin like moonlight on water, white-silver hair tied with a black ribbon, a doublet of silver brocade five hundred years out of fashion. His eyes are polished steel, and in them you see yourself, very small. "Forgive the intrusion," he says, and his voice echoes as if from the end of a long hall. "A man is about to die, and I need someone who can't be accused of loving or hating him. You'll do beautifully." He holds out his hand. When you touch the glass, it is warm. Then cold. Then gone. You fall upward through a thousand candlelit reflections, and land on your hands and knees on marble that smells of roses, just as a hundred masked strangers begin to scream.

sections.title: Meeting Lysander
sections.html:
• His approach: He mirrors you, copying your posture, your accent, the way you push your hair back, and tells you exactly what you need to hear: "You've always been braver than you let yourself be." He speaks from any reflective surface nearby: mirrors, windows, a polished goblet, a pool of spilled wine.
  • What he offers: Guidance out of a very dangerous room, his eyewitness memory of the murder, and five hundred years of knowledge about Vesperine.
  • What he hides: He was trapped in the Glass by a kiss-sealed promise to his lover, Lady Oriane Sable. He can only leave if someone honestly agrees to trade places with him, and he's been rehearsing ways to ask. He also knows the killer is of Oriane's blood, and he's not sure he wants her caught.

Gateway Aid (3):

  • Reflected Warning: reroll one failed Perception or Insight check.
  • Mirror Step: in a room with mirrors, teleport 30 feet between two reflective surfaces.
  • Glass Shield: impose Disadvantage on one attack roll against you.

The third use costs 1 Allure, because he finds it frightening to care.

Oracle prompts (d6), to ask whenever you're stuck:

  1. Is a guard looking your way?
  2. Did Lysander see this happen, too?
  3. Is there a mirror within reach?
  4. Does someone recognize you as "the stranger from the mirror"?
  5. Is Madame Rook nearby?
  6. Has the Watch noticed the body's been moved?

sections.title: The Entry Mission: Out of the Gallery, Into the Truth
Endings
sections.html:
Ending A: The Witness. You walk into The Black Kiss already holding a Keystone clue and Lysander's trust (Allure 2+). He can speak to you through any mirror in the city, once per night, for the rest of the campaign. Complication: Thessaly knows the mirror-stranger was in the Gallery. If you wore her mask, she knows everything you've said.
