npcs.text: Well-dressed adults who attend the masquerade willingly and boast about it like a spa visit.

npcs.name: Vexirra
npcs.text: A young copper dragon with scales like a new penny, a talent for impressions and terrible taste in jokes; insists she is an 'adult'. Desperately romantic. Sometimes visits the city disguised as a shy red-haired woman with freckles and copper-rimmed spectacles.
npcs.allure: Write her a letter that makes her cry (Performance DC 17)
aliases: the red-haired woman in copper spectacles

npcs.name: Scribbletail
npcs.role: Kobold chief poet of the Inkscale Troupe
npcs.text: Writes appalling sonnets; jealous of anyone the dragon likes.

npcs.name: Forewoman Brannagh Copperhand
npcs.text: Grizzled, practical dwarven guild boss who posted the bounty on Vexirra.

npcs.name: Pip Dewley
npcs.text: As players first meet her: Pip Dewley, the bubbly, curly-haired, full-size barmaid at The Gilded Thimble on Needle Row, quick with gossip and always asking for 'a little something for luck.' Buttons go missing whenever she's near.
npcs.allure: Persuasion DC 11, or automatic with sweets/buttons/a lullaby

ra.title: The Barmaid Goes Pop
ra.html: Read-aloud: The Barmaid Goes Pop. Pip leans across the bar, beaming, a tray of steaming teacups balanced on one hand. "Now, sweet thing, a little kiss on the nose for luck, and you'll owe me just one teensy song—" Someone drops a pouch of shiny brass buttons on the counter. Pip's eyes go enormous. There is a sound like a cork leaving a bottle, a puff of pink glitter, and the teacups crash down onto an empty floor. Something the size of your hand zips up out of the wreckage on dragonfly wings, clutching a button like a shield, glowing bright, delighted pink. "Ohhh, those are lovely," squeaks Pipwhistle Dewlace. "Oops. Um. Surprise?"

npcs.name: Dina Mire
npcs.text: As players first meet her: Dina Mire, the giggling, sun-freckled bath-attendant at the Lilywater Baths in Lanternside who scrubs backs, braids hair and gossips about everyone.
npcs.allure: Persuasion DC 13 (out-tease her or bring Sallowmere gossip)

ra.title: The Bath-Girl in the Bubbles
ra.html: Read-aloud: The Bath-Girl in the Bubbles. Dina is mid-giggle, a braid of somebody's hair half-finished in her fingers, when the bucket of cold water hits her. She shrieks, and the shriek turns into a laugh like a brook in spring. The freckles slide off her like wet paint. Her skin is green-gold now, her hair a cascade of willow leaves threaded with water-lilies, her eyes dark and rippling. Every frog in the drains begins to sing. "Well, that was rude," says Ondine Mirewillow, wringing out a lily. "And I was being so good. Mostly. Does anyone want their shoes back?"

npcs.name: Master Orrin Mintleaf
npcs.role: Dance master and fiddler of the Opera's after-parties
npcs.text: As players first meet him: Master Orrin Mintleaf, the beloved bearded dance master and fiddler who leads the revel-band at every Velvet Opera after-party, always in a wide-brimmed hat and tall, oddly heavy boots.
npcs.allure: Performance DC 14 (dance with abandon or win a music duel)

ra.title: The Dance Master Kicks Off His Boots
ra.html: Read-aloud: The Dance Master Kicks Off His Boots. The music is too good to stop. Master Mintleaf whoops, kicks one boot clean across the ballroom, then the other, and his hat goes sailing after them. Where his feet should be, polished hooves strike sparks from the marble. Gilded ram's horns curl from his chestnut hair; his trousers are suddenly fur from the hips down. The dancers scream, then laugh, then don't stop dancing. "No point hiding it now!" bellows Rillo Fennamint, pipes at his lips. "Who's coming to the after-party? The forest's only a short walk, and the moon's out!"

npcs.name: Madame Noor Vesperelle
npcs.role: Wealthy widow and hostess of the Black Fan salon
npcs.text: As players first meet her: Madame Noor Vesperelle, a rich, mysterious widow 'from across the sea' who hosts the Black Fan, the most exclusive masked salon in the Gilded Crescent, in a palazzo where every mirror is draped in black crepe. Invitations are black envelopes sealed with a lip-print.

ra.title: The Black Fan Falls
ra.html: Read-aloud: The Black Fan Falls. Madame Vesperelle laughs, that low, warm laugh that has made half of Vesperine fall in love with her, and snaps her black lace fan shut. "Darling," she says, "you've been looking at the wrong face all evening." Behind her, the crepe slithers from the great mirror like a shed skin. In the glass stands someone else: skin white as a bone in moonlight, lips black as Ledger ink, eyes with no stars in them at all. The candles gutter. When you turn back from the mirror, the widow is gone and only the other one remains, smiling exactly the same smile. "There," says Lady Nocturne Vesh. "Isn't that better? Now we can stop pretending you weren't already mine."

npcs.name: Brother Ash
npcs.role: Mourning friar who sits with the grieving
npcs.text: As players first meet him: Brother Ash, a tall, grey-robed mourning friar of no order anyone can name, who sits with the grieving at Lanternside wakes and Cypress Isle funerals.

ra.title: The Friar's Armor
ra.html: Read-aloud: The Friar's Armor. Brother Ash bows his head over the mourner's hands. "Let me take it away," he murmurs, "just for tonight." Then he looks up at you, and his face is full of an old and terrible tenderness. "No. You won't let me, will you?" The grey robe darkens and hardens; it is armor now, black plate grown over with thorns and inlaid with silver moths, and the petals of his cloak rise around him like ash in the wind. His lips glitter silver. "I am Sir Merrow Ashgrave," says the Sorrowkiss, setting down his helm. "And I am so very sorry for what I am about to do."

npcs.name: Notary Amar Thorne
npcs.role: Contract notary on the bridge to the Hall of Vows
npcs.text: As players first meet them: Notary Amar Thorne, a meticulous, soft-spoken contract notary with a tiny office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows, who never lies, not even politely.

ra.title: The Notary Closes the Ledger
ra.html: Read-aloud: The Notary Closes the Ledger. Notary Thorne blots the last signature, examines it, and smiles that small, apologetic smile. "Thank you. That's everything in order." The lamps dim. The little office seems to grow taller, and so does the notary: antlers unfurl from their temples, threaded with roses; the drab clerk's coat flows into dusk-colored velvet embroidered with thorns. On the desk, the ledger swells into an enormous book bound in red leather, its pages whispering names. "I am Amaranth, Herald of the Dusk," they say gently. "Please don't be alarmed, darling. Everything you signed was perfectly legal. I made sure of it."

npcs.name: Gristle Pike
npcs.text: A huge man with a hook for a hand and a voice like gravel.

npcs.name: Anka
npcs.text: A twenty-three-year-old maid at Château Dusk with puncture marks on her wrist and a glassy look: a thrall of Lucan's.

npcs.name: Lord Silvano Quell
npcs.role: Poet-heir of House Quell; candidate for Oathwarden
npcs.text: The beautiful, languid last scion of House Quell, a founding house gone to seed. Writes poetry, faints elegantly, and owes everyone money.

npcs.name: Lord Orsino Varga
npcs.text: A broad, grey-bearded shipping magnate whose ships carry half of Lanternside's trade.

npcs.name: Madame Liliane Corvaux
npcs.role: Opera Council: impresaria of the Velvet Opera
npcs.text: The Opera's glamorous impresaria; a sleek black bob with a white streak and a jeweled cane.

npcs.name: Archivist-Mother Severine
npcs.role: Opera Council: abbess of the Veiled Sisters
npcs.text: The serene abbess of the Veiled Sisters, keeper of the Ledger's rites.

npcs.name: Lord Tancredi Morrow
npcs.text: A silver-haired half-elf lord with a duelist's bearing and a black rose on his lapel.

npcs.name: Dowager Ysolde Vane
npcs.text: A sharp-eyed, powdered dowager who never leaves a card table and cheats with style.

npcs.name: Nell Daisy
npcs.text: A sunny flower-seller with a basket of bloodroses who sells boutonnieres at the Opera doors.

npcs.name: Sergeant Bettina Crane
npcs.role: Warden of the Tower of Penitence
npcs.text: The honest, outnumbered sergeant who keeps the city's prison tower.

locations.name: Carnelia
locations.text: A sun-drenched, wine-dark land of canals, vineyards and old magic, ruled less by kings than by contracts. Five hundred years ago Vesperine's founders struck the Accord of Lips with the Fae Duke of the Dusk: any promise sealed with a kiss is magically binding and recorded in the Ledger of Vows. A forced or stolen kiss creates no oath.

locations.name: Vesperine, the City of Masks
locations.text: Built on a hundred islands knit by bridges, gondola lanes and gossip; colored-glass lanterns over every canal. Masks are legal and fashionable at all hours. ~60,000 people. Ruled in practice by the Opera Council; policed by the Lantern Watch; currency gold ducats and silver kisses. Notable vices: masquerades, card salons, Vinehold wine, dream-moth dust, duelling for love.

locations.name: The Velvet Marches
locations.text: The countryside Vesperine depends on and pretends not to need: Thicketmoor, Lanternwood, Saltgrave Coast, Duskvine Valley, Emberpeaks.

locations.name: The Thicketmoor
locations.text: Brambles the size of houses, golden honey dripping from wasp hives, and warm mud pits ogres consider a spa. Travellers vanish. Mostly men. Mostly loudly.
locations.travel: 1 day on foot / ½ day by horse

locations.name: The Lanternwood
locations.text: A forest where the trees give off soft blue light and moths the size of cats drift between them. Sleepers who wander here wake days later, smiling, with no memory of their dreams.
locations.travel: 1½ days on foot / 1 day by horse

locations.name: The Saltgrave Coast
locations.text: Black cliffs, shipwrecks, and singing at night that every sailor pretends not to hear. Smugglers bring Syndicate cargo through the sea caves.
locations.travel: 1 day on foot / ½ day by boat

locations.name: The Duskvine Valley
locations.text: The most beautiful countryside in Carnelia: golden terraces, poplars, villages where everyone is a little too pale and very well-rested. Château Dusk crowns the hill.
locations.travel: 2 days on foot / 1 day by horse

locations.name: The Emberpeaks
locations.text: Steaming hot springs, copper-veined cliffs and rope sky-bridges. Miners leave love poems at shrine-stones to keep the dragon in a good mood.
locations.travel: 3 days on foot / 2 days by horse

locations.name: The Gilded Crescent (District 1)
locations.text: Noble palazzos facing the Grand Canal; balconies built for eavesdropping. Home of House Morrow and the shuttered Sable Palazzo.

locations.name: The Velvet Quarter (District 2)
locations.text: Theaters, salons, pleasure-gardens and the Velvet Opera, a cathedral of red plush and gold leaf.

locations.name: Needle Row (District 3)
locations.text: Artisans' lanes: tailors, wigmakers, perfumers, and the Atelier of Madame Rook.

locations.name: The Drowned Market (District 4)
locations.text: A half-sunken flea market under the old city: ankle-deep water, floating lanterns, stalls on stilts. Reached by the stairs at Gull Steps.

locations.name: The Hall of Vows (District 5)
locations.text: A white-marble temple-library on its own island: silence and the sound of a pen that writes by itself. The Ledger of Vows rests on a lectern of living rose-thorn, tended by the Veiled Sisters. Since the murder the ink bleeds and pages blank out.

locations.name: Lanternside (District 6)
locations.text: Docks, taverns, sailors, and the Lantern Watch's leaning headquarters, the Tilted House.

locations.name: Cypress Isle
locations.text: The cemetery island.

locations.name: The Velvet Opera
locations.text: A gold-and-crimson temple to spectacle: five tiers of private boxes, each with its own little curtain for 'private conversations'. Backstage is a maze of rope, sandbags and costume racks. Feel: perfumed heat, applause, whispers behind fans.

locations.name: The Rosewater Gallery
locations.text: A long salon above the stage lined with mirrors and rose-trellises around a fountain of scented rosewater. Its tall clock, the city's most famous timepiece, stopped at 11:47 on the night of the murder. The mirror wall's great central pane is very old and very flattering.

locations.name: The Dressing Gallery
locations.text: Racks of costumes, wig-stands, and Madame Rook's fitting table covered in feathers and gold leaf.

locations.name: The Sable Palazzo
locations.text: Aurelian's home in the Gilded Crescent: elegant, cold, too big, now shuttered.

locations.name: House Morrow's palazzo
locations.text: The Gilded Crescent seat of House Morrow, a founding family.

locations.name: The Atelier of Madame Rook
locations.text: A cozy shop overflowing with masks: feathered, porcelain, lacquered, beaded. Thessaly lives above it with three cats named after her ex-lovers.

locations.name: Vos Perfumery
locations.text: Glass bottles in every color, a copper still, and a tiefling who can identify anyone by scent.

locations.name: The Vault of Broken Vows
locations.text: Below the Hall of Vows; stores torn-out, annulled pages.

locations.name: Things That Shouldn't Be Sold (Mother Brine's shop)
locations.text: A stall-shop in the Drowned Market; you are asked a password through a slot in the door.

locations.name: Gull Steps
locations.text: The stairs down into the Drowned Market.

locations.name: The Tilted House
locations.text: Lantern Watch headquarters, leaning so badly that pens roll off desks.

locations.name: The Sable Crypt
locations.text: The Sable family tomb on Cypress Isle: cold marble, wilted lilies, a line of old family sarcophagi.

locations.name: The Blue Hour
locations.text: Sabine Velour's card salon: blue light, smoke, a grand piano, velvet booths and a gilded mirror in the back room.

locations.name: The Black Fan
locations.text: The most exclusive masked salon in the Gilded Crescent, hosted by the widow Madame Noor Vesperelle in a candlelit palazzo where every mirror is draped in black crepe.

locations.name: The Lilywater Baths
locations.text: The city's cheapest and most popular bathhouse; patrons who doze in the warm pools sometimes wake much later than they meant to.

locations.name: The Gilded Thimble
locations.text: A cozy tavern on Needle Row with pewter mugs and iron tankards on the top shelf.

locations.name: The Hush House
locations.text: A dream-reader's parlor opened this season, selling little blue bottles of sleep-tonic.

locations.name: Notary Amar Thorne's office
locations.text: A tiny notary's office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows; ink here dries into tiny roses.

locations.name: The Tower of Penitence
locations.text: Vesperine's prison: a narrow white tower on a rock in the lagoon, reached only by a Watch barge, where the condemned make lace, masks, and confessions.

locations.name: The Bog Causeway
locations.text: The causeway road from Vesperine into the Thicketmoor, where men have been vanishing.

locations.name: The Hive-Hall of Honeyhorn
locations.text: The Honeyhorn den, with famous mud wallows.

locations.name: The Sulking Stones
locations.text: Six grey standing stones in a circle, each vaguely ogre-shaped and scowling, arms crossed.

locations.name: The Cocoon Palace
locations.text: A towering tree of pale silk glowing like a paper lantern; court of the Moth Queen.

locations.name: The Smugglers' Grotto
locations.text: Sea caves on the Saltgrave cliffs where smugglers land Syndicate cargo.

locations.name: Château Dusk
locations.text: The château crowning the Duskvine hill, famous for the Harvest Masquerade and the Crimson Vintage.

locations.name: Duskvine village (Marta Ilic's inn)
locations.text: A sleepy valley village whose people have been disappearing.

locations.name: The Copper Road
locations.text: The courier road from Vesperine to the Emberpeaks, where mailbags are being snatched.

locations.name: The Vine Road
locations.text: The road from Vesperine to the Duskvine Valley.

locations.name: The Lair of Steam & Paper
locations.text: Vexirra's hot-spring lair.

locations.name: The Bridge of Sighing Lanterns
locations.text: A long, lantern-hung bridge to the Hall of Vows' island. Its lamps sigh when an oath is broken nearby.

locations.name: The Notary Quarter
locations.text: A tangle of archways, stairs and tiny offices around the Hall of Vows' landing, where contracts are witnessed and fine print explained.

factions.name: The Opera Council
factions.summary: Seven patrons of the Velvet Opera who own most of the city's debt: Ottoline (chair), Morwenna, Orsino Varga, Liliane Corvaux, Archivist-Mother Severine, Tancredi Morrow, Ysolde Vane. Four votes name an Oathwarden.

factions.name: The Lantern Watch
factions.summary: Vesperine's underpaid, overdressed city watch; HQ the Tilted House.

factions.name: The Thorn Syndicate
factions.summary: The underworld that sells anything in the Drowned Market, including secrets and debts. Run, though few know it, by Old Mother Brine.

factions.name: The Veiled Sisters
factions.summary: Keepers of the Ledger of Vows in the Hall of Vows.

factions.name: House Sable
factions.summary: Founding house; seat of the late Oathwarden.

factions.name: House Morrow
factions.summary: Founding house of the Gilded Crescent.

factions.name: House Dusk
factions.summary: Vampire nobility of the Duskvine Valley.

factions.name: The Velvet Opera company
factions.summary: Singers, stagehands, and carpenters of the Opera.

factions.name: The Honeyhorn Clan
factions.summary: Ogresses of the Thicketmoor.

factions.name: The Moth Court
factions.summary: Dream-eating fey of the Lanternwood; vassal of the Dusk Court.

factions.name: The Drowned Choir
factions.summary: Merfolk sirens of the Saltgrave sea caves.

factions.name: The Copperhand Miners' Guild
factions.summary: Dwarf and gnome miners of the Emberpeaks.

factions.name: The Inkscale Troupe
factions.summary: Vexirra's kobold poet-servants.

factions.name: The Dusk Court
factions.summary: The Fae Duke's court 'just behind the sunset'; creditor of the Accord.

factions.name: The Oathless Glass (gateway characters)
factions.summary: Those who reach through the Glass for the PCs.

factions.name: Independent
factions.summary: No faction.

timeline.event: During the Duke's first collection the Glass cracks; shards scatter across many worlds.
Seraphine leaves the stage and goes to the balcony.
The unmasking kiss; Aurelian dies. Varo lifts the vault key from his coat in the cloakroom. The Oathless Clause wakes the Glass and pulls the PCs through.

readAloud.html: "In Vesperine, every promise is sealed with a kiss. Last night, one of those kisses killed a man."
"Everyone has kissed a mirror once. A wish, a dare, a promise whispered to your own face at three in the morning. You thought no one was listening. Something was."

It's late. The room is quiet except for the hum of the ordinary world. You catch your reflection, in a mirror, a darkened window, a glass of something amber, and for a moment you don't recognize the face looking back. It looks like someone who never kept a promise. Then the reflection smiles, and you are not smiling.

[Gateway character's arrival — see "How they appear."]

The glass goes soft as warm wax. Cold silver closes over your fingers, your wrist, your heart. Every promise you ever whispered to a mirror plays back at once, in your own voice, a hundred times over. You fall upward through a forest of reflections: ballrooms, canals, candlelit faces in masks, a woman with a silver braid weeping over a hatbox, a man in midnight-blue falling and falling. Then rose-scented air, the roar of a crowd, and a floor of cool marble under your palms. Somewhere very close, a clock has stopped ticking. A voice in the dark says, almost fondly: "Ah. The oathless have arrived."
Carved to smile, I cannot laugh; I wear no face, yet I am half of every lie the dancers tell. Lift me, love, and break the spell.
Given freely, I weigh nothing; broken, I'm as heavy as stone. Lips make me, lies unmake me, and I am never wholly your own.
I arrive before the lover and linger when she's gone. You cannot see or hold me, yet I swear where she has been.
What can be stolen, yet never be touched, lost while you hold it, and taken with a kiss — and returned to its owner only by being spoken?
I have leaves but no branches, a spine but no bones; I hold a thousand kisses and I've never been kissed.
I have a face but cannot see, two hands but cannot hold. I strike, but I wound no one; stop my heart and I grow cold — yet the moment of my dying is the truth I've always told.
We stood too proud to say it, so we stand here proud and still. Three words will set us walking — if one of you has the will. Not ours to speak; we're only stone. Let her who loves us speak alone.
I am the feast you never eat, the kiss you never feel, the road you walk on sleeping feet, and lose when you grow real.
First the gull, who cries for none; then the bell that tolls the drowned; then the wave that breaks, the wind that lies, and last, the heart that makes no sound.
I'm born of crushing, laid to sleep in the dark; the longer I'm buried, the brighter my spark. I loosen your tongue and I loosen your laces — I'm blood in the chalice of holy places.
I grow bigger the more that I'm shared, I burn without any fire; I'm lighter when carried by two who have dared, and heaviest kept by a liar.

"Never thank them. Never give your name. Never eat the honey. And if one of them kisses you — darling, check your pockets, your purse, and your soul, in that order." — Vesperine nursery rhyme, recited in salons as a drinking game

readAloud.title: The Black Fan Falls
readAloud.html: Read-aloud: The Black Fan Falls. Madame Vesperelle laughs, that low, warm laugh that has made half of Vesperine fall in love with her, and snaps her black lace fan shut. "Darling," she says, "you've been looking at the wrong face all evening." Behind her, the crepe slithers from the great mirror like a shed skin. In the glass stands someone else: skin white as a bone in moonlight, lips black as Ledger ink, eyes with no stars in them at all. The candles gutter. When you turn back from the mirror, the widow is gone and only the other one remains, smiling exactly the same smile. "There," says Lady Nocturne Vesh. "Isn't that better? Now we can stop pretending you weren't already mine."

readAloud.title: The Rose Merchant's True Face
readAloud.html: Read-aloud: The Rose Merchant's True Face. Cael sighs, the way a man sighs when a card game has gone on too long, and sets down his glass. "I did so enjoy being ordinary," he says. Every rose in the room opens at once. The red coat lengthens into rose-petal velvet stitched with thorns; his skin deepens to the violet of the last minute before night; and from his dark curls rise antlers twined with climbing roses, brushing the chandelier, which chimes. His eyes are molten gold. "Prince Caelum of the Dusk," he says, bowing, "and still, I promise, your friend. I simply wasn't allowed to say so until now."

readAloud.title: The Bath-Girl in the Bubbles
readAloud.html: Read-aloud: The Bath-Girl in the Bubbles. Dina is mid-giggle, a braid of somebody's hair half-finished in her fingers, when the bucket of cold water hits her. She shrieks, and the shriek turns into a laugh like a brook in spring. The freckles slide off her like wet paint. Her skin is green-gold now, her hair a cascade of willow leaves threaded with water-lilies, her eyes dark and rippling. Every frog in the drains begins to sing. "Well, that was rude," says Ondine Mirewillow, wringing out a lily. "And I was being so good. Mostly. Does anyone want their shoes back?"

readAloud.title: The Dance Master Kicks Off His Boots
readAloud.html: Read-aloud: The Dance Master Kicks Off His Boots. The music is too good to stop. Master Mintleaf whoops, kicks one boot clean across the ballroom, then the other, and his hat goes sailing after them. Where his feet should be, polished hooves strike sparks from the marble. Gilded ram's horns curl from his chestnut hair; his trousers are suddenly fur from the hips down. The dancers scream, then laugh, then don't stop dancing. "No point hiding it now!" bellows Rillo Fennamint, pipes at his lips. "Who's coming to the after-party? The forest's only a short walk, and the moon's out!"

readAloud.title: The Barmaid Goes Pop
readAloud.html: Read-aloud: The Barmaid Goes Pop. Pip leans across the bar, beaming, a tray of steaming teacups balanced on one hand. "Now, sweet thing, a little kiss on the nose for luck, and you'll owe me just one teensy song—" Someone drops a pouch of shiny brass buttons on the counter. Pip's eyes go enormous. There is a sound like a cork leaving a bottle, a puff of pink glitter, and the teacups crash down onto an empty floor. Something the size of your hand zips up out of the wreckage on dragonfly wings, clutching a button like a shield, glowing bright, delighted pink. "Ohhh, those are lovely," squeaks Pipwhistle Dewlace. "Oops. Um. Surprise?"

readAloud.title: The Friar's Armor
readAloud.html: Read-aloud: The Friar's Armor. Brother Ash bows his head over the mourner's hands. "Let me take it away," he murmurs, "just for tonight." Then he looks up at you, and his face is full of an old and terrible tenderness. "No. You won't let me, will you?" The grey robe darkens and hardens; it is armor now, black plate grown over with thorns and inlaid with silver moths, and the petals of his cloak rise around him like ash in the wind. His lips glitter silver. "I am Sir Merrow Ashgrave," says the Sorrowkiss, setting down his helm. "And I am so very sorry for what I am about to do."

readAloud.title: The Notary Closes the Ledger
readAloud.html: Read-aloud: The Notary Closes the Ledger. Notary Thorne blots the last signature, examines it, and smiles that small, apologetic smile. "Thank you. That's everything in order." The lamps dim. The little office seems to grow taller, and so does the notary: antlers unfurl from their temples, threaded with roses; the drab clerk's coat flows into dusk-colored velvet embroidered with thorns. On the desk, the ledger swells into an enormous book bound in red leather, its pages whispering names. "I am Amaranth, Herald of the Dusk," they say gently. "Please don't be alarmed, darling. Everything you signed was perfectly legal. I made sure of it."

readAloud.title: The Dream-Reader's Wings
readAloud.html: Read-aloud: The Dream-Reader's Wings. Madame Hush leans across the little table, her veil stirring with each whispered word. "Tell me," she breathes, "what did you dream of last night?" Behind you, someone in the waiting room has nodded off, and the dream-reader's head turns toward them like a flower toward the sun. Her veil falls away. Behind her, two great shapes unfold and fill the room, wings of dusky violet and gold, each patterned with a staring eye. Every candle bends toward her. Silver dust drifts down like snow. "Forgive me," whispers Queen Ilysse of the Hush, and her eyes are pools of ink. "It has been such a long time since I had something sweet."
I'm given to you, yet others use me more; I'm carved on your grave and called at your door. Lose me and live, but you'll answer to none — what can be stolen by kissing someone?

The Velvet Opera is a furnace of candlelight and perfume. A thousand masks turn toward the Rosewater balcony as the great clock above it — oddly silent tonight — is ignored in favor of the hand-bells. Midnight. The Oathwarden, Lord Aurelian Sable, sweeps the diva Seraphine Lark into his arms, and the whole house roars as their lips meet.

Then he staggers. His fingers claw at his golden mask. Black — black as spilled ink — spreads from beneath its edges, down his cheeks, across his lips. He falls. Someone screams "Poison!" and a hundred masked faces scatter like startled birds.

In the chaos, a tiny woman in crimson with a jeweled lorgnette taps your shoulder. "You," says Dame Ottoline Graves, "have no oaths in this city. How wonderfully useful. Come with me."
Everyone has kissed a mirror once. Tonight, one of them kisses back.

Pitch: You tumble out of a mirror into a murder scene ten seconds after the victim drops. A silver man who lives in the glass is the only witness, and he'll only tell what he saw if you promise to set him free.

Your reflection smiles, slowly and fondly, the way someone smiles at an old friend. Then it steps aside, and someone else is standing behind you in the glass: a tall man with skin like moonlight on water, white-silver hair tied with a black ribbon, a doublet of silver brocade five hundred years out of fashion. His eyes are polished steel, and in them you see yourself, very small. "Forgive the intrusion," he says, and his voice echoes as if from the end of a long hall. "A man is about to die, and I need someone who can't be accused of loving or hating him. You'll do beautifully." He holds out his hand. When you touch the glass, it is warm. Then cold. Then gone. You fall upward through a thousand candlelit reflections, and land on your hands and knees on marble that smells of roses, just as a hundred masked strangers begin to scream.
I show you the world, but I keep none of it; I give you your face, but I've never worn it. Look into me and I look back true — I am you, and I am not you.
Pitch: A torch singer from another world deals you into a high-stakes card game in a smoky salon. Tonight she has promised to hand you over to the Syndicate, and she would very much rather not.

The song gets louder until it fills your head: a smoky, honeyed voice wrapping itself around a melody from your own world, a song nobody in this room should know. In the glass, the room behind you has changed. Blue light. Cigarette smoke curling through it. A woman in midnight sequins leans on a grand piano, silver streaks in her finger-waved hair, opera gloves to the elbow. She looks straight at you and lifts one gloved hand out of the mirror, holding a playing card between two fingers: the Queen of Hearts. "Pick a card, sugar," she says. "Any card. They all go to the same place." You take it. The glass ripples like a curtain, and you step through into blue smoke, piano music, and the clink of chips, while somewhere far away a hundred people begin to scream.
I've a face but no head, a crown but no throne; I've lovers and fools and a king of my own. Shuffle my fortunes, I'll never complain — and fifty-one sisters will share in my reign.

Pitch: A rose-crowned fey prince offers you anything that fits in your two hands for a single dance. His first gift is a burglary: steal back his love-token from the Moth Queen who still hates him, before sunset strips his glamour bare.

The glass fogs over as though someone on the other side has breathed on it. A finger draws a heart in the fog, then crosses it out and draws a rose instead, with a flourish. Then a long violet hand slides through the surface with no ripple at all, a thorned ring on every finger, holding a single red rose out to you, stem first, thorns carefully removed. "Come and see something beautiful," says a voice like warm honey poured over gravel, "before it ends." You take the rose. The world folds like a love letter. You are standing in tall, cool grass under trees that glow soft blue from within, and moths the size of cats drift overhead like slow lanterns. The sky is the violet of the last minute before night, and it stays that way.
I wear a hundred eyes and never once have seen; I dance with my own shadow, in gowns of dust and sheen. I fly to the one thing that will burn me clean — Say my name, and enter, guest of the Queen.

Pitch: A grinning siren drags you through your bathwater into a sea cave as the tide comes in. She dares you to kiss her for luck, rob a smugglers' warehouse, and outrun the wreckers, then hopes you never learn she's the one who sold her sisters out.

The water goes still as glass, and beneath it a face looks up at you, laughing, upside down: sea-green scales along her cheekbones, black hair drifting with sea-glass and tiny bells, eyes the color of moonlit surf. A cool, wet, webbed hand closes around your wrist. "Hold your breath, darling," she says, and her voice comes up through the water in bubbles. She pulls. You go down and down through warm water that turns cold, through dark that turns blue, through a rush of salt and bells, and you surface gasping in a moonlit sea cave with the roar of surf all around you. The water is at your waist. It's rising. She surfaces beside you, shakes out her hair, and grins. "Welcome to Saltgrave. Can you swim? Say yes."

I'm caught in nets but never fished, I'm owed by all at sea; I steal the sand and give it back, and twice a day I'm free. I keep no clock but keep the time, the moon's my only master — wait on me, and I'll come home; fight me, I come faster.

Pitch: An exiled vampire gentleman has to ask your permission to enter your mirror, and everything after that. Tonight he needs you to walk into his ex-lover's masquerade and find proof that her steward framed him, before dawn and before the steward finds the cages you just opened.

The room in the mirror is your room, perfectly ordinary. Except: in the reflection, a black velvet coat with garnet buttons sits in your armchair with no one inside it. A ruffled cravat. Oxblood gloves, one resting on the arm of the chair. A wineglass lifts itself in a toast. "Please don't scream," says a voice, warm and dry and amused at itself. "I've had a very long century. I'm going to ask you something, and you're allowed to say no. That's rather the point." The glove turns, palm up. "May I come in? You do have to say yes." If you say yes, the coat stands, bows, and offers you its arm, and as you take it the mirror's surface gives like velvet. You step through into candlelight and the scent of crushed grapes, and a masked orchestra in the next room strikes up a waltz.

I was poured to seal a lie, red as blood and twice as dry; I keep a secret, keep a name, I bear a crest but feel no shame. I'm warm when I'm made and cold when I'm kept — break me, and the truth runs free.

teasers.title: The Courting Moot of the Honeyhorn Matrons
teasers.hook: Men are vanishing on the Bog Causeway, among them Pell Ambrose, the Velvet Opera's stage carpenter, who fled the city the morning after the murder.

teasers.title: The Dreamthieves of the Moth Court
teasers.hook: Across Vesperine people fall into enchanted, smiling sleep, dusted with silver moth-powder, among them Teodor Graves, Dame Ottoline's grandson. Save him and the Council buys one extra night.

teasers.title: The Song Beneath Saltgrave
teasers.hook: Ships wreck on the Saltgrave cliffs every night, lured by song. The Lantern Watch blames the Drowned Choir.
teasers.tone: Salt, storms, piracy, and voices that pull you overboard.

teasers.title: The Crimson Vintage
teasers.hook: Villagers of the Duskvine have been disappearing for weeks, and everyone blames Countess Morwenna Dusk, the valley's reclusive vintner and a member of the Opera Council.

teasers.title: A Hoard of Love Letters
teasers.hook: Every love letter in Vesperine has stopped arriving; couriers on the Copper Road lose their mailbags, not their gold.

teasers.title: The Glass Remembers
teasers.hook: You tumble out of a mirror into a murder scene ten seconds after the victim drops. A silver man who lives in the glass is the only witness, and he'll only tell what he saw if you promise to set him free.
teasers.tone: Solo gamebook; flirtation and intrigue; fade to black.

teasers.title: The Blue Hour
teasers.hook: A torch singer from another world deals you into a high-stakes card game in a smoky salon. Tonight she has promised to hand you over to the Syndicate, and she would very much rather not.
teasers.tone: Solo gamebook; flirtation and intrigue; fade to black.

teasers.hook: A rose-crowned fey prince offers you anything that fits in your two hands for a single dance. His first gift is a burglary: steal back his love-token from the Moth Queen who still hates him, before sunset strips his glamour bare.
teasers.tone: Solo gamebook; flirtation and intrigue; fade to black.

teasers.title: Hold Your Breath
teasers.hook: A grinning siren drags you through your bathwater into a sea cave as the tide comes in. She dares you to kiss her for luck, rob a smugglers' warehouse, and outrun the wreckers.
teasers.tone: Solo gamebook; flirtation and intrigue; fade to black.

teasers.title: Night 7: The Seventh Bell (Climax Set Piece)
teasers.hook: The Opera Council must name a new Oathwarden before midnight, or the Accord fails.

teasers.title: The Fine Print
teasers.hook: Teodor learns his grandmother signed her first name into the Book as surety for his Grace Night.

teasers.title: Visiting Hours
teasers.hook: Brine needs a prisoner silenced before the Council hears them.

teasers.title: The Deepest Vintage
teasers.hook: Lucan escaped, and he has gone down to the deepest crypt.

teasers.title: The Warden-Song
teasers.hook: Kray's sentinels now guard Brine's Drowned Shard under the Drowned Market.

teasers.title: What Climbs Up the Glass
teasers.hook: When the Glass opens, every mirror in the gallery speaks with Mirelle's voice: something is climbing.

partyHint: Solo or 3–5 players, levels 3–8 (solo entry adventures: levels 1–3)
